paras: Therefore, my friend, go beyond this discussion (of scientific events), as the happy occasion of the festival has arrived, and people have been provided with good and beneficial manners. There acts are not to be tested on rational basis but upon the trial of love. Our streams are now full of the water of life of love. Our king has come down to our streets once again. The lovers of prosperity walk in appealing styles and protect their lapels from unclean things. Time has come to commit breach of repentance. The repentance upon the taking of God’s name (Ahad, Ahad) has been swept away by the deluge of love. Time has arrived for it and there is none to watch upon this. The watchman of your wisdom has gone into sleep as love has dominated upon you. every drinker of love has drunk the wine of love and fully intoxicated with it. We have to pledge for the time being all our possessions of wisdom and care. The red coloured wine has become like the life pleasing red lips of the beloved and all our possessions are overlapped with rubies from all sides. Our gathering has also become entertaining and pleasing to heart. Therefore, get up and put the black gram on fire to protect yourself from the evil eyes of others behind its smoke. [Explanation of burning of the black gram has been given earlier — Translator]. Now I am fully pleased with the cries, blabberings and madness of the intoxicated fellows. My dear! I feel that this should be situation for ever.

Now Hilal has become a friend of Bilal and the wounds of the thorns have become beautiful flowers and gardens. My body has become a sieve with the sharp pricks of the thorns making my body and soul as a garden of good fortune. I desire that my body should remain before the thorns of that Jew as my soul is intoxicated and deprived of all senses because of my love for my beloved. The fragrance of one soul is reaching my soul and I hear the good news of the arrival of my beloved.
Muhammad has returned from his ascent of the heavens to congratulate and bless and offer prosperity to Bilal who has devoted himself entirely to him. Mall all prosperity be upon Bilal.

chapters.title: High State of Bilal
chapters.subtitle: H. Abu Bakr Siddiq’s return to the affair of H. Bilal, his torture by the Jews for his saying: ‘Ahad, Ahad’, and their increase of their hate and enmity; and narration of the affair before H. Mustafa Muhammad and his suggestion for the purchase H. Bilal from the Jews

paras: When Abu Bakr heard this inspiring truth from H. Bilal, he decided not to tell anymore to him to stop saying ‘Ahad’, and then went before the noble Prophet and spoke to him about H. Bilal’s commitment adding that makers of heaven’s measurements, well settled in mind, marching on the path of spiritual progress, is now caught in the net of your love. The royal falcon is under pains at the hands of the owls. His great treasure is buried under garbage and filth. The owls are causing troubles to the falcon and plucking its hairs and feathers for no wrong on its part. Its only wrong is that, it is a falcon just as there was no wrong on the part of Yusuf other than his beauty. The place of birth and residence of the owl is nothing but ruin and that is the reason for its anger for the falcon saying: why do you think of that green and colourful garden and the streams. Why do you remember your residence which is a palace of the king and your sitting place being the wrist of the king? You consider the residence of the owls as worthless and create mischief and turmoil there.

Our place is so grand that the sky feels jealous of it, and you call it as worthless and ruin! You play tricks with us so that the owls may take you as their leader and king. You create suspicious and madness in their minds and call our paradise as ruin. O ill-natured fellow, we shall thrash so much on your head that you will stop your tricks and nonsense.

sections.heading: Torture of H. Bilal
paras: They turn his charmaikh, (the wooden board with four nails to tie one’s hand and feet with ropes) facing towards the east, tying his hands and feet on it without clothes and beat him with thorny sticks. Blood starts oozing from hundreds of places of his body, but he raises his head, and says ‘Ahad’, and drops it down. I advised him to keep secret his faith and hide it from the accursed infidels. But he does not heed like the fellow whose doomsday has arrived, closing once and for all, the door of repentance. He does not heed to it as he is one caught in love.

Love, repentance and possibility of patience are thing’s which are impossible to go together. Repentance is so small like a worm before love which is so large as a python. Repentance is the conduct and quality of the creatures and love is the quality and conduct of God. Love being a quality of God, who has no concern for anything, cannot go towards anybody except God. Love is entirely meant for God. Love for anything other than God is like copper plated with gold. Its appearance is bright, but its content is nothing but smoke. When brightness vanishes, smoke makes its appearance making the love of other things go cold. When the grief-increasing smoke appears, it becomes so frigid that neither love remains nor tis impacts. Its beauty returns to the place of its origin leaving the body go filthy, ugly and distorted. The light of the moon and its reflection go back to the moon leaving the black wall black. The body ceases to possess light and life remains without any beauty and worth. As against its beautiful water what remains is only mud and that wall-like-body appears like a ghost without light. The counterfeit loses its little golden polish, which goes back to the gold mine. The disgraced copper becomes black like smoke and its lover becomes more black faced and disgraced.

Love of the wise originates from the gold mine which is the base of gold, and it goes on increasing day by day, as, the real beloved (God) is real, possessing its great qualities. O gold mine of love! All greetings and praises are for You! there is no doubts at all in Your greatness, as there is none to participate in its goldenness in the mine. When one brings together the counterfeit in the mine, its gold runs away into mine of the world of non-worldliness (Laa makaan) or hidden, unseen, unseeable world. It is like both the lover and the beloved, (counterfeit Gold and its lover) dying within each other out of fear of each other, like the dead fish, when water of whirlpool dries up and does not remain anymore. As against, Love of God is like the bright sun of perfectness: the world, the light of which is the world of non-material, abstract commands and laws and the entire material is like its shadow and result.

The Propeht upon hearing all this was immensely pleased and bloomed like a flower and he became more anxious to hear more. When the hearer was such as the great Prophet, the tip of every hair of the body of the speaker becomes a regular tongue. Then the Prophet asked as to what should be done. H. Abu Bakr said: ‘I shall purchase him from his master at whatever price he may say. I shall not care for apparent loss and bear with injustice, because Bilal is like a prisoner of God upon His land, which is caught in the wrath of the enemy of God.

chapters.title: Purchase of Bilal from the Master
chapters.subtitle: The Prophet’s suggestion to H. Abu Bakr to take him as a partner in the purchase of H. Bilal as those people would inevitably fix heavy price for him out of their dislike for him. He advised Abu Bakr to become his agent in this behalf and take half the price value from him and share with him in this act of excellence

paras: The Prophet told Abu Bakr: “O searcher of great prosperity! I shall become a partner in this purchase. You may become my agent for half of the deal of purchase and take that much price from me.” H Abu Bakr said: “I shall serve you a hundred times”. So saying he left toward the house of that infidel (Umaiah bin khalaf) of unlimited infidelity. He said to himself: “a pearl from the hand of a child can be purchased at a low price with ease. Satan purchases the wisdom and faith of these foolish people on the price of lowly worldly gains. He presents this dead and deadly world with such a beauty and decoration before them that He purchases pay two hundred gardens its worth for it. He presents the moon with his magic power in such a way that he takes away hundred purses from them. Prophets taught them the trade and presented before them the bright lamp of faith, but ghosts and devils through magic powers opposed them and presented the prophet as of no worth before them. An enemy with his magic powers makes the people enemies of each other: so much so, that many at times the married life of a coupe ends in divorce. They stitch their eyes with magic.

In similar manner, the devils stitched the eyes of the Bilal’s master, so that he sold Bilal to H. Abu Bakr as though he was a scrap. This pearl (Bilal) was costlier than both the worlds. H. Abu Bakr decided to buy this precious pearl from a donkish child. Before the donkey, pearls and oysters are the same and his fellow was so donkish that he did not see the difference even between the pearl and the ocean. He was a denier of the worth of ocean and pearls just as an animal, which has no taste of decoration to value pearls. God has not provided that discrimination in the head of animals to enable them to think of rubies and go in love for pearls. Have you ever seen any earrings in the ears of a donkey. The entire inclination and taste of the donkey is toward grass fields. Read in the Surat ‘Tin’ the verse: we have indeed created man in the best of the moulds: Laqad khalqnal insaana fii ahsani taqwiim (Tin: 95: 4) to know that soul is a great gem. ‘Best of the mould’s is higher in status than the throne of God. Best of the moulds is beyond the reach of your thought and imaging capacity. It is impossible to explain about its worth and grade. If I attempt to do that, not only I but also the hearer will burn out. Therefore, it is wise to keep the mouth shut in this matter and not to take the donkish wisdom towards this understanding.

sections.heading: Words Coming from God
paras: H. Abu Bakr went toward that donkey. We sounded his door chain, and the door was opened. He entered into the Jew’s house with blank mind. He sat down with blank and unconscious mind with a fire of anger around him. Very bitter and harsh words came out of his mouth, and he said: “why do you beat that friend of God. What kind of meanness is this that you one inimical to light? If you find your own religion to be true, how does your heart bear with harm upon another truthful to his religion. You should consider him to be as much attached to his religion as you are to yours. Your behaviour shows that you are not true to your religion itself as otherwise you would not have doubted the truth of the prince of another religion. You consider yourself to be true to your faith. So also, is Bilal to his. You look at all others in your distorted mirror. Do not do so, o eternally rejected and accursed fellow!”

Whatever was coming through the lips of Abu Bakr was full of great wisdom. If I try to say the same thing, I may be disabled. These words of wisdom were gushing forth as though from the source of river Euphrates. They were gushing forth from the non-material, spiritual, dimensionless world of ‘Laamakaan’ but coming through his mouth. That is to say they were coming from God Himself. This is similar to water gushing froth form the rock which did not contain any water within or around. God had made the rock as his shield and curtain through which he flowed water just as wine is poured from out of the flask.

sections.heading: Eyes and Ears: Tools of God
paras: You may consider the flow of light from the spring of your eyes, without any deficiency and obstruction. It does not get this wealth of light either from your flesh or from your fat. God as a Friend and Grantor has used your eye as a means to exhibit the light. In the hollow of your ear there is an absorbing air which absorbs the sound, which recognises the truth and falsity of statements. What kind of tiny bones is the ear made of that they accept and decipher the sounds and words coming towards them. These tiny bones and air are just curtains. It is God only who is there in both the worlds of matter and spirit to grant these capacities. Without any doubt, He alone is the hearer and talker. As otherwise, you may see that both of your ears are just parts of your head. All these are created things and they do not possess these qualities, of their own.

sections.heading: Deal Struck
paras: Umaiah bin Khalaf, upon hearing Abu Bakr said: “If you have so much sympathy for Bilal, O the one habituated to grace, pay me the money and take him with you. if your heart burns so much for him, you may buy hi for me, without spending money for this purpose, you cannot meet your object”.

H. Abu Bakr said: “I shall perform a hundred acts of worship and five hundred prostrations if we strike a deal. I have a slave, but he is a Jew. He has a fair colour and beautiful face, but a heart blackened with the colour of infidelity. You may take him in exchange for your black skinned but bright hearted slave”. Then that master sent a man to call the fair slave, who was really very fair and beautiful. So beautiful that the infidel, Umaiah, was wonderstruck and his stone-like heart instantly went out of control.

This is the case of the seers of external qualities that their hard, stone-like hearts become soft like wax. That fellow, however, did not agree and started bargaining for something more upon this exchange. Then H. Abu Bakr added some quantity of silver, upon which that infidel’s greed came to terms. He sold out H. Bilal and there was a settlement without any hitch. He offered the pearl and in exchange took a piece of stone. He was very satisfied that he has made a very profitable deal. He has given black in exchange for white. The deal was completed as both agreed upon the offer and acceptance.

chapters.title: Pleased with What One Has
chapters.subtitle: The infidels’ laughter with a feeling that Abu Bakr has met with a loss in the deal

paras: The hard-hearted Jew gave a loud hilarious laugh full of sarcasm and treacherous victory. H. Abu Bakr asked him for the reason and in reply to it, he laughed all the more and said: “if you had not been so insisting and determined in the purchase of that slave, I would not have sold him at this high price, but sold at one-tenth of it, as in my opinion he is not worth half-a-penny. But by showing your anxiety, you increased his value.”

sections.heading: Inner and Outer Worth
paras: H. Abu Bakr said: ‘you are a fool. You have sold a pearl at the price of an apricot like a child. In my view, he is of the worth of both the worlds. I look at his soul and you look at his colour. He is pure gold which has become black so that he may be an object of contempt in this world of fools. Eyes that can see only the seven colours are covered up with the curtains of body, because of which they cannot see the soul hidden behind this curtain. Were you to bargain still more in this deal, I would have given a price worth all my wealth and property. Were you to go still beyond what you offered, I would have borrowed a lapelful of gold from others and given to you out of my concern. You have given me at a cheap rate as you had purchased at a cheap rate. You did not open the jewel box and see the pearl in it. Your foolishness has given me a closed jewel box. You will soon see how much of loss you have incurred. You have lost an unopened box full of rubies. Like a negro you are pleased with black colour. In the end you will regret very much. None ever sells his own fortune and good luck as you have done. A great fortune had come to you in a slave’s apparel, but your unfortunate eyes did not see anything other than the apparent. He presented before you his slavery and your ill-nature showed tricks as cleverness.

sections.heading: Decorated Falsehood
paras: As against him, you took a black-hearted with a white body as a senseless idol worshipper. This white is yours and that black is mine, and both of us have been profited. This is what is meant by: “O infidel, your religion for you and my religion for me”: lakum diinukum walia diini: (kaafiruun: 109: 6).”

This itself is the punishment for the rejectors of true faith. A wooden horse covered wit ha silken overall on its back. Similarly, the graves of the rejectors are full of fire and smoke but on their outside full of hundreds of decorations. So also, the wealth of the oppressors which are good to look at but contain within them the blood and miseries of the oppressed. So also, the hypocrite is externally engaged in fasting and prayer, but within himself has worthless black ash. And like the sterile cloud, that is only full of thunder, which is of no use either to the soil or to the fruits. Its beginning is pleasing like treacheries and false promises, and the end full of disgrace”.

sections.heading: Untold Impacts of Touch and Movements
paras: Thereafter, H. Abu Bakr held H. Bilal’s hand in his hand, who was thin like a toothpick due to hard overworking and extreme hunger. He became a real toothpick and found the way into a mouth with a sweet tongue. He was brought before the Prophet, as he had accepted his religion through his heart. With his broken condition, when he looked at the face of the Prophet, he fell down unconscious upon his back. For some time, he was senseless and unconscious, and upon regaining consciousness, started shedding tears of joy. The Prophet pulled him toward himself and took him in his arms. None can know of the grants and graces that he got from the Prophet’s closeness. This can be explained by a few examples.

What happens to copper that comes in contact with alchemy. Or a poor fellow who abruptly came in contact with a hidden treasure. Or a half dead fish due to deprivation of water suddenly falls into a river. Or a caravan lost from its way once again comes on tis path. Were the words with which the Prophet spoke to him at that moment to fall upon the night, it would have gone out of the darkness; and become a bright day. I cannot explain in any jargons of what all that happens in such situations. the jargons of the Prophets and saints that cast their impressions and impacts upon the hearts without spoken words are matters of tasting, are impossible to be explained in words. Only men of tastes understand them. You know very well what the sun tells to the plants and date palm when it enters into the constellations of Taurus. When the spring season starts. This day is called as ‘nauroz’ in Persia and differently called in different countries. The sun does not speak but causes such impacts which give new life to the plants, and freshness is caused everywhere. You also know as to what clean water in the plants tells to the plants, twigs, flowers and fruits. It refreshes them and becomes sweet in fruits.

sections.heading: Unspoken Commands and Their Offshoots
paras: Similar are the impacts of God’s artisanship on all thing’s of the world without any ostensible means and instruments just as the magic spells of the magicians. The means and impacts arising from God say many thing’s and true commands to all thing’s without words and moving of lips. This is not in respect of only that which instantly comes into existence but also in respect of the impacts by these existences upon existences which are of routine nature. [Philosophers say that routine acts and impacts of major acts resulting from creations are not new acts of God, because if God’s will is eternal and prior to creation, then the impacts and routine acts will also have to be taken as eternal; and on the contrary, if they are taken as results or impacts of creations, the same question arises in respect the earlier creation and the chain goes on. Therefore, both are wrong conclusion. Therefore, these cannot be a willing on the part of the eternal and all creations are products of the earlier creations. Dialecticians disagree and say that willing by God itself is creation and further creations of results are also part of the will. There is no need for further creation by the earlier creation. Thus, all are combined together and occur appropriately at appointed time and in appointed way — Qazi Sajjad Hussain]

Rumi however continues to say: that God’s authority and impacts of His authority are beyond the understanding of the common people. As in the matter of the fundamentals. Common sense is only a blind follower, it is better to be a blind follower in respect of the branches that arise from the fundamental premises. [ this is just as accepting branches of the tree as the products of the stem and connected with it, when the wisdom of the common people accepts whatever is said by the Prophets about God, it naturally follows that they should believe in them in respect of collateral aspects also — Translator]. If wisdom questions as to how one can surrender wisdom to total submission, you may tell it that it should be on the basis of a thought that you cannot understand everything. There are many things beyond the reach of wisdom. May peace and prosperity be upon you!

chapters.title: Why Not Partnership for the Prophet
chapters.subtitle: The Prophet’s disapproval with H. Abu Bakr Siddiq of his purchasing of H. Bilal totally out of his own cost, when he was told to take the Prophet also as a partner in the deal and H. Abu Bakr’s seeking pardon

paras: After some time, leader of the two worlds and the emperor of this world, Muhammad got angry with Abu Bakr and said: “O truthful, I had told you to take me as a partner in the honourable purchase of Bilal! But why did you purchase him for you only? Tell me, O clean natured, why did you purchase him for your own self. Tell me clearly the reasons!”

sections.heading: Total Submissions to the Prophet
paras: H. Abu Bakr said: “we both are the slaves of your street. I purchased him in my own name to free him, and I have freed him from slavery well in front of you. you may take me alone as your slave now. I shall never seek any freedom from your slavery, as my freedom lies in your slavery, and without you, everything is harsh and hard for me. You are the one to give life to the entire world and make ordinary people special and in particular, me. My soul used to see in the dreams in my youthful days that the tablet of the sun was offering salutations to me. It had pulled me up from the earth toward the sky, and consequently and had evolved high and became its companion. I had thought that all that was impossible, and it was nothing but madness, as at no time an impossibility be possible. When I looked at you, I found that I was looking at myself. How great is the quality of this mirror! Impossibility became possible when I looked at you, and my soul sank deep into grandeur and brightness. I realised, in fact, you are the real sun and the sun in the heaven is worthless before you. you are the soul of all cities. When I looked at you, the worth and value of the life-giving-worth of the heavenly sun fell down in my view. Because of you, my viewing of the world became highly elevated, and I found no worth at all in anything of the world.

sections.heading: Praise of the Praiseworthy
paras: I sought for light and found myself to be light, all in all. I tried to search for beauty and found myself to be so beautiful so as to be of envy for the hoors. I searched for Yusuf with fine and clean silvery body, but I found you as the land of all beauties as though in a land of Yusufs. I was in search of paradise, and I found it in every part of your body. from my angle what all I say is praises and appreciation, but from your angle, it is nothing but depreciation and deficient assessment. My praise for you is like the praise of God before H. Musa by a simple-minded shepherd. He was telling to God: “I shall pick lice from your hair and feed you with milk. I shall stitch sandals for you and place before you to wear”. This praise of God was totally unsuitable for God, but He took this depreciation and degradation as high praise. In similar manner, it will be a great favour to me if you take my deficient and unworthy statement about you as worthy, and I am sure, you will do that. There is no wonder in it!

sections.heading: The Prophet’s Praise of the Humble
paras: “Please have mercy upon the deficiencies of wisdom as you are far higher than wisdom and understanding of men like me. Those in love must know that a great fortune of fresh means of love has arrived in this ancient world form the spiritual world of angels. That is a world which has many wonders and provides guidance to the unguided residents of this world through godly messages in the form of revelations. O my people! Take the good news that a great expanse, of spiritual pleasures has arrived. Be pleased, as all narrowness’s and deficiencies have been replaced. His steps will spoil all misguidances. Sun has arrived into the shanty of the heir narrow crescent, when the Prophet sought from a humble slave like Bilal, when he said ‘O Bilal, provide comfort to us through your pleasing azaan. You are giving this call for prayer in slow tone out of the fear of the enemy. Now, you may go upon an elevated place and make an announcement of the blindness of the enemy who cannot see the brightness of God.”

The noble Prophet as an announcer of pleasures, breaths into the ear of every man in distress: ‘Get up, o the one beaten on your back! Get up and proceed on the path of prosperity. How long do you want to be in this narrow, ugly prison of this world full of lice. Be careful to see that no one hears of your helplessness! Be silent, and silently proceed on your path of prosperity. Without caring for that they think about you. wisdom tells all this to man, but, O Prophet, how can you be silent, as the root of enemy hair of yours is openly announcing before the world.

sections.heading: Worthless Reject the Worthy
paras: Inspite of all this open announcements, which are in the form of beatings of so many drums, the jealous enemy has become so deaf that he says: “where is any sound?” someone throws fresh flowers on his face but instead of getting pleased, he says, out of his blindness as to what is causing this pain. The impacts of flowers become injurious attacks for him. A Hoor gives him an affectionate pinch to wake him up and pulls him up toward her with affection. But this blind fellow feels that he is being harmed and asks her as to why she is causing pain and disturbance to him. He tells her “why are you pulling my hand and caressing my body. I am in sleep! Leave my alone so that I may sleep.” This blind fellow does not know that his is the hoor that the has been seeing in his dream. It would be better for him, if he opens his eyes, gets up and sees the prosperous feet of that beautiful moon.

sections.heading: Sufferings of Great Men
paras: Just as the blind sleeping fellow felt the graces for him as troubles, it may be seen, that those selected for and destined to progress suffer much more than others. This is because, they tease and rub with the causes of progress just as one teases beauties to be taken note of by them. He teases the beauties so much that some times even the blind fellows get disturbed. So also, a man in search of progress. Not only he suffers but he also makes the disinterested also suffer, who are like the blind fellows. Many a times, he goes to the blind and surrenders himself to them, who, out of their disregard and resentment get annoyed and create turmoil in their streets, which act as an indirect support for his cause.

chapters.title: Self-Acquired Knowledge
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of H. Hilal, (may God be pleased with him), who was sincere servant of God without having learnt obedience to God from others by way of followership, but his own hidden reasoning, not out of the helpless state of slavery of another, just as H. Luqman and H. Yusuf had done. This Hilal was a guard of the stable of a blind muslim chief. A blind man is aware of his mother but cannot realise about her person and form. Inspite of his not seeing her, if he honours and respects his mother, he can get deliverance because: “when God wishes good for a servant, he opens both the eyes of his heart so that he may see the hidden things. Search for this way through his life of the heart, because the life of the body is like that of an animal

paras: When you have heard about the high qualities of H. Bilal, you may now hear about the weaknesses of Hilal. He was far above Bilal in the matter of his proceedings on the way, of truth, being inimical to bad habits. He was not like you in going o the wrong path, which you do at every step, rather you go toward stoniness as against pearliness.

chapters.title: Lacking Determination
chapters.subtitle: To say something on similar lines

paras: This is like a person who became the guest of a rich man. The rich man asked him about his age; ‘My dear son, tell me how old you are. tell me correctly. Do not increase and decrease. Tell the exact age! “he said: it is eighteen, seventeen or even sixteen years. It may even be fifteen or perhaps ten years, my brother!”
The host said: “Go away from here as you have a confused mind. Go away as far away till the time you came of mother’s womb.”

chapters.title: Reverse Moving Horses
chapters.subtitle: A narrative similar to this talk

paras: A person asked for a horse from a rich man. He said: “you may take that blackish white horse!” He told him: “I do not want that horse!” the rich man asked: “why?” He said: “it is very haughty and takes back steps. It moves towards its tail on the reverse side”. The rich man said: “keep its tail toward your destination and let it move backside. By moving on the backside, it will reach your house”.

sections.heading: Mischief Potential for Good Purpose
paras: Tail of your horse is your haughty self-full of the craze of passions. That is: it moves always in the opposite direction. Its passions are, in fact, the base of its reverse going tail. Therefore, you may turn its reverse going passions towards the other world. When it is in wrong direction, it reaches the right place. When you shut the door of the food of its passions, the passions will rise their heads towards wisdom and nobility. This is just as: when you cut one branch of the tree, the tree’s energy to grow will go toward another branch making it stronger. Similarly, when you turn its tail in the other direction, it will move slowly to search the right and safe destination.

sections.heading: Physical, Mental Capacities Limited, Not Spiritual
paras: Great and appreciable are those horses (of the self) which are obedient and go on the right path on their own. They neither go in the reverse direction, nor are they haughty. They put their masters (bodies) on the right path. They are fast in speed and determined like the body of H. Musa, for whom a small patch of dry land of the size of a blanket, had become long and wide, at the meeting place of two water bodies, about which he had said. I shall not give up until I reach the junction of two sees or until I spent seven hundred years or years and years in travel: La abrahu hattaa ablugha majma’al Bahraini aw amdhia huquban (Kahaf: 18: 60)

That distance of seven hundred years or years and years of travel was seven hundred years long in the journey of love to perform which he was fully determined. This long journey would inevitably lead him to a high elevated place of paradise. When this was the determination of his body, the determination of his soul would be up to the highest in the highest places of spiritual level: a‘laa ‘illiyyin. Strong, determined, horse riders jumped into the racecourse to compete with and go ahead of others, while weak and dull headed fellows pitched theirs tents in lowly places.

chapters.title: Spirit to Be Free
chapters.subtitle: Another similar narrative to explain the same matter Return to the narrative of H. Hilal

paras: In similar manner, a caravan came near a village, when the gate of a village well was found open. One of the travellers said that they should camp on these nights of extreme chill here for some days along with our goods. there came a voice from the village: ‘you will have to keep your goods outside and then only you can enter the village’. (That is in order to protect yourself from extreme difficulties, you should go alone without bothering about your materials).

The inference is that while entering into the circle of those nearby to God, you should keep all your unwanted possessions outside and think of entering all alone. Other things than a clean heart is not allowed here as it is a highly elevated place.

H. Hilal’s heart was a master, and his soul was bright, and he was the slave of a Muslim chief, as a guard of his stable. Though he was a slave guarding a stable. He was a king of kings. He was not only a guard of the horses but also of his self, and far ahead of many things. But his master, the chief was not aware of his high status as he had the sight of Iblis who looked at the water and mud of which H. Adam was made and not the treasure that lay hidden underneath. He was looking only at the five senses of Adam, which he shared with other animals of the six-dimensional world. But he did not see the base of high wisdom and knowledge of the soul that was the special feature of H. Adam as against other animals. This is because, the colour of mud is clearly visible to the apparent eyes, but the light of faith is hidden underneath. This has been the situation of all prophets of God.

sections.heading: Different Capacities to See
paras: One looked at as obelisk but not the bird that was sitting atop. This bird was a royal falcon full of extraordinary abilities. Another looked at the bird, but only upon the flapping’s of its feathers, but not a hair that is held in his beak. Thus, there were two persons one, only looking at the obelisk, the second only at the flapping of the feathers, but both did not look at the hair that was held in its beak. But a third one, who looked at with the light of God worked at both the bird and the hair in its beak. He said: ‘look at the hair in the beak. So long as you do not look at the hair held in the beak, you will not know of the reality. Looking at the obelisk and the bird is something which many can do but looking a the hair in the beak needs a very deep sight. Man’s body is like the obelisk, his knowledge and worship are like the bird and his inner spiritual light is like the hair in the bird’s beak which only keen eyes can see.

So also, another man saw decorations in the slushy mud of man, while another looked at his heart full of knowledge and actions. Man’s body is like the obelisk, one his knowledge and acts are like the bird. One may imagine three hundred birds for comparison or only two birds, according to his ability.

A man of normal prudence sees only these two qualities that is, his knowledge and action and nothing behind or before him. The hair hidden in its mouth is a hidden special quality, which is a special light through which he sees what is unseeable by others. It is this light that gives immorality to man’s soul. A bird holding a hair in its mouth or the acts of the man with the special light can never be temporary and passing. His knowledge always receives inspiration and encouragement from his soul. This inspiration is self-generated, not borrowed or taken from others.

chapters.title: Contempt Prevents Deep Sight
chapters.subtitle: H. Hilal’s falling sick and his master’s ignorance of his sickness due to lack of concern, and contempt for him and the Prophet’s heart coming to know of it, and his visit to him and offering consolation

sections.heading: Stable Man
paras: As misfortune would do, H. Hilal fell ill and became very weak. Revelation from God informed the Prophet of it. But his master was not aware of his sickness, as he had as well no concern for him. He was only a worthless person of no consequence. A noble man lay ill in the stable for nine days and none was aware of this.

But that great man, emperor of the people (the Prophet) who had a wisdom as large as a hundred oceans was capable of reaching everywhere. Revelation from God came to him, and God’s mercy informed him that H. Hilal was sick. The noble Prophet went to the honourable Hilal to make enquiries about his health. Behind the sun of revelation, that moon (Prophet) was proceeding, and the companions were following him like stars. [The Prophet has said: My companions are like stars; you will be guided by following anyone of them]. The moon says that they are stars. They are guides to those travelling during night, and blazing fire for the rebellious as shooting stars.

The companions told the chief that their king has come, and he jumped out of joy and clapped his hands with pride and pleasure. Then he came down from the upstairs and started falling at the steps of the informer. Then he offered his respects and salutations to the Prophet with a pleased face, joyous like the rose. Then he said: “With God’s name, please honour the house by entering into it, so that this gathering may become like paradise. So that my house may attain a greatness higher than the sky as I have the honour of seeing the pole of the time.”

The Prophet said with reluctance: “I have not come to see you!” there was a slight disapproval in his tone. Then he said: “what is the worth of my soul for myself. It is yours! Please tell me for whose sake you took this trouble, so that I may become the dust of his feet, as there is a place for planting him in your garden.” By saying this, he gave up his contempt, and the Prophet was pleased to give up the disapproval of his conduct. Then he asked him: “where is that crescent (Hilal) of the sky of the space beyond heavens (‘arsh), who out of his humility has a place to settle on the carpet of moonlight. He is a king but hidden behind slavery, who has come into this world to investigate its affairs. Do not say that he is your slave and guard of your stable. But know that he is a treasure hidden under the ruins. How strange that, that full moon has turned their like the crescent due to sickness, under whose feet thousands of full moons fall.
The chief said: “I am not aware of his sickness, but for the part some days he has not come at my door. He lives in the company of camels and other animals. He is a guard and stays in the stable.”

chapters.title: Fragrance of Common Features
chapters.subtitle: Entry of the Prophet into the stable to enquire about H. Hilal’s health, and gracing him

sections.heading: The Prophet Went in Search of H. Hilal and Entered into the Stable. It Was Dark, Ugly and Filthy but When Love Entered into It, All These Things Vanished. That Male Lion (Hilal) Felt the Fragrance of the Prophet Just as H. Yaqub Felt the Fragrance of His Son, Yusuf
Miracles Do Not Cause Faith but Weaken Enemies
paras: Miracles do not become the causes of faith. Fragrance of commonness of features absorbs the qualities of the Prophets. Miracles are for the purpose of defeating the enemy, but the fragrance of the commonness of features is to snatch the hearts. The enemy gets defeated but does not become a friend. How can one whose neck is tied up become a friend?

With the impact of the fragrance, H. Hilal work up from sleep and wondered as to how there was such a fine fragrance in the bin of dung. Then he looked from under the legs of the animals and saw the lapel of the unmatchable Prophet. From the other corner of the stable he dragged himself and came to the Prophet and kept his face upon his feet. Then the Prophet kept his face upon his face and kissed his head, eyes and face and said: “O my friend! What kind of such a hidden pearl you are! O journey man from the ‘arsh, how are you? Are you well?”

H. Hilal said: “what can be the condition of the man in distressing dreams, who is woken up by the falling of sunshine on his face? What can be the condition of a thirsty man be who is sucking water from wet mud to quench his thirst and suddenly finds a flood of water near his head?”

chapters.title: Progress to Be Slow and Steady
chapters.subtitle: To explain that Prophet Muhammad heard that H. ‘Isa walked on water and said: “if he had greater confidence in God, he would have walked on air

paras: The Prophet heard that: Jesus Christ was carried upon by the river telling him; as you are the water of life, you are safe from drowning in water.”

The Prophet said: “If he had greater certainty in God’s authority, air also would have become like plain land for him to walk upon, just as in my case that I rode upon the air on the night of ascent (Mi‘raaj) to meet God.”

H. Hilal further said as his another example: what is the situation of that dirty, blind dog which got up from sleep and found itself to be like the lion. Not such a normal lion which can be shot with an arrow, but as one with whose fright the swords and arrows would break or like a blind fellow crawling up on his belly like the snake gets his eyes brightened and opened to the pleasing spring season and gardens.

sections.heading: Transfer from Physical World
paras: What about the one who get rid of his physical, apparent qualities of life and gets into the place of residence in the non-physical spiritual world. A fellow who not only resides in that place beyond the space (laa makaan) but also gives physical qualities to others around whose dining sheets all lions become so lowly as dogs. From his non-physical, spiritual quality, he provides bones to these dogs. These lions are the situations of disciples in search, who though on the path of the search of God are still at low levels being satisfied with a bone like the dog. They should not aspire for greater results as they have not become spiritually clean enough for them. While still being and this low level, they should not think of more. This is like the prevention of an unclean man from the touching of the Quran: Laa yamassuhu illaa al mutahharuun (waqi‘a: 56: 79). So long as he does not clean himself of the physical dirt and of the physical material qualifications, he should not try to go close to these great ideas.

sections.heading: Giving Up Human Qualities Is a Precondition
paras: When the disciple is told of this, he says: “whether I am clean or unclean, what else can I read in this material world? You may tell me that being unclean I should not go to the fountain; then you may also tell me how can I clean myself without going to the fountain. there is nothing but mud and dust outside the fountain and one who does not go into the fountain cannot clean himself. There is a contradiction here. You are also like a fountain from which cleanliness of the soul can be done. If water of the fountain and the generous qualities of the great masters are cleansing, it is incumbent upon them that they should take the unclean ones with them and cleanse them, other wise it would be a great for an enthusiastic disciple which would remain with him for ever”.

The master would say: water and the master, both have hundreds of honourable generosities in them, with which they would accept the unclean fellows and cleanse them. What I mean is that you should not take simply the human qualities as your object, and cleanse them including their cleansing, but that you should get rid of them in toto and try to add other spiritual qualities in the place vacated by them. Okey! Goodbye”!

sections.heading: Progress to Be Slow and Steady
paras: O Ziaulhaq! You have a light which can protect you from the worst of the mischief-making-birds. Your progressing, and moment by moment increasing of light protects you; and you are hidden from these mischievous birds just as the sun is hidden from the bat. What is the curtain that lies before the sun to protect it other than its own excessive piercing rays, its brightness and sharpness? This curtain of the sun is also the light of God of which bats and nights are deprived. When these two are behind the curtain and far away, they have become so frigid that they feel extreme chill before the black-faced and sinful fellows. When you narrated a little about the affairs of Hilal, as Hilal is taken so far as the narrow crescent, you may now bring about them in a larger extent as like the size of the full moon. This narration is like that between a disciple as crescent and the master as the full moon. Yet there is a commonness between them, but the difference is only with the extent of knowledge, which is totally devoid of ill will and mischief. The disciple is also cleansed of inner defects, yet he has to proceed little by little towards the perfectness of the master, just as the crescent proceeds toward full moonliness. The master gives him lessons of progress every night. Slow movement takes the raw fruit toward ripeness. He tells him to avoid fastness and stresses upon slowness telling that one has to go to the terrace by stepping upon the rungs of the ladder one after one. You must heat the cauldron little by little as a master cook does as meat is cooked for soup and taste in a slow manner

sections.heading: Even God’s Working Is Slow and Steady
paras: Was not God capable enough to create the heavens (and world) in one instant without any doubt by simply saying “Become” (Kun). Then why did he take six days to do that and that too a day stretching to a “Thousand years as per our calculation” as has been said: created the heavens and the earth in six day: Khalqz alsamaaawaati wal alardha fi sittati ayyaam: (A‘raaf: 7: 54) and six other times all over the Quran). And the length of His day as: A day in the sight of your lord is like a thousand years of your reckoning: Inna yawman ‘ida rabbika ka-alfa sanatin mimma ta‘udduuna: (Hajj: 22: 47).

[Thousand years of one day of our reckoning speaks volumes of the extent of the long period taken over for creation. Our day is not the same everywhere in the globe. A day includes both the bright day of sunlight and the dark night. It is exactly 12 hours of the day and 12 hours of night on the equator. Thus, God’s Day is 24 hours of the day into 355 days of the year into 1000 years. As we go northwards during summer, the duration of day increases and of the night decreases. The opposite of it happens in the southern hemisphere. That is; days are shorter and the nights longer and vice versa. And the day at the North Pole and South Pole consists of six months of day light and six months of night. That is: one day of the poles equals 365 day on the equator. Therefore, year there is 365 days by 365 days. This is the day of our reckoning. This multiplied by 365x365x1000 years is God’s Day. Again, while the rotation of the earth is one day (24 hours), the rotation of Venus is 243 days of earth. This duration goes on increasing as we go to other cosmic bodies.

However, “day of our reckoning” requires the considered on the arithmetical time of seconds, minutes and so on. But God is not governed by this time scale. He has His own time scale which his beyond our understanding. He is timeless and spaceless. This leads us to consider the duration of the time of reckoning to millions of years from the time of big bang to this day for the creation of everything the first event of creation being the event of big bang. These two verses taken together with reference to the explanation given two verses taken together with reference to the explanation given above in vol the entire subject of cosmology, astronomy, biology etc in the evolutionary process, which as still in the process of evolution — Translator]

sections.heading: Time for Making of Adam
paras: Birth of a human baby takes nine months, proceeding level by level. This is the conduct of the Great king. So also, the creation of Adam took forty days (of thousand years each) and there was an increase of his mud, little by little! And the period from this morning to that morning of each of the days of these forty days was a thousand years, when at last, he assumed the form that he had, and his children now have.

Therefore, O searcher of the path of Truth, you are still immature, but you want to run fast. you are yet a child and you want to make yourself a master and guide. You want to grow faster than others like the pumpkin. Where do you have the capacity to receive inspiration from God, to struggle for it and the capacity to stand firm upon it. Pumpkin for its fast growth seeks the support of a wall and tree. With your baldness and lack of capacity and self-possession you want to grow like pumpkin. To start with, your vehicle to proceed was like a straight cypress but as time went on you became dry, empty and devoid of pulp. O pumpkin, know well that very soon your green colour will turn yellow as it was not original coming from within but adopted from outside like the make-up powder.

chapters.title: Greed of Wealth, Love, Sex
chapters.subtitle: Story of an old woman who beautified her ugly face with make-up powder, but it was of no use, and she did not look beautiful

paras: There was a ninety-year-old woman whose face was full of wrinkles and pale like saffron. Her face had wrinkles upon wrinkles like the windings of a turban. But she had a desire to be married. All her teeth had fallen, and the hairs were white like milk. Her tall height had bent down like a bow and all her senses upturned. But her love and sexual craze for a husband was perfect. She had a desire for hunting, but her net was torne into pieces. A roaster crowing at in appropriate time! A man desirous of travelling but without a path to tread upon! There was an empty cauldron with fire below!

Her case was like that of a fellow who desires to go to the battlefield but has neither the horse nor the legs to ride upon. Or of a person who wants to play the flute but does not have. The flute or the lips to play. May not even the rejectors of God suffer from the pangs of love in old age. How pitiable is the fellow who is provided with this craze in old age!

When the dog becomes old, its teeth fell off. Instead of biting men, it resorts to eating filth. But look at these sixty years old, dog like wretches, whose teeth become shaper, day by day. The hairs of the old dog fall down from the skin, but their doggish fellows put on silk garments. Their love and greed for wealth, gold and sex goes on increasing every moment like the breeding of puppies by bitches. This is an age when they are the capital and possession of hell, and God’s wrath takes them to the butchers to pull out their skin. When people tell them: “may you live long”, their hearts get pleased, and their mouths open with laughter and smile. They consider this curse as a prayer and blessing, which in fact is a curse. They do not open their eyes and raise their heads in caution. If one such fellow were to see a little of the final end of next life, he would say: “may such a long life be for you alone”.

chapters.title: When Prayer Becomes Curse
chapters.subtitle: Story of a darvesh who prayed for a man from Geelan: “May God take you back to your native place” with all security and safety

paras: A well-built beggar told a rich man from Geelan: Put some food into my begging bag as I am in need, so that in return, I may pray for you.” After collecting bread, he said: “O God, send him back in all safety to his native place.”
The rich man said: “if it is to that house of mine that I have seen, O confused fellow, may God send you there.”

Mean fellows spoil the mood of every good speaker, and make his high talks go low. Therefore, what has to be said depends upon the level of the audience, just as the tailor has to cut the size of the cloth to stitch according to the measurements of the wearer. As the audience cannot remain devoid of such lowly people, the speaker has no alternative than to speak of lowly and less worthy matters.
Leave this discussion at this level and proceed on to the story of that old woman.

chapters.title: Deficiencies of Old Age
chapters.subtitle: Return to the story of the character of the old woman

paras: When a man attains old age, he is not a man on the manly ways. Such a fellow may be named as that old woman about whom we said earlier. This fellow neither possesses any wealth and investment nor has any acceptability anywhere, nor even the capacity to accept the same if offered. He can neither please anybody nor can be pleased. He does not have any perfectness nor a desire to attain. He has no proper tongue to speak-well, or ears to hear properly, nor wisdom, nor insight. He does not have consciousness, unconsciousness or any thoughts. He has no beauty and the demands and expectations of admiration that the beautiful ones expect. He is ugly with layer upon layer of ugliness like the layers of onions. He has neither completed his walk on the path of gnosis of God, nor he has a step for others to step upon. He does not have any vigour, warmth of love, passions or this sighs of failures.

chapters.title: Fit for Nothing
chapters.subtitle: Story of a darvesh who was told “not available” for anything that he asked for

paras: A darvesh went to a house and asked for stale or fresh bread. The house owner said: “where is it here? Are you mad that you mistake this house as a bakery? He said: “Give me a piece of dried fat; and was told: “this is not a butcher’s shop”. He said: “O master, give me a fistful of flour.” And he said: “do you think that this is a flour mill?’ then he said: “Give me a little water in a tumbler.” And he replied: “you are not standing before a well or a stream to seek water”. The house owner made fun of and ridiculed at everything from bread to husk that he asked for.

The darvesh then entered into the house and lifted his shirt up tried to sit down to empty his bowls. The house owner said: “what the hell are you doing?” then the darvesh said: “keep quiet! Let me relieve myself in this ruined place. A place where there is nothing to live upon, it fit only for emptying the bowls.”

sections.heading: Fit for Nothing
paras: You are not a falcon to catch a prey and as one taught to pray upon by the king. You are not a peacock with hundreds of decorations and designs upon you to please and brighten the eyes. You are not a parrot to fed with sugar so as to turn the ears upon you to hear sweet sounds. You are not a bulbul to cry in the garden like a man in love. You are also not a hoopoe to carry a message as it did when H. Sulaiman asked it to go to the queen of Sheba. Nor you are a crane to enhance the worth of the surroundings of a place by going to India in winter and to Turkey in spring season. For what job are you fit to be engaged in? what kind of a bird you are to prepare a dish of it to eat with food?

sections.heading: What the Worthless Should Do
paras: You are of no worth! You may go away from the place where people keenly look at, assess worth and bargain the price to buy. You may go to the shop of God who is a very generous and good buyer. He purchases those materials which nobody thinks of looking at, because of being worthless old scraps. No counterfeit and duplicated material is rejectable in His court, as His object in purchasing is not profit-making. His buying and profiting are only for the reason that He is very generous and of extremely good conduct. His grants and graces have no limits and therefore do not have disappointed with Him.
Leaving this matter at this I proceed toward that old woman’s story as there is no end to the discussion which I had till now.

chapters.title: How to Hide Ugliness
chapters.subtitle: Return to the story of the old woman

paras: In the neighbourhood of that old woman there was a marriage celebration and they had invited her also. That old woman decided to attend the function and so she blackened her eyebrows, black like tar after sharpening and dressing them well. She kept a mirror in front of her face in order to dress well and made-up her face, cheeks and chin. She smeared too much of powder, but the wrinkles of face could not be hidden. She tore off ten written verses from Quran and pasted on her face to hide the hollows of her face and make herself as a gem in the circle of other beautiful women. Her face had so many hollows which she pasted with so many sheets of the Quran, that whenever she touched the mantle on her head, these would fall down. She would wetten those sheets with her tongue and again paste them all around her face. And again, on resetting her mantle, these would fall on the floor. When she did like this for many a times and could not avoid their falling, she cursed upon Satan for this.

sections.heading: Pretention and Show for Applause
paras: At this, Satan took a physical form and said to her: “O vicious lady with dry flesh, to whom none would approach! I had never thought like this in my entire life and I have not seen, anyone as vicious as you are! You have sown a strange seed of disgrace that you have not left the Quran without it. You are an army with five divisions within five divisions of the devils. O ugly woman! Spare me from your curses. How long can you steal the ten verses of Quran on paper to make your face colourful like the apple.

sections.heading: Stealing the Words of Great Men
paras: How long do you steal the words of the men of God like that old woman) in order to sell them to the people to receive their applause? Borrowed and pasted colours did not make your colour rosy. A branch of tree tied upon another tree cannot be like its own original branch. At last, when the mantle of death comes over to you all those ten verses of the Quran pasted on your face will fall down. When the command of marching from this world comes, all the magic of our oratory and words will come to end. The time of total silence will stand before you and direct you to stand up. Great regret upon the one who does not possess regard and concern for truth.

sections.heading: Beautify the Heart
paras: Polish and brighten your chest for a day or two and make it a mirror to keep the record of your possessions. When you do this, your soul will become so effective as that of the handsome Yusuf whose birth took place at a very rare occasion, when Saturn and Jupiter come together in the same constellation (Sahib qaran). As an impact of Yusuf’s soul elderly Zulaikha became youthful. Just as the temperature of the chilly water changes upon receiving the impact of sun, your temperament will also change. With the impacts of the warmth of the soul of Mariyam (Mary) the dry lips of the date palm got refreshed to provide dates.

O elderly woman! How long do you want to stand in opposition to the laws of nature (fate). Forget all that you have done so far and search for now attainments. There is no hope of the regaining of the lost beauty of your face, whether you smear your face with powders and colour and blacken your eyebrows. This is what a sinner must also do to come back to the goodness and noble acts.

chapters.title: What Are Miracles and Their Impacts
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a sick man in whom no marks of regain of health were seen by the physician

paras: A sick man went to a physician asking him to test his pulse calling him to be a specialist in it. He told him: “I especially choose you because, through the beating of the pulse, you can find out the condition of the heart as the vein of the wrist has a direct connection with the heart. As the heart is hidden from the sight, you may search for it through something resembling it, as the pulse has a connection with it.

sections.heading: Invisible Powers of Materials, Prophets and Saints
paras: Air is hidden from the eyes, but it can be seen in the movements of dust and leaves and find out whether it is moving from right side or the left. Movement of the leaves clearly indicates this. You can know of the impacts of love on the heart in the intoxication like-signs in the eyes. As you are away from the essence of God, you can see it through His attributes, and the attributes through His messengers and miracles. Miracles and hidden marvels create impacts upon the hearts of the people which are provided to some selected saints, as there are hundreds of doomsday-like-turmoil’s in their hearts, the minimum impact of which is that one nearby to them also gets impacted by them. Their hearts also become lively. They also become fortunate to be close by to God. The saint places all his mental and spiritual possessions before them. A miracle impacts upon non-living objects, whether it is a staff or river as in the case of H. Musa; and the moon as in the case of H. Muhammad, which became obedient to them. Their power of miracles comes to those who are nearby to God. Staff, river and moon are the means of exhibiting directly the power of miracles on lifeless objects to put on indirect impact upon hearts of men. When they put a direct impact upon the heart of men without any intermediary, an invisible connection gets established between the prophets and saints on the one hand and their immediate, closest followers on the other side. This has greater impacts than upon the lifeless objects.

sections.heading: What Are Miracles and Their Impacts
paras: Impacts upon the lifeless objects are temporary, instant and short-lived. They put a permanent impact upon the clear, sincere hearts. This is like the strength that one gets by eating on non-living bread, which is made of another non-living malt. How great it would be if one gets strength and vigour without bread, directly coming without the medium of bread. You may consider the limitless dining sheet of Jesus Christ feeding the people without visible means. So also, in the case of Mary who was provided with fresh fruits from a dried-up tree. So also, the messages they got without any physical, visible, communication system.

Miracles cause their impacts from the perfect soul upon the seekers of the perfection of their soul, just as life causes impacts upon the body. consider the miracle as a river and an imperfect soul as a land-bird, which cannot live upon water, as against a water bird. The impact of the miracle upon air imperfect soul is to make it humble and weak, but to give greater vigour and strength to the worthy, matured person and making him more active. If you do not feel such an impact upon your heart, you may ignore the power of miracles and devote yourself in entirety to wisdom and apparent arguments, because you are not one of a perfect heart or of imperfect heart, but one somewhere in between. The impacts from God are clear upon the apparent sensual perception. They can also carry the hidden commands of these impacts upon the heart. This is like the impacts of the medicines, which are not visible but certainly have their hidden impacts and results. This is also like the impacts seen in certain objects caused by magic and sorcery. In these cases, the apparent acts are different from the impacts and results. There are hidden powers in them, but when they act upon, certain objects you can see those hidden powers in some other form.

sections.heading: See God Through His Impacts
paras: When all these things and their powers make appearances before you, then why do you not see God through His impacts upon so many things. Causes and effects though not seeable as materials; yet they can be considered as materials like the rind and pulp of fruits. If you ponder over all causes and all effects, you can know that all are from God. When you are in the habit of believing in and befriending many things upon the bases of their impacts, what makes you to remain unaware of the Granter of these effects and impacts. On the basis of some thoughts and ideas, you fall in love and befriend those of the same mental and perceptive. Then, why do you not befriend the king of everything (both physical and non-physical) between the east and the west.
However, be sure that there is no end to this discussion; and so also there is no end to our greed to know more and more.

chapters.title: Man, Searchers What He Does Not Have
chapters.subtitle: Return to the narrative of the sick man

paras: Return and speak of the narrative of that sick man’s affair with the well informed and secretive physician. The physician caught his pulse and came to know fully well about his sickness that there was no scope for his recovery as his tuberculosis has reached the last stage. Instead of saying this he asked him: “to fulfil and satisfy all his desires to get rid of the chronic illness. Do what ever you feel like doing and do not hesitate at all, as otherwise any hesitation to do that and follow of the regimen will cause you more trouble. Regimen and forbearance are very harmful for this sickness. do whatever you feel like doing. It is for such and such a sick person that God’s saying: “do what you will: I ‘maluu maa shi‘tum: (Haa Miim: 41: 40) can be taken liberally.”

sections.heading: Meeting of Desires Before Death
paras: The sick man said: “Uncle, thanks to you. you may go on your line, and I shall go to the riverbank to have a nice time.” So, saying he was strolling as per his desire along the riverbank to get the gates of health open. On the river bank a Sufi was sitting, washing his hands and face to increase his cleanliness. His eyes fell on his neck, and he got a strange, foolish desire to give a blow upon it. He lifted his hand to take an aim for this, thinking: “if I do not fulfil my desire and it goes unfulfilled, this would become further of sickness as that physician has warned. That is why I should give blow on his neck as otherwise I would be disobeying God’s command: and do not make your own hands contribute to your destruction: wa laa tulquu bi aidiakum ilattahlukati: (Baqara: 2: 195). Patience upon the desire and regimen in my case results in death. Therefore, give many blows upon his neck and do not be inactive like the lazy.”

sections.heading: Risky to Beat a Weak Man

When He Gave a Blow There Was a Loud Sound of the Blow, the Sufi Cried Out: “O Disobedient to Your Parents and Pimp for Your Own Wife” and Thought of Giving Two-Three Blows upon Him and Pull Out His Beard and Mustacheos. but He Saw Him to Be Very Tired and Sick, Very Thin, Degraded, Weak and Ill Clad. Then He Looked upon His Weakness and Thought: “He Would Die If I Give Him Just One Blow. He Is Completely Ruined by Tuberculosis Rendering Him Completely Weak and Shattered
Greed of Long Life
paras: People suffer from tuberculosis which has no remedy, but at the same time, think of giving blows to others upon the instigations from Satan. They are very pleased by giving troubles to innocent people and always in search of the defects of each other. O the one desirous of hitting upon the neck of others, why do you not think of your own neck. You think that satisfying the desires of your self as a remedy for your sickness and you think of slapping upon the faces of weak and humble. The one who told you that this is a remedy for your sickness is the same Satan who had taken your father Adam toward the wheat grain telling: O both of you and your wife, as seekers of help may eat this grain as a medicine for your weakness as stated that you should become immortals: aw takuuna minal khalidiina: (A‘raaf: 7: 20). He cajoled them and hit them upon their necks; but his hitting reversed and became a punishment for himself. He made them slip in a slippery place, but God came to their rescue and protected them.

sections.heading: Certainty of Faith in God’s Help
paras: H. Adam was a mountain though full of shakes. He was a mine of antidote and therefore remained unaffected by poison. When you are not even a particle of antidote, why are you careless about your relief? Where do you have that trust and reliance upon God to be protected by Him, which H. Ibrahim had? Where do you possess that honourable state that H. Musa had? H. Ibrahim’s dagger did not cut the throat of H. Isma’il, because, of his total reliance upon God. Because of H. Musa’s reliance upon God, a highway was created for him in the sea. You do not have that reliance to be protected from disasters.

These are the cases of reliance upon God of the prophets. There is also the well known case of H. shaikh Shujaa‘ Sayid, who dropped down from a minaret. But air filled up in his clothes and acted as a cushion and he remained unharmed. You certainly do not have such fortune with you and in such a case you should not go toward destruction.

sections.heading: Results of Lack of Certainty
paras: You should know that thousands of such persons fell down from the top like the people of ‘Aad and got destroyed in entirety. You can see such persons in lakhs who fell down upside down from heights. You do not know how to walk on a tightrope as the acrobats walk and therefore be thankful to your legs and walk on the ground, and do not think of walking on the rope. Do not make feathers and wings of paper and try to fly down from a top the hill, as because of such madness many heads were lost.”

sections.heading: Sight and Insight
paras: Though that Sufi got filled up with burning fire within him, yet he was careful enough to look at what was to come in the end. Only that person in the first rank remains safe like the bird which looks at the net and avoids picking up the grain. Two far-seeing eyes are a great asset for a wise man which protect his body from going wrong. The greatest Muhammad, who saw every particle of hell while still remaining away from it. He saw the ‘arsh, (empyrean) and throne of God and the paradise while living upon the earth itself. He saw them so clearly that he tore off all the curtains of carelessness and ignorance.

sections.heading: Search for Non-Existents
paras: To remain protected, you should shut your eyes from the presently visible things and think to look at the final end of matters. In such a case you will see all invisible, non-physical existents as present before you. you will also see that the directly visible existents to the eyes are imperfect and lowly. You will see that every man is in search of non-physical existents throughout the day and night. A beggar in search of generosity which is not existing before him. So also, a businessman is in search of profit which his not existing at the moment. This is to come later. So also, a farmer is in search of a non-existing crop in the ears of his plants which do not exist when he does to the field to plough. Students search of knowledge in the schools which they do not possess. So also the worshippers search for the contentment which they do not have. All of them have thrown behind their back what all they presently have before them and gone after things which hare not present before them. All this is because the mines and activities and treasure of God are nothing but non-existents initially and invisible.

On this point, earlier also I have painted out (in the fifth volume) in detail. Do not consider that as different from what I say now. I have said there that every maker searchers for a vacant place where the object of his making does not exist. An engineer searches for a vacant site to build a structure, or ruined houses which have lost their roofs. A water carrier takes an empty vessel with no water and a carpenter searchers for a house that has no doors.

sections.heading: Why Death Is Hated Through It Leads to Non-Existence
paras: Inspite of all this, look at this strange thing that these hunters of non-existents hate death which take them to the world of non-existence. Think over. When all your hopes in the life are upon meeting non-existents, why you try to avoid this path to non-existence. Why do you quarrel with your very nature which goes on searching for non-existents? when you are called toward non-existence (after death). When you are a friend of non-existences all though in every matter why do you try to avoid another kind of non-existence? This is inspite of the fact that, you are disgusted of everything that you have; and thrown the fishhook of your heart in the river of non-existence. Yet you feel disgusted of this means of the achievement of your object. The fishhook of your heart has provided you with lakhs of objects, but you call this final object of non-existence as death and loss of all your possessions. Look at this strange logic and magic that you call the tree of greater achievements as death. The magic of this artistry has shut both of your eyes to such an extent that your life is more inclined towards your possessions and existents which hare like a deep well. Yet there is a hidden design of God in this, that this well is covered up with a forest full of poison and snakes. Because of the hidden design he considers the well as a place of refuge to such an extents that death itself throws him into this well. This is how wrong is mistaken as right and right as wrong.
My dear, you know what many wrongs on man’s part that I have spoken of have been heard by me from Shaikh attar also.

chapters.title: Misconceptions Bring Misfortune
chapters.subtitle: Narration of Sultan Mahmood and a Hindu slave

paras: Shaikh Fariduddin Attar, may God’s mercy be upon him, has narrated about sultan Mahmood Ghazi in a poem that in a battle in India, he got a Hindu slave as a war prize. He made him his vicegerent and made him sit with him on the throne. He made him the commander of his army and called him as his son. All details spread out in his poem may be seen layer by layer in this poem written by this great scholar of faith, shaikh Attar. The sum and substance is: the boy sat along with the great king on the golden throne. But instead of getting pleased the boy started crying and shedding tears. The king told him: “O good fellow with a good fortune, why do you cry? Does this rulership appear unpalatable to you? You have become higher than the sky and companion of the king! You are sitting on the throne; and the ministers and the armies are standing in ranks before your throne like the moon and stars.”

The boy said: “the reason for my crying is that my mother in the city of my country upon getting angry with me used to always curse me by saying that she would like to see me in the hands of Mahmood the lion. And my father used to scold her: “what kind of anger and disapproval is this? Can you not think of any other milder curse, which is lesser in pain than this life-taking curse? You are very hard-hearted and merciless that you become a killer for him with hundreds of swords.”

“I used to get wonderstruck at his strange talk. I used to feel extreme sorrow and fear thinking: ‘ah, what kind of a person of hellish nature this Mahmood is that he has become a citation of cruelty and torture. I used to shiver at your thought. I was totally unaware of your generosity and honourable treatment. My mother is nowhere now to see me on your throne. O king of kings! Amy my father is also not here to see me in this state, that I am sitting by the side of the king of faith in all comfort.”

sections.heading: Poverty Is a Boon
paras: O the one devoid of courage, know this that the fear of poverty and lack of possession is frightening like Mahmood as was for that boy, though he was a very generous king. But your nature always keeps you afraid of poverty and lack of possessions. It is like that Hindu slave’s fear of Mahmood. If you were to know the benefits that you get from poverty and deprivation. You would consider them to be as generous and profit giving as Mahmood was. Then you would say: it is not the present bad situation but future reward that should be considered. You are half-hearted and ignore the fact that your poverty is a guarantee of betterness in future like what Mahmood the generous was to that boy. Therefore, do not hear what your pitiful mother tells you out of misguidance and ignorance. When you become a victim of poverty of true knowledge, you will later cry on the doomsday just as that boy cried in later life. Though your body is the up bringer of your physical existence like the mother, it is your enemy more inimical than a hundred enemies.

sections.heading: Good Effects of Bad Company
paras: When the body becomes sick, it engages you in the search of medicines; and when it is strong and healthy, it makes you mischievous like devil. Consider this body as your coat of mail, which is not good either in winter by becoming cold, nor in summer by becoming hot. Similarly, your body does not give you comfort any time. But for development of patience, which is a quality of the heart, a bad companion is a better friend that he prepares your heart to be large enough to bear troubles with patience and pleasure. Patience makes the moon brighter on the dark nights, for which it has to wait for long. Patience of the flower in the company of thorns makes it more fragrant. Patience of the milk in the midst of blood and dung makes it worthy of giving life to the baby. Surrounded by the rejectors, the patience of the prophets made them prosperous and special servants of God.

sections.heading: Patience: Harbinger of Success
paras: Whenever you see one in good clothing’s, you may think that he had patience and worked hard to make money. Whenever you see an ill-dressed, poor fellow, you may consider that this is due to his lack of patience on pains and troubles. when you see a person in distress and full of remorse. You may think he has disconnected his affairs with God and depended upon untrustworthy affairs of the world. Had he resorted to patience and not established his affairs with dishonest friends, he would not have received a slap of separation on his face. He would have resorted to consonance with God just as honey does with milk. He would have had the occasion to say: I do not love that sets: Laa uhibbulaafiliin: (An‘aam: 6: 76), just as H. Ibrahim had said when the star disappeared. Certainly, he would not have become lonely after losing companions, just as fire remains lonely after the caravan left the camp. When a man does not remain patient in loneliness and becomes a friend of untrustworthy fellows, he will have to feel sorrows of separation and undergo losses. This is what happens when a man deviates from the friendship of God out of impatience and goes to seek help of unworthy fellows. When you have sincere sense of friendship like pure gold, you should not keep it in trust with untrustworthy fellows. Develop the habit of keeping your good things with you only so that they are not lost and remain protected from mismanagement. Let your habit be like that of the One who has created habits, who has given good habits to the prophets. If you give a lamb in trust to Him, he will give a flock of sheep as it is He who has created all habits. But you are in the habit of keeping a lamb in trust with a wolf and thus you create a situation of keeping the lamb and the wolf together.

sections.heading: Bad Results of Ignorance
paras: An ignorant and foolish fellow tries for your friendship, and you allow him to do so. In the end it will result in troubles for you. He is like a bisexual who has, both the male and female organs and will be true to exhibit the functions of both. He hides the male organ from women and make them as his sisters; and when he goes to men, he hides the female organ, behaves like man and sits with them. But men of wisdom and insight find out his duality and God will show the hidden organ to them as clearly as the trunk of the elephant.
