God clearly shows his reality from his styles and behaviour so that His friends may not fall into his trap. This is not the case only with a person possessing these two physical organs together, which do not give him perfect manliness. This is also so, with many other men also, who do not possess real manliness. So also, in the case of the ignorant fellow who hides his ignorance and poses himself as a scholar. You should be very careful about all these three types of fellows.

sections.heading: Difference Between Mother’s and Father’s Love
paras: Do not ever hear the sweet and pleasing words of an ignorant fellow as these are like outdated poisons. He will call you as dear to him as his mother and the brightness of his eyes. These words from him do not increase anything other than sorrows and false desires. A mother openly tells a father that her child has become weak and dull upon going to the school. She accuses the father telling: “Had this child been from your other wife, you would not have put so much cruelty upon him.” But the father would say: “Had this child of mine been from another women, she would also speak the same nonsense.” Be careful to run away from such magic words of the mother and know well that a slap on the child’s face by the father is better than the sweets given by the mother. Consider the commanding self of the man as the mother and his wisdom as the father. Beginning of the father cause many restrictions but their ends are great relaxations.

sections.heading: Trust in God and Proceed
paras: O provider of wisdom! Hear our grievances and provide redressals to us. So long as you do not worth for something for us. No one will wish for that for us. The demand in us for goodness is created by You, and You alone fulfil the same. We are nothing! You are the beginner, and you are the culminant. You alone speak. You alone hear and you alone remain. Inspite of providing of so much of beauty and proper dressing, we are absolutely nothing. Keeping this in view, you may also increase the desire for worshipping and prostrations before you and do not cause any laziness, slackness and feelings of helplessness under the false notions that all our actions are already decided by fate.

sections.heading: Till Here Givin to Ustad for Corrections on 6-8-2022
Predestination: Guides and Misguides
paras: Predestination and fate are the feathers and wings of the perfect people as well as they are a chain and prison for the lazy. It depends upon how they take its meanings. Consider predestination as the water of the river Nile which was water for the faithful and blood for the rejectors, as had happened during the days of H. Musa. Wings and feathers take the falcons toward the king and the crows toward graveyards. Predestination is antidote as well as poison depending upon the takers. You may now return to the story of sultan Mahmood and the Hindu boy to understand as to how your perceptions and imaginations go wrong and get obliterated as the antidote was mistaken by his parents as poison. The noble king was misunderstood as predestined cruel, but the Hindu boy found out the truth about the kindness of Mahmood. You may also do so and proceed on this line. Do not be afraid of Mahmood for his imagined cruelty. Fear the stage of ignorance in which you are now living as your fear of baseless thought will not sustain and get obliterated. You are also to be obliterated in the end. What happens is: one obliteration of yours falls in the love of your already obliterated wrong thoughts, making one obliteration lead the other obliteration. When these unworthy thoughts and baseless fears go away, your own senselessness becomes clear to you.

chapters.title: Acts and Omissions Remembered After Death
chapters.subtitle: The noble Prophet has said: those who passed away do not regret death, but regret for what they lost

paras: [There is no Hadith(s) to express this meaning. However, it is stated in the Quran that the deniers express regret not upon the loss of their physical body but upon the non-performance of good acts, which they had considered to be of no worth during their lifetime. It is a cause of sorrow for unbelievers: Wa innahu lahasratun ‘alaa al kafiriin: (Haaqqa: 69: 50) —Qazi Sajjad Hussain and Translator]

Truly has said that commander of humans (Muhammad): whoever passes away from the world has no pain of death, regret and loss, but hundreds of regrets upon what he has lost by not doing good things during lifetime. He said that there is no regret of death, but their regret is connected with what they lost, thinking as to why they did not take death as their ultimate object which is a treasury to keep safe all wealth and materials. But they had made life alone as the centre of their object of all thoughts with their defective sight, which all got lost in death. The regret of these dead people is not on death, but upon imaginary marks and symbols in which they spent their whole life. They think we did not care to think that these symbols are just showy like surf, which shake and receive their sustenance from the sea. When the sea throws the surf upon the shore it ceases to float and enters into the graveyard of surfs. There, you may ask the surf as to what happened to its movements and vibrations. ‘Now the sea has put you into extreme inactivity’. When you ask these questions to it, will answer to you not with the lips but with its body language that these questions should be put not to it but to the sea.

sections.heading: See the Cause of Events
paras: Symbols and markings do not come into action without the actions of the sea just like the surf. Dust cannot go high up without being lifted up by the wind. When you have seen the actions of the wind, you may see the air thorough the wind. And when you have seen the surf, you may look at the sea through the surf which has created it. Be careful to look at these things and the forces behind them. It is this looking that is useful to you as otherwise your body is nothing but the warp and weft of your flesh and fat. Your fat cannot increase the light of the candle and your flesh cannot be roasted meat for the drunkards. Therefore, ignore this body and melt it down in full through austerities and devote yourself to sighting, looking and observing things hidden behind.

sections.heading: Emptiness: Prerequisite for Creativity
paras: There is a sight which sees only two yards of the way and there is a sight which sees the face of the kings of both the worlds. There is an immeasurable distance between them, and therefore search for the eyeblack that can brighten your eyes to the see the Knower of all hidden things. When you have heard about the ocean of the non-material-existents, you may try to be always in the world of nothingness of the non-material existents. because the base of the workshop of all materials is this world of nothingness, which is devoid of space and markings and, but only emptiness. You may see that all masters search for nothingness, emptiness and defectiveness to exhibit their talent and expertise to bring about their products or to set aright defects. Inevitably the master of all masters, who is totally not in need of any means and support (samad) has His workshop in the world of nothingness and emptiness. Wherever this nothingness is more, His workshop and creativity turns towards it.

Thus, nothingness of possessions is at the highest level and therefore, the dervishes who deny every material for themselves are at a higher level than all others. In particular that dervish, who has no care and concern for materials and even for his body. to look at he is totally a destitute, but he has nothing to desire and think for. One who asks for things is one who is in need or who has lost what he had. But a contented man has no care even for his body and does not need anything. He is entirely different. Therefore, try to be one like him and do not ever complain of any deprivation for the body as body is like a horse that runs very fast towards destruction. We have said this much to you. beyond this, may be thought about by your own self. And when your thinking gets tired, you may resort to meditation.

sections.heading: Man Acts, God Accepts
paras: Meditation stimulates and activates thinking. Make it like the hot sun to warm up the rigidity of mind. But also be careful to know that mere acts of worship and meditation will not lead you toward God. What is required is an attraction from God also. And first because this attraction is not in your control, but in God’s control, do not lose hope. Go on doing acts of worship and meditation as non-performance of acts speaks of disinterestedness, haughtiness, laziness and pride and these things are not worthy for a man of action, boldness and courage. Therefore, my boy, do not also go for the acceptance of good acts as it is not in your hands. Go in for obeying the commands of good acts and avoidance of bad acts. This alone is in your hands. Do your duty and leave the rest to God. The bird of acceptance will fly from its nest at some moment all of a sudden and you will see the light of the morning, and you will no more be in need of your struggles. You may put out the lamp. This light will open up your eyes and it will provide to you the insight through which you will see the inner aspects just like seeing the pulp beyond the rind. One with the grant of this light looks at the sun of all existences in a particle and the entire ocean in a single drop. He will see the appearance of God in every particle of the universe.

chapters.title: Be Careful About Revenge Taking
chapters.subtitle: Further return to the narrative of the Sufi and Qazi

sections.heading: [Continuation of the Narrative of the Sufi Who Was Given a Blow on His Neck by the Sick Man]
Fighting with a Weak Man
paras: While thinking that he should also give a slap to the sick man who gave a blow on his neck, the Sufi thought that he should also not do so and put his head in the risk of getting cut off. He thought I am a wearer of torne clothes, as such, I am a possessor great patience and consonant with fate which has made it easy for me to bear with the pain of the blow.” He found his opponent in extreme weakness and thought that if he also gave a blow to him, he would get splashed with it like molten lead, and the king would punish me and order for the payment of blood money to his heirs. His tent is already torne and its pegs are broken. He appears to be in search for an excuse to fall down by expecting a revenge from me for his blow at me. If he falls down and dies it will be a calamity upon calamity for me for the sake of this already dead fellow. This will entitle me to go under the sword of punishment for murder.

sections.heading: Great Worth of Judges
paras: When the Sufi felt that it was not proper to hit upon his opponent, he decided that he should be taken before the Qazi (judge), as the Qazi is a measure and balance of truth and his inclination is always toward truth. He is a cause to put an end to the mischiefs and treacheries of devil and one to imprison him. His words bring about peace. He is a scissors to cut off the causes of quarrels and malice and one to put an end to the quarrels and arguments of opponents as plaintiffs and defendants. His spells imprison the devils in the bottle and his order puts all mischiefs to end. When a greedy opponent looks at his balance, he gives up his arrogance and greed and becomes obedient to his command. Without this balance, even if you give more than his demand, his cunningness will never agree even to this. How can his hollow nature agree with you because of its foolishness and lack of wisdom? Qazi is merciful and one to put an end to all quarrels. He is like a drop from the ocean of the justice of the doomsday.

sections.heading: Parts Speak of the Whole
paras: Though a drop is very small and slow in motion, it exhibits the softness of all the water of the ocean. If you keep the mosquito net clean and clear. You can see the large river like Tigress in a drop. Parts speak of the conditions of the wholes just as twilight is an announcer of the oncoming of the sun. twilight is so certain a thing that upon it God has sworn and declared it to be upon the clean body of the Prophet, which is the exponent of his soul by comparing it with: I call to witness the ruddy glow of the sunrise: Falaa uqisimu bil shafaqi: (Inshiqaq: 84: 16). An ant which possesses only are grain shudders at the thought of the loss of the grain. Had it been in a harvest home it would not have done so. Similarly, if a man looks at further possibilities, he will not feel distress upon losses.

sections.heading: Resorting to Revenge Taking
paras: Now you may come to take the lesson from this narrative. The Sufi was heartless and fast in taking revenge. One who commits many harms but has a happy heart will not think of taking revenge. There is a possibility that he might forget the achievement she had made by that time. Or wreck lessness puts curtains before him and hide many things from him. But a man has many ill wills and enmities within him. Otherwise, if man is totally clean and cleansed of all bad qualities, he becomes an object of envy for the clean sky. But man is imprisoned within so many rights belonging to him. Therefore, he should try to practise to give up disobediences little by little and seek forgiveness so that he may not suddenly be caught by the police officer of God. Therefore, my dear, put all your efforts to keep yourself clean

chapters.title: Different Interpretations of Words and Events
chapters.subtitle: Sufi’s dragging of his assailant to the Qazi

paras: The Sufi went close to the fellow who hit him and caught hold of his garment and dragged him to the Qazi and asked him to make this inauspicious donkey sit upon on inauspicious donkey or give him lashes as a punishment or in any other way he would be pleased to. Because, if a person dies as a result of your punishment, there is no payment of damages for it and you are totally absolved. A person who dies as a consequence of your punishment gets saved from the punishment of the hell also.”

sections.heading: Judges Protected for Bonafede Wrongs
paras: Because as per law there is no liability upon the judge if a person dies due to the imposition of punishment by him. He is a vicegerent of God and a shadow of the justice of God. He is a mirror of both the plaintiff and the defendant. He imposes punishment for the cruelties perpetrated to protect the interest s of the oppressed, and not for his own gains, out of anger or for his own personal satisfaction. The final justice is however by God on the doomsday. As such, if there is a unintended mistake on the part of the judge, there is a no personal liability upon him to pay damages to the heirs of the deceased by the murderer or hiss male successors. But in the case of the Qazi, it has to be paid by the treasury as he has acted as a representative of God. You may turn to pages relating to the rules of the treasury to know more in this regard. One who kills for his own sake is liable and one who kills for God is protected.

sections.heading: Some Rules on Blood Money
paras: A father may beat his son for disobedience and the dies. In such a case the father has to pay the blood money to his son’s heirs, because the father has killed him for disobedience for his own sake as there is a duty upon the son to serve his father. However, when a teacher beats the student and he dies, there is no liability on the teacher. This protection to him is to maintain his dignity and teaching as controlling and chastising is a part of his duty. A teacher is like the patron and trustee for the student, with a quasi-parental authority. All those with such states of frustrating are covered by the same legal provision. There is no legal duty cast upon the student to render service to the teacher, as against a son who has a duty to render service to the father. Thus, there is no liability on the teacher as he beats the student only in the student’s interest as against a father who beats the son for non-performance of his duty; and therefore, liable to pay blood money. [This is as per the decision of H. Imam Abu Hanifa. However, other authorities do not agree with this and say that there is no liability on the father — Qazi Sajjad Hussain]. Father beats his son for his own sake and therefore, he is liable to pay blood money.

sections.heading: Justice for God’s Sake
paras: Thus, you may see that liability arises in cases of personal interest. Therefore, you may cut off the head of your personal interest with the honourable sword, Zul fiqaar, of H. ‘Ali. Become absolutely selfless as though you are no more alive. When you give your self-interests, whatever you do becomes something like what God does. Whatever you do will be like what does as stated: you did not throw but Allah threw: wa maaramaita iz ramaita wata kinna alldha ramaa. (Anfal: 8: 17). You will remain totally absolved and safe. The liability to pay damages will be upon God and not upon the holder of His trust. You may see the details of this in the books of law and juris prudence.

sections.heading: Look to What You Want, Not Collaterals
paras: Every shop is meant for the sale of a particular commodity and therefore this Math(s)navi is a shop of spiritual commodities obtainable not by paying money but by resorting to faqr (self-imposed destitution and deprivation). If such legal and juristic reference are made, it is only to make you know the differences just as what you see in the leather shop are very nice footwear, but if you see wood, it is a wooden mould of the woot with which you are not concerned. There are silk fabrics in a textile shop and also a measuring steel yardstick, but you go to the shop for the purchase of fabrics and the yardstick. Our Math(s)navi is a shop of oneness and unity of God. And whatever else you see in it is an idol. Appreciating of the idols is for the interest of the common folk. Consider it as the phrase: “tilka gharaniiqul ‘ulaa” “They are the high flying birds ‘saras’ or “exalted females”. [This refers to a statement” tilka qharaaniiqul ‘ulaa wa an shafaa‘atuhunna litartujii: these are exalted females whose intercession is to be sought. This sentence was recited by the Prophet instead of alakuzzakaru wa lahul unthsza (what! For you the males for Him the females. (Walaain: 43: 21). Upon this the infidels present there fell in prostration, as those was a recognition and appreciation of the names of their idols lat, ‘uzzaa and Manaat in the preceeding verses 19 and 20. This isa fabricated story, which is very well explained by Maulvi Muhammad Ali in the exegesis of the Quran in the Holy Quraan, published by ‘Islamic review’ office, oriental Road, woking surrey, England, 1917, in pages 1016, 1017 and 1020 — Translator].

sections.heading: Rumi’s Different Interpretation of Gharaaniqul ‘Utan
paras: Rumi continues: He read this while reciting the surath wa-alnajm in fastness. But his was a trial or expression of amazement and not a part of the surath. Hearing this the infidels became prostrators, not of the idols, but as an impact of the shock of the statement. There is also a secret behind this that when common people hear matters not relating to God’s oneness, but matters of others, they cast their attention on idolatry instantly and later turn around and develop interest to hear about God’s oneness also. Yet taking this incident as true, many other things can be explained but there are many matters in words within words, all twisted within each other, about which it is not reasonable to raise question and try to find answers, which will lead to many more questions and doubts which do not lead anywhere. Therefore, you should go with and give importance to H. Sulaiman and not the devils around him. This is what the researchers on certainties do and avoid the creators of suspicious and doubts.
But stop at this and bring up the narrative of the Sufi and Qazi about the weak and sickly person’s cruelty.

chapters.title: Where Mercy Is Bad
chapters.subtitle: Further narrative of the Qazi and Sufi

sections.heading: Law Not Enforceable upon Dead
paras: The Qazi told the Sufi: “spread out your board and then lay your carvings on it so that I may see the good and bad of them as the saying goes: First spread the board and then make decorations on it. Where is the fellow who beat you and where is the scope for taking revenge on this fellow? The defendant is so sick and weak that he is just like a mental image. Law is enforceable on the living and those with assets. Where is the law for the residents of the graveyards?”
Those people who resorted to self-imposed destitution are more dead in a hundred ways then the really, physically dead.

A dead person is dead in a single way, but the Sufi’s are dead in a single way, but the Sufi’s are dead in a hundred ways. Their death is not a single affair, but they face three hundred thousand killings and for each of these hundred thousand killings and for each of these killings, there are unlimited blood monies. God has killed them many a times and spread-out uncountable lots of blood monies. Just as jarji’s (st. George) got killed and regained life within himself in a hidden way for sixty times. He got killed with the spear full of the taste of death upon the command of the Judge and cried out every time: “give me another injury.” I swear upon God: as against the love for another killing

sections.heading: Dead in Love of God Are Living
paras: The Qazi further said: “I am to issue orders upon the living. I am not the one to issue orders for those buried in the graves. Though this defendant does not appear to be under the grave, but many graves are their in his body. you have seen many dead bodies in the graves, but here you may see a grave in this dead man, if you have the eyes to see! If a brick falls upon you from the grave, you cannot seek justice (damages) from that grave. no wise man will do that. Do not be angry and inimical to a dead person. Be careful not to quarrel with the paintings of the walls of baths.be thankful that a living person did not hit you, as God refuses to entertain one rejected by men. Anger of the living man is the anger of God and also a beating from Him, as God is ever living without any material body and skin. So also, is the case of the devotee of God who lives for Him and with Him as He only is the real living, though he may be physically dead (Baaqi Billah). God killed him and cleansed him of the meanness of man and blew His soul in him, like the butchers who peal out the skin of animals and blow air into it so as to make the flesh remain fresh and fatty for a long time.

sections.heading: God Blew Soul into Man
paras: The blowing of His soul done by God remains with this dead man till the doom’s day. His blowing of the soul is not like the blowing of air by the butchers. There is a great difference between these blowing’s. One is good in entirety and the other is vicious. The butcher takes away the life and this is a bad act, but God gives life which is everlasting. God’s blowing of soul is not that can be explained in words but to the tasted and experienced. Do not try to go deep into it like going into the depth of the well. Come up high above the fort wall from the deep well of the world. “Making this defendant sit upon the donkey is not a wise and rational act. Firewood can be kept on the back of a donkey but not the painting of fire and fuel. Donkey’s back is not a proper place for him to sit. Top of the coffin is more suitable for him to sit. Consider as to what is his cruelty. Cruelty is placing something in place not suitable for it. Be careful not to seat him in an unsuitable place and cause his destruction.”

The Sufi said: “Do you think that his giving me a blow is justified for these reasons and even for that he should not be punished and made to pay damages? How can it be justifiable that every dishonourable bear should slap up on the sufis and go completely free without any harm?”

The Qazi said: “what care can a Sufi have for a slap on his face. Forget it, and do not quarrel with a sick person.” Then, he asked the defendant: how much money, less or more, od you have with you.” he replied: “I have six dirhams only as the possession of the world.”

Then the Qazi told him: “keep three dirhams for yourself and give the other three dirhams to the Sufi and do not plead anything anymore. You are sick and weak and a poor beggar. You need three dirhams for your bread.”

After this judgement, the Qazi and the Sufi were engaged in some other talk, but that sick fellow, misguided from the right path, happened to look upon the neck of the Qazi, which appeared to be much better than the Sufi’s. he straightened his hand to give a blow on it thinking that the cost of my earlier blow has been very low and cheap. As though to tell some secret to the Qazi, he went nearer to his ear and gave a blow upon the Qazi and said: “O the two opponents of mine! Both of you may take all the six dirhams, with this I shall be completely free, without defects and anxieties of any kind.

chapters.title: Hazards of Justicing
chapters.subtitle: The Qazi’s getting upset with the blow of the sick beggar and the Sufi’s speaking ill of the Qazi

paras: The Qazi was very much upset, and the Sufi said: “certainly your order was based on justice. There is no doubt in it. But my dear master of faith, why did you seek something of another which you did not seek for yourself. You do not know, one who sinks a well for another to tall will at last, fall in it himself. Perhaps you have not heard of the statement. My dear sir, act upon it if you have heard of it. There was such an order in your judgement which resulted in a blow upon your neck. I do not know what results your other judgements would bring upon your head and feet. With your generosity you showed mercy upon a cruel fellow that you provided three dirhams for him. The rule is that the hands of the oppressor should be cut off, but instead of this, you gave power and authority to them. You are unsuitable and ignorant in the matter of justicing like that ewe which milked the baby wolf.

sections.heading: Pains, Sorrows Give Good Results
paras: The qazi said: “We have to be in consonance with the blow and the cruelity that comes to us from the decisions of God. I am quite contented in my heart with the commands given in the books, even though I have a bitter face because truth is always bitter. My heart is like a garden and my eyes are like clouds. Clouds weep but the garden gets pleased and laughs at their weeping. Sun laughs fearlessly in a period of famine, when gardens go into a situation of losing life to death. Thus, you see that weeping is better than laughing. You have heard this statement of God. Let them laugh a little: they will weep much: Falyadh-hakuu qatilan wal yabkuu kath(s)iiran: (Tauba: 9: 82). In such a case why show a laughing face when the head of a slaughtered goat opens and shows its teeth when it is burnt to remove hairs from its face. You will be a cause of brightness for your hours, if you shed tears like the burning candle. Sour face of the parents is a protector of the child from all troubles. O senseless laughter, you have tasted the pleasure of laughing. Now you may taste the desire of crying which is so sweet as a mine of sugar. When the thoughts of about hell make you cry, hell appears to be more pleasurable than paradise. Laughters are hidden in cries just as treasure’s are hidden under ruins. Pleasure is actually in sorrows, but people are not aware of it. This is like the life-giving water hidden in darkness. Paths of life are full of footsteps showing the reverse-going marks just as the thieves wear shoes with buck soles therefore be careful not to be satisfied with only your own two eyes but take other eyes of a friend and make four eyes to find the proper way and read the appreciation of the good ones who have their affairs by mutual consultation: wa amruhum shuurraa bainahum: (Shuuraa: 42: 38). Better consult a friend and do not feel proud of yourself.

sections.heading: Learn from Masters in Silence
paras: A noble friend is a guide of the path; rather he is a path matter. It is a disciple of the company of the masters that you should maintain silence before them, and not make yourself as a prominent gem on the finger-ring. You may see such a situation in the Friday prayer when all assemble and sit in silence with one thought and object. Collect all your affairs on a single point and do not make yourself a point of impatience, when you are in search of the proper point. Hear this from the Prophet’s saying that in the ocean of thoughts, you should search for guidance from friends just as guidance is sought from the stars. He has said: “my companions are like stars, whomsoever of them you follow, you will get guidance.” Cast your eyes on the stars and search for your path (in the darkness of the oceans and deserts). Silent observance, and hearing in silence are the proper ways. Speaking in the company and presence of the Shaik creates confusion and therefore do not talk. Even if you speak of two truthful words, it will lead to a wrongs and confusions that will follow you more effectively.

sections.heading: Mouth Goes of Control While Talking
paras: Have you not heard, o confused one, that talking on different subjects leads to dragging of talks differently by causing confusions. Be careful not to be an initiator of talk even in respectful right matters because words have the tendency to pull more words. The moment you allow your mouth to open, it goes out of your control. Once it goes out of control, it will proceed to make confusing and unpalatable statements just as water comes first then the residue when the cock of the bottle is opened and held upside down. It is only from the greatness of the prophets that only true inspiration come from their mouths, as has been said about the prophet in the Quran: Nor does he talk of his own desire: wa maa yantiqu ‘anil hawaa: wal najm: 53: 3). This is because desires of the self do not arise from those kept pure and clean by God. Make yourself one who expresses himself through actions as against words so that you may not be out-witted by others, as I have been.

chapters.title: Why Disparities in Creations
chapters.subtitle: Sufi’s questioning the Qazi

paras: As the qazi had said that one hould have consoncance upon all actiosn of God, the sufi said to the qazi: “when gold is from the same mine, when one piece of it is a cause of profit and another of loss. When all creations are by the same single hand of God, why one is smart and another dull. When all streams are from the water like honey and another like poison. When the light is from the same sun only why there is a false dawn and a true dawn. When the eyeblack is the same, why it brightens the eyes to see straight and another to see criss-cross. The mint of God is the same, why there is a correct impression on one coin and why a twisted one on another. When God has said that the path of religion is my path, why there are leaders and dacoits in religion. Why from the same person are born a scholar and also a duffer, when it is well known that son is the secret bearer of father. Though there are thousands of creatures from the same One God, why there are lakhs of turmoil’s and lack of peace. Why they all do not see unity in Him. How so many opposing things come about. It is beyond understanding when the maker is well settled

chapters.title: World, Full of Opposites
chapters.subtitle: Qazi’s reply to sufi

sections.heading: Rest of One, Disturbance of Another
paras: The qazi said: O sufi, do not get perturbed. You may hear a detailed narration in this regard. Hear this carefully and understand and see the matter well. If you cannot see, think over it deeply. You may know that the disturbance in the mind of a lovers arises from the sobriety of the beloved. She is well settled like a mountain with her pride and poise, while the lover shivers like a leaf. The laughter’s of the beloved create cries and the charms of her face bring about loss of the honour of the lovers. The what and why of these situations is like the surf that moves atop the unfathomable ocean. The similarity and oppositeness are not in their essence and results. There is no need for any similarity between the beginning and end, and the cause and effect. They need not be similar but should not be opposite. For this reason, all of them are in different forms and dresses. An opposite does not create an opposite and bring it forward but runs away from it and gets out of it.

sections.heading: Similar, Same and Opposite
paras: What is sameness? If is only an example just like an example of good and bad. Sameness does not make another sameness of itself. It can only get an example of itself as something similar to it. Two things cannot be the same and therefore the question of one as the creator and the other as created does not arise. So also, there cannot be a question as to why and which is better than the other. Opposites and similarities are uncountable like the leaves of the trees of the garden. Opposites and similarities are like surf on the flatness of water on the surface of the sea. Consider that the ocean has no question of ‘why’ for its movements and peace. They are not like the checkmates and movements at the hands of the chess player on the chessboard. “why” cannot be a part of the essence of the ocean. So also, in respect of God. This is an example of the state and essence of God. You can only observe. His acts and not His essence. And there is no opposites in God’s essence and in the acts of His creations.

sections.heading: Great or Small; None Can Answer All Question
paras: You and your life are His petty toys which contain your soul. There are no ‘why’ and ‘how’ for them. It is not possible to assess His essence. When you cannot assess your own soul, how can you understand God? He is an ocean to be understood from every drop which come into existence. Our body is visible and destructible, but wisdom and soul are not and are greater than the body. how can the answer to those questions. how and why come into our narrow, petty minds. Even the totality of the lies in accepting lack of knowledge about these questions and at and admitting ignorance. [Even the Prophet said: O God, I cannot make an assessment of your reality as You do upon Your own self: Laa uhisii th(s)anaa’an ‘alaika antu kamaa ath(s)maita ‘alaa nafsika: (Hadith(s)_ — Qazi Sajjad Hussain]. When total wisdom is helpless here; what about ordinary wisdom made of madder. Have you ever, at least smelt of the fragrance of the ocean of creation and return to Him of the world? The body says: “I am certainly a shadow of yours. How can anybody expect any support from the shadow? Wisdom again says: ‘This assessment is not of that state where the capable may feel proud of any consibler to be above the incapable. Both are estranged equally in this place. Even the sun becomes a particle here and renders service to it. Here, the lion is helpless before the deer, the falcon spreads its feathers in helplessness before the partridge.if you do not believe in this, you may think as to why the Prophet said to lay people: ‘Please include my name also in your supplications’.

sections.heading: Learn from the Lowly Too
paras: “You may say that the noble Prophet did not say this to receive benefits from ordinary people as he was very great before them; and he did so only to teach this method to his followers by coming down from his level so that there may be no feeling of high and low among them. Yet this makes it clear that the highly can also seek good things from the lowly and there should be parity between them. This does not mean that the highly cannot get any benefit from the lowly. If he were to mean this; it would amount to keeping the community in ignorance because if nothing can be learnt from the lowly, and the lowly would be deprived of instruction from the highly.” I would not agree with you in this regard in full. This act of the Prophet was to convey that treasure exists in the ruins; and many a times the treasures of the benevolences of God are with such people who appear to be lowly to others. He keeps His unlimited treasures in such people appearing as ruins.

sections.heading: Why Seventy Schisms?
paras: Though every part of one’s wisdom is a spy to see hidden matters, your suspicion along with it is like the reverse markings that the thieves make on their shoe-soles to make the onlookers mistake the forward march as reverse march with this, the truth has vanished from the minds resulting in seventy, rather hundred schisms in the community.

sections.heading: Rewards by God After Troubles
paras: The qazi continued: “I shall tell you about a secret considerable point on: “what you desire”. Keep the ears of your heart open and hear it carefully. Whenever a trouble comes to you from the sky, bear with that and be hopeful of good reward later. You have received a blow and you may wait for something good also, just as a butcher gives the bony flesh of the neck along with the soft flesh of the animal’s thigh. Because God is not that king who would give a blow on you and not grant a kingdom and crown later. The entire wealth of the world is just like a wing of the mosquito for Him and there is an uncountable compensation for it later. You may remove from your neck the golden yoke of this world and prepare yourself to welcome a blow on it from God. This is a blow which all prophets have received, and its pain elevated their heads high above. Therefore, try to keep yourself within yourself under self-control with patience so that He may provide a safe house for your residence. Otherwise, He will take back the reward of the house. He has kept for your finding that there is none to receive it. Keep in the mind of your house.

chapters.title: Why Turmoils and Disturbances?
chapters.subtitle: Further question of the sufi with the qazi

paras: The sufi asked the qazi: what would have happened if this world had always been under the wide cloud of God’s mercy, without bringing turmoil’s and stinging of bites every moment. Night would not have stolen the light of the day’s lamp and autumn did not spoil the comforts and beauty of the gardens. Cup of health would not be in need of a stony burden of medicine to get rid of sickness. peace would not be under the fear of troubles. what reduction would have been there in his grace and mercy if there had been no troubles and anxieties. Everyone would have been happy and comfortable, and the lives of men and jinn would not have been disturbed. There would always have been full affection and taste of life and souls also would have been better with full enthusiasm.”

chapters.title: Turk and Tailor
chapters.subtitle: Qazi’s answer to the question of the sufi and his citation of the example of a Turk and tailor

paras: The qazi said: “O sufi, you have a very dry brain without any sense like the letter kaf(k) which does not have a dot. You have not heard of the treacheries of the tailors that a sweet-tongued person told the other night. He was telling about a lot about the stealing qualities of tailors even from earlier days that, while cutting the fabrics they steel some pieces. He was telling stories upon stories of their stealing qualities and those around him were hearing in full attention

chapters.title: Speech and Attention of Audience
chapters.subtitle: Exegesis of the Prophet’s statement: “God provides points to speak to the speakers as per the capacity of the audience.”

sections.heading: Acceptances Make Things Great
paras: When the audience finds a speech well, the fiery speaker speaks very well: all parts of his body become narrators. If you find someone as a good speaker, you may think that he has good audience. A teacher is very active and enthusiastic when he gets an intelligent student. A sarangi player plays twenty-four tunes but when he does not get lighteners, he becomes like a sarangi himself. Neither he remembers a song nor a sonnet. Even his fingers fail to move on the instrument. Had there been no ears to hear the inspirations from the hidden world, there would not have been any revelations or messages of joy. Had there been no eyes to see the great workings of nature, neither the sky would have rotated, nor the earth smiled at its own beauty. The statement of God: Laow laaka lamaa khalqtul aflaaka, addressing to the prophet that: ‘but for you I would not have created the heavens (Hadith(s)), is also to speak of the point that very deep and piercing eyes are required to observe the heaves.

Common people are interested only in food and sex out of their love for them. They have no interests in the wonderful creativity of God. If there is no dog to lick, you will not put any soup in the earthen bowl. Therefore, you may go and become a dog at God’s bowl like the dog of the companions of cave so that His grandeur may take you away from the tastes of other worldly bowls.

chapters.title: Tongue and Throat Are Enemies
chapters.subtitle: Haughty claim of a Turk that the tailor would not steal anything from him and his making a bet

paras: AS the speaker detailed about the stealing expertise of the tailors, which they secretly do, in the presence of many people the over-confident Turk from the city of Khafa among the audience was very much upset with the curtains lifted by the speaker. The speaker was revealing the secrets for the wise just as the secrets are revealed on the doomsday. It may be known that when secrets are revealed wherever and whenever you go, you will see two enemies doing so — tongue and the throat. You may consider the tongue as the reporter of the doomsday and the throat that speaks of the secrets as the bugle of israfil which put the society in turmoil, because god has created many reasons for anger and thrown out disgraces in the streets. The speaker said a lot about the treacheries of the tailors which made the Turk unhappy, angry and painful.

chapters.title: Smartest Tailor
chapters.subtitle: Turk’s search for the tailor’s house

paras: The Turk asked the narrator: “who is the smartest master tailor in treacheries and tricks in your city.” He was told: “there is a tailor whose name is Porshush. He is like a slaughterer for the people in thieving and cleverness.

The Turk said: “I assure you, even with a hundred efforts, he will not take even a thread from me.” But people told him. Many very much cleverer than you have been out beaten by him. Do not try to boast. Do not be very proud of your wisdom as you are sure to be lost in his tricks. The Turk became more angry saying that he was prepared to make a bet that the tailor would not take anything from him, either old piece or a new one. The instigator further instigated him, and the Turk said: “this is my Arabian horse which is pledged to you which I shall give to you if the tailor steals my fabric from me; if not I shall take another horse from you in the bet.’

Out of his anger, the Turk did not sleep for the whole night, and he fought with the thief in his dream. He took a piece of silk fabric in the morning and went to that tailor shop in the bazaar. The tailor saluted him in great enthusiasm and got up from his place and started talking. The Turk got greater honour than he deserved and put the feelings of love in his heart. Getting highly pleased, with melodious voice, the Turk spread his silk fabric of Istanbul before him and told him to cut the fabric for making a long coat for wearing in the battlefield. The lower part of it should be loose enough and the upper part narrow. The upper part is for beauty and the lower part should not come in the way of his fast walking. The tailor said: “My dear sir, I shall render a hundred services; and kept his hand upon his chest as the token of acceptance. Then he took measurements and opened his lips for talking non-sense relating to the stories of the rich and their gifts and grants; and also of the miserly who reduce in paying even what is due: all this, he said in a funny manner and cited the names and addresses of the people. Then he took his fire-like scissors and started cutting and narrating the stories to make him laugh.

chapters.title: Lost in Jokes
chapters.subtitle: The tailor’s jocular talks making the Turk laugh rendering his eyes shut providing opportunity to steel

paras: The master tailor cut a joke and the Turk got tired of laughing and fell down. When the Turk started laughing, his narrow eyes became all the more narrow upon which the tailor cut a piece of fabric and hid it under his thigh in such a way that it was hidden from everyone except God. God sees everything but He keeps it in hiding but reveals the secret when things go beyond limits. The pleasure of laughing took away the first claim of the turk. What silk fabric, what claim and what pledge? Know that the Turk was inebriated in jokes. Then he started flattering the tailor to say more jokes as they became his food. He said such a laughter -creating-joke that the Turk fell flat on the ground allowing the tailor to cut another piece and tug it in his waist belt, while the inebriated Turk was enjoying the joke. The same type of wrong the Turk committed for the third time and pleaded to him to cut more jokes for God’s sake. He said some greater-laughter-creating joke than the earlier two and the Turk fell fully into his trap. Eyes shut. Wisdom have been lost, the challenging Turk was fully devoted to the jokes and inebriated with laughter. Then the tailor cut a further piece as this laughter provided him with a very large field. When the Turk again pleaded to him for further joke, the tailor felt pity on him and kept his art of cruelty intact for other people. He said to himself: “this mad fellow has fallen in love wit hme being unaware of the losses undergone by him. O victim of imaginary joke, you became a joke yourself. How long do you search for imaginary stories. There is no laughing story better than your own! You stand at the ruined mouth of your own grave.’

chapters.title: Sky Is Also a Joker
chapters.subtitle: Address to everyone who gets trapped in such trials

paras: O the one having entered into the grave of doubts and ignorance, how long do you want to see the tricks and jokers of this master tailor, the sky? How long do you want to swallow the treacheries of the world? Neither your wisdom is on the proper track nor your soul! The joke of this sky had brought an old, bearded fellow along with a youth. It has destroyed the wisdom of lakhs like you. it is a conman tailor for all, that tears and stitches the clothes of a hundred-year-old man as well as of a boy. Elderly men and children sit before it like beggars so that it may make fun of both the good and bad ones. If its jokes have provided freshness to the gardens, during spring, upon the oncoming of autumn all grands are destroyed.

chapters.title: Jokes Result in Sorrows
chapters.subtitle: The tailors telling the Turk to keep quiet as more jokes from him would narrow down his coat

paras: The tailor told the Turk: “leave all these at this. If I cut more jokes, you will be in a sorrowful situation. Then your coat will become very tight. Does anybody put himself to loss like this? Were you to know the secret behind this laughter, you would have considered is as more troublesome than a hundred ones. O inebriated Turk! Give up your laughs, as your life has been lost. If you do not, you will go down very much.” Not only that! O when the tailor lifted his hand from the coat, the inebriated Turk lost even his horse upon which he had made a bet.

After citing this narrative, the qazi continued to speak to the sufi: hear the sum and substance of all this! You are like that foolish Turk; the traitorous world is like that tailor. The silk fabric is for the purpose of goodness and piety with which the coat should have been stitched, but you lost the same in jokes and laughs. Your time is your silk fabric, and the laugh-causing words are passions and desires. Day and night are the pairs of scissors and laughter is wreck lessness. The Turk’s horse is faith, and the devil is waiting to knock it off. Be warned. Take care of yourself and keep yourself away from jokes.

chapters.title: Stars Have No Impacts
chapters.subtitle: To explain that the jobless and story-seekers are like the Turk; the tricky, traitorous world is like the tailor; passions and love of women are like jokes in this world. Our passing life is like the silk fabric before the tailor to make the dress for our life and resorting to piety

paras: The silk fabric of your life is getting cut off by the scissors of passing months. The treacheries tailor making use of the scissors tore out the fabric of your life. You wait upon and desire that your star should always be in cutting jokes, laughter and prosperity. You want to run away from it as you are very much afraid of its troubles, enmity as calamitous behaviour. You feel sorry even upon its silence, ill-effects and constrictions. When Venus and Jupiter are not dancing, and Mars and Saturn are on the declining path, you start thinking as to why Venus is not dancing forgetting that man should not bother to think that stars bring about prosperity and cause calamity; and they themselves are neither calamitous nor prosperous. Your star even tells you that you will be at a loss, if you laugh and be merry just as the Turk. Therefore, do not look at the rotation of these stars but look at the One who causes rotation to your love.

chapters.title: Greed Never Ends
chapters.subtitle: Destitute cite this world as an example that gives peace to them

paras: A person was going toward his shop. He found the way blocked by women. He was in a hurry, and he found his feet burning because of this blockade caused by the crowd of women beautiful like moon. He turned his face toward one of them and said: “O degraded women, in what a large number are you all, young and old.” The women turned her face toward him and said: “You are degraded! Do not consider over large number in this manner. Inspite of our being so spread out upon the land, you are not satisfied with your craze. Because of deficiency in women, you indulge in homosexuality in which both the doer and the done get disgraced in the world”.

So, saying the qazi advised the sufi: “do not cast your eyes upon these incidents of the world which are agreeable to the sky. Do not consider the provisions made by God as deficient and see that inspite of famine, fear and resultant threats you are so desirous of the world. Inspite of these troubles, people do not go away from it but sacrifice their lives for it forgetting the harsh consequences. Consider these troubles as a bitter trial and protect yourself from the torture of the rule of the city of Balkh and Marv.

“Think of the fate of the Jewish Ibrahim of the days of king Bahram Gaur who had become an example of miserliness and meanness and suffered a lot. Consider the other H. Ibrahim, the prophet of God, who ran away from honourable status and went forward in godly pursuits. He was not burnt by fire, which is a great miracle, but the other miserly Jewish Ibrahim got burnt in the fire of hell. The sites of your shoes point toward the opposite direction. You should go in the opposite direction of the thing of desire, when the desire thing itself will come towards you.”

chapters.title: Why Troubles Caused
chapters.subtitle: Sufi’s further questioning

paras: The sufi said: “that Great Helper God is really helpful and has the authority to provide benefits to us without any loss. The one who converts fire into flowers and trees, can also make it harmless. The one, who brings flowers from the deep pits of earth can also make the deep pits into gardens. The one who gives freedom to swing to the cypress can also convert anger into pleasure. One who brings existents from non-existence has every reason to keep existents intact. How can He meet any loss if He does not destroy the thing that He creates and puts life into it? What is there to prevent Him from granting to his creatures without the creatures asking? He can also protect the weak from the domination of devils who are waiting to pounce upon them. And also, from the mischiefs of men’s vicious self and the trails of Satan.”

chapters.title: Pleading Ignorance to Teach Others
chapters.subtitle: Qazi’s reply to the sufi

sections.heading: Why Opposites in the World?
paras: The qazi said: “Had there been no bitterness in affairs, there would not have been good and bad, and difference between a stone and gem. Had there been no commanding self, devil and desires, there would not have been injuries, stylish walks and fights. In such a case with what names could God have called them all, who as good and bad, are all his servants. How would He have called some as patient and contented and dignified, brave and wise. How could there have been the patient, truthful and generous without there being the accursed, dacoits and devilish. Brave men like Rustam and Hamza would have been like the cowards; and learning and wisdom would have become worthless and shattered into bits and be no different from ignorance and misguidance. Saltish stagnant water and fresh water from the fount would have been the same in the shops and there would have been no difference between this world and that world.”

sections.heading: Pleading Ignorance
paras: Then the qazi further said: “I know that you are not unaware of all this. You know very well. Still you ask these questions for the sake of the information of the common unknowing people and to eliminate their doubts. People remain ignorant and suffer in the world because of their lack of interest in knowing things and remaining away from the world. All these troubles are nothing in comparison with the loss of nearness from Gods. This is because: they will pass off from the world after some time but not from that world where they will have to stay for ever. One who knows about his is the real rich man. He knows that the pains, sorrows, cruelties and poverty of the world are a result of the people’s remaining away from the Real Friend; and this remaining away from Him gives greater hardship and pain.

chapters.title: Separation Worse Than Pains
chapters.subtitle: Narrative to say that patience in pains is easier to bear than the patience upon separation from friend

paras: A woman told her husband: “you have completely wrapped up your concern and consideration for me. You do not take care of me properly. How long do you keep me in this wretched condition?”

The husband said: “I work hard to earn money for our expenses as I am helpless, and I struggle a lot for some money. My dear, it is duteous upon me to take care of your food and clothing. These, I am duly taking care of. I am not short in them.”

The women showed her sleeve of her garment. Her garment was of rough cloth and unclean. She said in a rough tone: This rough shirt of mine put’s scratches on my skin. Does anyone provide such a garment to his wife?”

The husband said: “I shall tell you one fact my wife! I am a poor man, and I can provide only this much. This shirt is of rough cloth and hard and unappreciable. Upon this you may think over keenly, whether this is, hard and rough or a divorce from me! This garment is good for you or separation from me.”

sections.heading: God Enquiries of You in Pain
paras: In this manner, my dear friend thinks over while passing remarks upon pains, poverty, sorrows and hard work whether it is better to bear with them or total separation from them. It had also whether these are better than the bitterness of going away from God. If Jihad, and fasting are hard and difficult to, they are better than separation from God. How can there be any pain if that Most Gracious, just puts a question to you as to how you are my dear sick man? It gives great consolation. He does so through these pains themselves. He may not appear to speak to you in this manner as you do not have the wisdom and capacity to hear this question directly from Him. But your own taste of pleasure puts this question upon you. this is because: the voice of consolation that comes from God is beyond your understanding, but you certainly get a peace of mind, if your feel that it is from God.

sections.heading: Beloved Also Think of Lovers
paras: You may consider the beautiful beloveds of this world to understand this point of consolation. They are the physicians of the heart, and they also have concern for the lovers in their hearts. When they can not come to enquire out of fear of the world and sense of modesty, they send a message through ha messenger. And if sending a messenger is also not possible, they do think of the lovers in their hearts. No beloved remains unaware of the situations of the lover. You may yourself think that the beloved may be thinking of you, which thought gives you a solace. (This itself may be taken as a messenger and thought). If you cannot understand the same through the affairs of others. You may read the stories of love and romance.

sections.heading: Parents Remembered in Difficulties
paras: This is all about your remaining away from God. For your whole life, you have not bothered to think about these matters. You are like the Turk who eats half cooked meat. They do not wait for it to be fully cooked. Being half cooked you are unable to develop full taste. Inspite of your seeing the grants and authority of God all through your life, you are in greater forgetfulness than those who have not seen at all. Those who have not seen are totally ignorant, but you are more ignorant than them inspite of seeing. If you had thought over all these matters taking these matters as your teachers and yourself as a disciple, you would not have disputed on these matters, and kept quiet. You could have thought about your own parents to think that they are no more with you, yet they do something for you. and even now you think of them in times of difficulties and get solace by taking their names. So also you could take lesson from the fact that the darkness of night gets lost in the brightness of the day. Everything is not permanent and all though there are changes and alterations.

chapters.title: Ostentation and Hidden Greatness
chapters.subtitle: Example of a gnostic’s question to a priest: you are older than your beard or your beard is older than you?

paras: A gnostic enquired with an elderly priest whether he was older or his beard. The priest said: “I was born earlier, and beard came later. I have seen more of the world without beard.” The gnostic said: “the colour of your beard has changed from black to white though it came later, but your bad nature has not changed a bit. It was born later to you but proceeded much ahead of you, but you are still engaged in enjoying the taste of delicious foods and still possess a brain dried up in their love. You still have the same colour with which you were born but not gone a step ahead. Your curd is still sour in the churning pot not getting separated as butter and buttermilk. You still happen to be in the same state of soft sticky clay in which H. Adam was kept for forty years, even though you have been heated in the potter’s kiln for a long time. You have kept your steps firm in the mud like grass even though you flutter in the air with the air of your greed. You are roaming about in the desert of Tia like the followers of H. Musa since forty years, but still not gone out of Tia with your foolishness. You roam about fast every day from morning till night but find yourself in the same place as at the beginning like the followers of H. Musa.

sections.heading: Body Speaks Like Tongue
paras: Inspite of your roaming about for three hundred years, you are in the same place like the followers of H. Musa with the love of the calf in hearts in which those fellows were caught. So long as the love of the calf remains in your heart, you will not get out of the whirlpool of Tia. You have the love of other unlimited grants and benevolences apart from the love of the calf. You are of the conduct of the ox and therefore good qualities have gone out of you because of the love with calf. You may ask about these matters every part of your body which hare though dumb, still have hundreds of tongues with which they speak out.

sections.heading: Events Pass Off, Products Remain
paras: They are always talking about the grants received from the great provider to the world which are all written down in the pages running on for epochs of the world. You are very much interested only in hearing the stories, which you hear from every particle of your body. right from the moment in which every particle of body came into existence from the world of non-existence (‘adam) they have seen so many occasions of joys and sorrows. This is because: no part can grow without a taste of growth, and it also becomes very weak with every occasion of sorrow. These particles continued to remain intact, but those occasions of joy have gone away. Rather, they did not go away but got hidden in your five senses of hearing, seeing, smelling, tasting and touching) and seven other physical parts (head, chest, back, two hands and two legs). This is like the cotton that grew in summer season. Summer passed off, but cotton continued to remain, but the summer season went out of memory. Or take another example of ice that was formed during winter, which remained before us even after the departure of winter. Ice isa memorial of the troubles of winter and flowers and fruits are the memorial of summer.

sections.heading: Products Talk of Impacts
paras: In similar manner, my dear young man, you may see that every part of your body speaks of a story of the grants it has received, first like a woman who has given birth to twenty children. They are all quite well, keeping written within them stories of the good moments they have seen. A woman does not become pregnant without there being an inebriation of love and pleasure. So also, a garden cannot produce fruits without the impacts of spring season. Pregnant women and the children with them are the witnesses of the love with pleasures. Every tree became pregnant to provide milk to babies, just as Mary became pregnant with the command of the King of the world. Though the heat of fire is not visible in water but hidden within it, lakhs of bubbles forming the surf move about forcefully speaking of heat. Though fierce fire is hidden within water, only surf points out of its impacts with its tens of fingers.

sections.heading: Unspoken Communications
paras: In similar way parts of the body of those who have met with God speak with their unspoken words and states that they are full of and carriers of the qualities of God. They are so much inebriated with the impacts of God’s beauty that their mouths simply gape without telling a single word, and their eyes became blind to the beauties of the world. This situation of speaking and expressing though body language is not from the elemental world and therefore are invisible to the eye and inaudible to the ear. They are born out of the radiance of God upon them and are therefore, colourless and hidden behind the curtain. We have said ‘born’, but in fact, they are not ‘born’. We use this only to stress as a means of expression. Therefore, you may not speak of the states that you attain until a command comes from God. Do not be like the bulbul that sits beside the flower singing songs. The flower full of its youthfulness, enthusiasm and fragrance speaks of tis worth without words. Therefore, you may not act like the bulbul, singing and resort only to hearing. Both words and states are the examples of the situations of meeting with God. They are like the feathers that take you to Him, and they are just and perfect witnesses. Both of them are the accepted subtle, beautiful and pleasing witnesses of the matters of existence and annihilations. This is like the ice that speaks during summer of the affairs of winter and its coolness at every moment. It speaks of the cold winds of the winter, which were then facing very hard days. So also, the fruits of the summer season speak of the pleasures of the pleasant winds of summer during the winter season. They speak of the smiles of the sun of those days and of the meeting and mingling of the brides of gardens.

sections.heading: Pleasures, More Than Sorrows
paras: The state has passed off, but its memories remained with you. you may recall these to your memories or make inquiries with the memorials. If you are smart in finding yourself surrounded by sorrows, you feel desperate. You may ask your sorrows as to why they refused to acknowledge the grants provided by the Grantor of all Grants. Thinking of these grants is important for you. you are most of the time provided with spring and pleasures as otherwise you body would fall down and go deformed like the heap of fallen flowers. Our body is like a heap of flowers and your thinking is like their essence. It is very strange to see rose water becoming a rejector of rose. Even grass is disgusted of the thankless. They are of the nature of monkies. But upon the thankful like the prophets, the sun and clouds sacrifice themselves. Quarrels and rejection are the qualities of monkies. Thankfulness and praising is the path of the prophets. Thankless people, like the monkies get spoiled in this world and that world. They are exposed as such. Thankful people following the conduct of prophets are elevated to higher levels like the pious and worshipping people. Dogs, more so the barking dogs, roam about in the streets full of houses. But the men of honour with the light of wisdom live unknown in ruins and poor localities. Something more than wisdom is required to understand all this. If this kind of light had not remained under eclipse, philosophers and rationalists would not have missed their way. Very keen-observing, wise and intelligent have seen the marks of foolishness clearly on the noses.

chapters.title: Men with Different Qualities and Objects
chapters.subtitle: Story of a poor man who searched for provisions without hard work and efforts

sections.heading: Fine External, Internal Grants
paras: a helpless, poor fellow in pains, who had received thousand of injuries from poverty, used to praise God in his prayers and supplications: “O God and Protector of the flocks, you have brought me into this world without any efforts from my side. You may grant provisions to me, similarly without efforts from my side. You have given me five gems in the jewel box of my five other hidden faculties (memory imagination, intelligence, ratiocination and reflective capacity). Your grants are uncountable and unassessable. I am ashamed of my inability to explain about them. As you are my Creator and You alone do it, You may set right the supply of provisions to me.”

For years together, he went on supplicating like this, and at last, his helplessness succeeded, and his prayer was accepted like that of the fellow who was provided with permissible food without working and putting tiring efforts during the days of H. Dawood, the just, on the lines of God, when an ox fortunately entered into his house. [This narrative is explained in detail the third volume of Math(s)navi]. The man in pains exhibited his miseries and won the game in the field.

sections.heading: Opposites Rule the World
paras: During this long period of praying, many a times he used to get disgusted and lose hope for the non-acceptance and delay in acceptance of this prayer. At this, later on the Generous God used to revive his hope, please him and assure him of acceptance. While putting efforts on this, when he used to get tired and lose hope, he used to hear a voice from God: ‘come over to me. God is the One who elevates high and lowers down. Nothing is possible without those two acts. Look at the lowly state of the earth and the high elevation of sky without those two at different levels, there is no possibility of any motion. This earth also has another type of lowly and elevated state. For half the year, it is barren and for the other half it is fresh and green. Look at the times full of lowly difficulties and high prosperities. There is another oppositeness of time; that half of it is day and the other half is night. This combination of high and low provides health and prosperity at times and diseases at others. All affairs of the world may be considered as such like famine and prosperity, war and peace and trials and mischiefs. This world flies upon these two feathers in the air and upon the wo only life exists in fear and hope, so that the world may at time shiver like a leaf in the winds from the cool winds of left side and hot winds of the right side; and life and death.’
World of colours and colourlessness

All these opposites are created in this world so that the pot of uniformity of Jesus in a single colour may make the pot of this world with a hundred colours appear cheap. Because that world is like the mine of common salt and whatever that falls into it becomes like salt. Look at the mud of the grave. persons of all colours become one coloured in the grave. this is about the physical salt mine of the world for the apparent bodies. But there is a different kind of salt mine for the invisible, non-material things. It isa hidden mine which is fresh from the beginning to end. Its freshness is the opposite of the staleness of the other. Its freshness has no oppositeness, and no opponent and enemy. This is like the light of Prophet Muhammad with the sharpness of which lakhs of darknesses became bright. Jews, idolators, Christians and magicians all got a single colour of boldness through his light.

Lakhs of long and short shadows became one with the teachings of this bright sun. there was no shortness, length or expansion. All kinds of shadows got merged into this sun. yet the singleness of colour that comes about on the doomsday is clear before all the good and bad ones as all hidden things become apparent in that world. Our forms assume shapes as per our conduct. At that time our thoughts assume the shape of written words and the lower side of the blanket becomes the upper side.

sections.heading: Things Different in This World
paras: Secrets in this world are like the multicoloured ox. Spinning wheel of the faith produces threads of a hundred colours. This is a time of hundred hearts and hundred colours. There is no hope of a world of single colour here. When the black Abyssinian comes forward the white Roman goes back, and this is a night in which the sun is imprisoned. The ugly wolf is dominant, and the handsome Yusuf is in the depth of the well. The Copts are the dominant people and pharaoh is the king, so that provisions and senseless laughter may go into the share of barking dogs for some days without obstacles. the lions are in the wait in dens so as to hear the command of ‘come on, forward’.

sections.heading: End of Vices and Consequences
paras: Then the lions will come forward in the open fields and God will clearly settle the accounts of profits and losses with all clarity. Then the truth will dominate over untruth and over the oceans and lands. Multicoloured ox will be sacrificed on that day. Doomsday is a day of mass sacrifices. It is a day of feasting for the faithful and of slaughter for the oxen. All water birds will float on that day like the ships on the ocean. Those to be killed will be killed upon the evidence of the witnesses and those to be delivered are those, who had certainty of the occurrence of that day. The falcons will fly toward the king and the crows will go toward the graveyards, as bones and components of dung are the food of crows in the world.

sections.heading: Inner Qualities Decide Good and Bad
paras: Where is the sugar of wisdom and where is the crow? Where is the dung-worm and where is the garden. the soul of a vicious hearted man is not fit for Jihad. So also, oloewood, musk and the back of the donkey have no connection of any kind. Women do not have a duty to fight in the field of jihad against enemies. This jihad with physical efforts and bravery and strength is a minor jihad. How can women and the cowards play a role in the major jihad which is against their own vicious self. A woman becoming brave is rare and possible when a brave man is hidden in her to be born. This is very strange and rare excepting as in the case of Mary, who had a brave child in her like Jesus. Similarly, there are women hidden within men and they become weak-hearted. They will appear like women in that world, who did not see manliness within themselves. Doomsday is a day of justice, and justice and grant is proper when the head wears the cap and the feet wear the shoes. So that everything may meet its object and everything that has to set in the west may set (like the sun). every object will go to its seeker. This is like heat coupled with the sun and water as the companion cloud.

This world itself is a torture chamber of its Maker. You can see His wrath if you torture and oppress others. Look at the hairs and bones of the victims of God’s wrath. His sword has shattered and spread them all over the land and oceans. Look at the wings and feathers of the birds that are spread over in the net which are explaining about the wrath of God without the aid of words, such a wrathful person dies and leaves behind a heap of mud in the form of grave, which also vanishes with the passage of time.
Different object of the different people

God’s justice brings together everything — friend and mate. Elephant goes with elephant and the mosquito with mosquito. The companions of the noble Prophet were four friends (Abu Bakr, Umar, Uth(s)man and ‘Ali) are with him. And the companions of Abu Jahl, with Abu Jahl, with him (‘Utaba, a great Makkan leader of the infidels who was killed by H. Hamza in the battle of Badr and Zulkhi mar, a magician who was called as such as he used to cover up his face wit ha veil). The object of destruction of Jibra‘iil is sidratal Muntihaa, the farthest Lote tree, at which the knowledge of all creatures ends. The final destination of those desires of eating in the dining sheet. The object of the gnostics and searching of God is the receipt of the light of God, and the final end of the philosopher’s rests at their wisdom. The object of reaching of the pious worshipper is the God of all goodness, and that of a greedy fellow is a purse full of gold. The object of the noble people is good acts and of the worthless is lowly ignorance. That of those in search of the hidden life is patience and peace and of those addicted to apparent shapes is the markings made on stone. The object of those sitting in isolation is God, the door of all good, and that of the worshipper of beautiful faces is women. The object of the lover of God is God alone and that of Iblis is illegalities. Pharoah’s object entirely related to the Nile and of the owner of the donkey is donkey’s tail.

In similar manner, you may consider the fresh and old. But if you do not want to think over, you may go away and attend to the job of your taste. Our food is a tasty drink in a goldcup and that of the dogs is porridge in an earthen bowl. God says: we have given that to everyone who was fit for it and provided to him the requirements that were essential for him. We made one a lover of bread and made another disgusted of worldly pleasures. We intoxicated him with the love of their beloveds. When you are happy with your conduct which has its own results why should you run away from tis bad results. If you have taste for femineity, you may take up the veil and covering sheet; and if you find bravery to be worthy, you may take up the sword. If you find fighting to be pleasing, you may wear the coat of mail; and if you are inclined toward homosexuality, you may become an object of it by offering your backside.
There is no end to this discussion. Think of that poor man who because of deprivation found himself injured.

chapters.title: God Answers to Prayers
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the guide-note to a treasure in which a dome was identified and ordered to go and shoot an arrow in the direction of Ka’aba: there is a treasure hidden in the place where the arrow falls

sections.heading: Day Dreaming: Waqi‘a
paras: A hidden voice said to that poor man in his dream. It was not actually a dream. It was some strange situation that occurs to the sufis when they are something as though in a dream, when actually they are not sleep. It is situation between waking state and sleep and is called waqi‘a in sufis jargons. The voice said: O the one having undergone many hardships! Search for a paper from an old paper merchant in your neighbourhood, used as an exercise book. This paper has such and such colour and shape. Read this paper secretly. After taking this paper from the old paper merchant, you may silently go away from the people around. Be warned to read it alone and do not allow anyone to participate in reading. With all these efforts, if this matter becomes known to others, you may not feel sorry as what is provided to you will not go to anyone else even to an extent of half a grain. And if there happens to be any delay in this regard, you may not grieve; and be reciting Despair not of the mercy of God: Laa faqnatu min rahmtillaah. (zumar: 39: 53).

sections.heading: God’s Responses to His Searchers
paras: So, saying the announcer of this happy news, and put your efforts. When that poor man got into his normal consciousness, he felt so elated as not to be confined in the expanse of the world. Due to his excessive pleasure, his liner would have burnt, if God had not shown His mercy, benevolence and protection. The cause of his joy were many. One was that God heard and answered from behind seven hundred curtains. He got highly elevated, even higher above the sky because of the sharpness of his audition faculty, which pierced through the curtains.

When a searcher of God finds the seeing capacity of his eyes piercing through the curtains to attain honourable state and his other senses pass. Though the curtain, he receives continuing sightings and address one after another, which result in getting Informations directly from God.

Then the black army of the body gets defeated and dominated by the white army of the soul, the sun flashes its sword of light upon the darkness of ignorance and slashes upon all darkness of the searcher and severs all his worldly connections annihilating him in God. He then lives in God, and with God and receives the benefits of godly knowledge.

The other cause pleasure for that poor man was that there was no poverty for him anymore. He was sure to get that special treasure. He had another cause that his supplication has not been rejected and though late, it has been accepted by God.

Then he came to the shop of the old paper dealer and searched for papers of the exercise books here and there. Soon he found the specified paper before him, he held it in his armpit and said good-bye and blessings to the dealer, further telling that he would come back.

sections.heading: Knowledge Receivable from God
paras: He sat down in loneliness, read it and was amazed and estranged to see how such a precious guide to treasure was held in the exercise notebook. Then it struck his mind that God is the protector and guard of everything. A guard can never allow anyone to simply take away the things kept under his protection.
