Forests may be full of gold and materials, yet nobody can take away even a grain of millet without God’s permission. You may read a hundred books without interruption but cannot remember even a single point from them without His authority. But if you remain devoted to Him even without reading a single book, you can receive knowledge full of wonders straight from His pocket of knowledge. From his pocket, H. Musa got a bright hand, brighter than the moon, high aloft in the sky. This also indicated that man’s intellectual strength being a part of the total wisdom of God has the capacity to conquer heavens. So that you may know that what you search in the mighty heavens, is to be found in the packet of H. Musa. so that you may also know that the high aloft heavens are only a reflection of man’s knowledge. Do you not know that, well before the creation of all the things, God had created man’s wisdom as said by the noble Prophet: what God created first was wisdom: Awwala maa khalaqallaahul ‘aaql. (Hadith(s)). All this is very clear but hidden from many as a fly cannot be a secret bearer of the large sized anqa.

chapters.title: Vain Efforts
chapters.subtitle: Continuation of the narrative of that poor man and the place of the location of the treasure

paras: It was written on the paper that out of the city there is buried a treasure. Go toward the dome which has a grave inside, on the back of which is the city and, on its front, a large tract of forest. Turn your back toward it and face toward qibla (direction of Ka’aba of Makka) and shoot an arrow. Dig up the place at which the arrow falls. The poor man brought a big hard bow and shot an arrow toward the open land bordering the forest. With great joy he carried a pickaxe and shovel and dug up the spot where the arrow fell. He got tired and so also his implements ‘but found no traces of the treasure. The next day also he did the same but found no trace of the treasure. He went on repeating the same thing every day but did not find the place of hidden treasure. As this had become a clarity affair for him, people of the city started talking about this.

chapters.title: King Comes to Know
chapters.subtitle: Flashing of the news of the treasure and its reaching the king’s ears

paras: Everyone started talking about this, as such a type of game is not played by anyone. Everyone was talking nonsense and everywhere jealousy arose against him. The king was informed of this matter that he has found out a treasure in that place. They also revealed in secret that there was treasure guide with him. Upon coming to know of all this, the poor man found no other way than to go to king himself and submit to his wish and obedience to it, well before any trouble was created by the king for him. He took that paper and placed it before the king further telling, not a bit of treasure was found though he had wriggled very much like the snake. He has been engaged in this work since a month and any profit and loss was prohibited upon him. There would be a possibility that king’s good luck might lift the curtain from it, as he was a victor in battles, and opener of the gates of forts.

The king also tried for it for six months, by shooting arrows and digging the spot. He called for very smart bowmen, made them shoot arrows and searched for the treasure. Nothing was available excepting anxieties, failures and non-sensical talk. They got a name like that of the legendary bird ‘Anqaa, but not its qualities [‘Anqaa is a legendry bird with long neck which used to swallow large-sized animals and men. It had four legs mouth resembling human mouth with different colours. It had become a cause of great misery and was finally thrown into an island by God upon a curse of Hanzha b. Safawan, a prophet of those days. It is also called as Mughrib, meaning hidden and extinct — Translator].

chapters.title: King Lost All Hopes
chapters.subtitle: The king’s losing hopes of getting that treasure and feeling regret and discarding further efforts

paras: As there were hindrances in the length and breath of the region, the king got disgusted of the search for treasure with much regret. There were wells and wells dug up at every yard’s distance but no traces of treasure but only fanfare and laughter. He called that poor man in troubles and threw that paper before him with contempt and said: “take back this paper. It leads to nowhere. You alone are fit to make use of it as you have no other job. This is of no use for those who have their own jobs. They do not move around the thorns if the flowers are burnt out. There are few such madmen, who wait upon for the growth of grass from iron. Very hard-hearted people like you are required for this work and as you are very hard-hearted you may go on searching. If you do not get the treasure, you will not feel sorry for it; and if you get it, I shall make it lawful for you to possess.”

sections.heading: Love Is Selfless
paras: Wisdom does not run on the path of hopelessness. It is only love that runs on it in madness. Love has no concern for results and only wisdom follows the path that provides gains. Love is ruinous, body-melting and shameless. It is like the lower slab of the grindstone which undergoes all troubles. so stubborn it is that it never turns its back. It destroys all feelings of attaining of objects within itself. It maintains utmost sincerity and never thinks of any reward, which it gets only from God. God grants it without any exceptions from His own side and also takes it back from it without any reasons. Manliness and large heartedness is in giving without any expectations. Cleanliness of heart is not the quality of the showy ostentation’s fellows in the comminates. Such people search for reward and deliverance from harm while performing their worship and good deeds. selfies, clean-hearted, sincere people sacrifice themselves for God. They neither try to test God nor they tap the doors of profits and losses.

chapters.title: King Got Disgusted: Conflict Between Worthy and Unworthy
chapters.subtitle: The king’s losing all hopes and returning of the guide paper to the poor man saying we are disgusted of the matter

paras: The king got disgusted of that trouble of the guide-map and returned it to the poor man. King had incurred heavy expenditure and received ridiculous comments of the enemies and he got rid of the same. The poor man left and got involved in his own enthusiasm to pursue him madness.

sections.heading: Love Madness of Love
paras: He made love, full of pains, as his sole friend and sought his own treatment for his madness just as a dog licks its own wounds as a medical treatment. Love has no friends in its twists and turns, and nobody is its friend in the town. Nobody is as mad as a lover and his wisdom is blind and deaf. Because love is not an ordinary madness like other sicknesses. The science of medicine has no medicine to treat a lover. Even if a physician falls in love, he will wipe off all the pages of the medical books with the blood of his tears. All medical formulae are useless before it and the beautiful faces of all other beloveds are hidden from the lover’s eyes. Therefore, O lover, you should turn your face and hopes only towards yourself. Know this well that nobody is with you in your troubles except your own self.

The poor man addressed his own heart. Saying: man can have nothing but what he strives for: Laisa lil insaana illaa masa‘a: (Najm: 53: 39). Earlier, also he had not heard an answer to his prayer, even though he was doing it for so many years. Yet he stuck on to prayers and used to hear: ‘yes, I attend to it in a secret manner, as an inclination toward prayer itself is an answer to it. Earlier he had no response at all. The only hope was an answer to it from the great provider. At that time, there was no hidden announcer a messenger. Only the ear of his hope was attentive to hear a response: yes, only the ear of his hope. Speechless hope only used to tell him to come forward which used to wipe off the feeling of despair from the heart. His soul was like the pigeon trained to sit upon the roof which requires no calling. There is no need to chase it away also, as it is totally committed to remain at the roof as though it has its feathers tied to it. People of commitment are such that they will not go away even if you chase them out with free.

sections.heading: Address to Ziaul Huq
paras: O ziaul Huq, if you want to confirm this, you may chase the pigeons out and see for yourself. If you have a valid reason to chase them away, and you do that, they may leave the roof, but start hovering about it.

Your roof is the only place to pick up grains and the place to settle upon for the pigeon. Though it flies high in the sky with all freedom, it is caught in the net of your love. So also, if by chance, your soul stealthily deviates from your love and becomes, ungrateful to your excessive grace for deviation keeps a bowl full of fire on its chest telling to come back to the moon like beloved and clean itself of dust. This police officer of love is nothing but love itself which is so forceful. It tells it that the king of your love has called you back directing it to go back and bring you back. I am also like a pigeon on God’s roof and my pigeonhole and flight are in full inebriation being unaware of all other things.

“I am Jibra‘iil of love and the highest point to reach for me, like Jibr‘iil sitratal muntahaa is you alone. I am sick and you are my Jesus Christ to treat my sickness. the sickness of my love full of pearls like the sea, needs a great turmoil, and you may come forward to enquire fully about my sickness and provide treatment. When you come over to the sea of my love sickness, my sea will become entirely yours, all in all, as your own property. My love sickness has already become your sickness, this I have to tell only to eliminate. Your doubt and hesitation. All these pleadings and submissions that I make are your grants only. I have expressed only a little of them and the larger that remains hidden within me, has to be taken care of by God alone.

sections.heading: Cries and Lamentations of Lovers
paras: Lovers have two mouths like the flute, one of which is hidden in the mouth which cries and the other one is toward you which laments. These two mouths have created a turmoil in the surrounding. But every sensible man knows that both these sounds are towards each other. The turmoil’s in the flute caused by my breaths are due to the cries, sighs, lamentations and turmoil’s of the soul itself. If the flute had not met with the lips, it would not have produced sweet, sugary tunes for the world to bear with whom, O Hisamuddin, did you spend the night and from what side you got up in the morning that you are so enthusiastic in your behaviour like the stormy river. Were you in the situation about which the Prophet said: I spend my night with my lord. He feeds me and provides drinks abiitu ‘inda rabbi fayut ‘imunii wa yusqiinii: (Hadith(s)). You have thrown yourself in the middle of the river of fire. Inspite of this, you have come out of this fire as happened to it. Ibrahim, when the command was issued to fire to go cold: yaa naaru kuunii bardan: (Anbiyaa’: 21: 69).

sections.heading: Secrets Cause Unbearable Pain
paras: This command became your protector also. O Ziaul Huq! You are the sword of faith and heart. Many jealous of you say this and that about you, but all that is mud, and mud try their best to hide your sun like face, but it is of no use. But those with ruby like large and strong hearts are your beneficiaries and they pass on their benefits to others like your agents, which make even the gardens rich with smiles. Where is that strong man to take all your secrets. However, i can speak a little of the size of a maize out of the hundreds of heaps, to one who has the capacity to hear. But finding no one, I take a long sigh to relieve myself of the burden, just as it is reported about H. ‘Ali, that he used to put his mouth into the mouth of the well and take a long sigh. Bearing the burden of these spiritual secret information in very difficult without sharing with others. As the hearts of his brothers were full of ill will the depth of the well was the safe place for Yusuf. But my situation is so hard that I cannot bear with the intoxication of these Informations and therefore I shall throw myself into these troubles and turmoil, come what may. What is a small safe place like the bottom of the well? I shall pitch my tent in an open desert without carrying for consequences an open desert without carrying for consequences.

sections.heading: Cases of Forgetfulness
paras: When these are my situations, you may keep very hot, highly-intoxicating-wine on my palm and then you may see the grandeur of my state of intoxication. Tell to that poor man searching for the treasure to wait and continue his affairs and efforts, as we are not in a position to narrate them as we are totally sunk in the wine of sighting of God. Tell him to seek the support and protection of God and not from one totally sunk like me. Because I do not need that guide-map to treasure as I am so forgetful that I cannot remember myself and my beard. This is a wine which is so clean and pure that it reveals even a hair lain in it. There is no scope for one to remember oneself in it. One would lose all sese of self-existence seeing neither his face nor even his moustaches which represent causes of one’s honour and pride.

sections.heading: Distinguished by Playing with Beard
paras: O my cupbearer! Give me a large strong dose and relieve this elderly man of the thoughts of his own pride and of his playing with his own beard and mustacheos. Eliminate his sense of superiority from his mind. He pleads of his superiority and disinterestedness towards others by playing with his beard to show that he has no concern for others and ot hear their words. Discard him in total with all contempt as we are fully aware of his treacherous designs. If you have contempt for the poor fellows like us who have deliberately discarded the world, you may also do the same, as we are not concerned with you, also. One may not be aware of the consequences of one’s designs, but the masters see very clearly what is to come after a century in a threadbare manner. What others see in the mirror is seen by them upon the unbaked brick. What an old man with a long beard cannot see in his own house is seen by a young beardless boy in all detail.

sections.heading: Comparison of Uncomparable God
paras: Go and fall into the river of love if you are so proud of yourself as you are of little work like a fish. Man’s greatness lies in humility, which you have given up. Why are you sticking to the beard which is like a scrap of grass. You should know that you are not a scrap. You have such great qualities of which the pearls and gems feel jealous. Your place is more worthy upon the waves of the oceans but in depths. The oneness of God has to be seen not in terms of numbers like one and two. Its pearls and its fishes are not separate from it. They are like His waves only. But they are of no worth at all. His pearls and fishes are His angels and humans close by to Him. Making something as His partner or participant in Him is an impossibility upon impossibility. Even a comparison of Him with the ocean and its possessions is far far away from Him. There is no partnership in this ocean and no twists and turns. It is quite clear and absolute. But I cannot speak of it to the double-seeing people who see two things of one, because of their own defects. As we are with idol-worshippers who are squints, we are compelled to speak in terms of comparisons. That essence which is beyond definition and comparison cannot be understood other than through bringing something to compare and deny the comparison while explaining in words. Either you may swallow this kind of supportive identification like the squints or shut your mouth and remain contented with silence. As you are with midst of idol worshippers you have to speak in comparison. You may explain these facts if you get a person of insight by making indirect references, again and again or by silence or by clear talk, depending upon his state or making a loud announcement in a double-seeing manner. Goody bye.

sections.heading: Troubles Are Great Teachers
paras: If you see one who is able to share your secrets, you may speak to him just as a bulbul sings before the flower. If you see a goatskin like hollow person full of tricks with worldly gains in view, keep your mouth shut and make yourself like a sealed earthen pot. Do not shake yourself before that hollow fellow as he is an enemy of water (of truth), as otherwise the stone of ignorance will break your earthen pot. Have patience upon the tortures that the ignorant fellow gives even without your telling anything to him and treat him well with the special wisdom that God has given to you from His own side. Patience upon the pains given by the ignorant provides more clarity and light to your heart as patience has a cleansing quality. Nimrod’s fire provided greater light and reflective capacity to the heart of H. Ibrahim. Troubles given by the idolators and rejectors of the days of Noah to H. Noah’s patience became the polish to brighten the mirror of H. Noah’s heart.

chapters.title: Worthless Have No Worth for Worthy
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the disciple of Shaik Abul Hasan Kharraqaani, may his secrets be clean

paras: A darvesh left from the city of Taliqan to meet Abul Hasan at Kharraqaan upon hearing a lot about his virtues. He crossed many mountains and large valleys, with all sincerity and devotion to see the shaikh. The troubles and cruelties he saw on the way are worth mentioning but I skip them all.

When that young man come to his destination, he found out the address of the residence of the shaikh. With all due respect he shook the chain of the door, and a woman pushed her head outside and asked him as to what he wanted. He said: “I have come to see the honourable sir.” The woman made loud laughter and said: “Look at your beard. You are old enough to be wise. And also look at the troubles taken by you on your journey! Did you not have any work to do in your own place that unnecessarily you came over to this place? Either you had a foolish desire to roam about or you suffered a lot in your own place, which compelled you to leave it. Or the devil kept two-pronged stick on your neck and pushed you on the insinuation of a march on journey.” She said many other such unsuitable, observe and silly things all of which I cannot speak out. With these unlimited funny similarities, the young man fell into the pit of sorrows.

chapters.title: Misconceptions About Sufis
chapters.subtitle: The visitor’s seeking to know the whereabouts of the shaikh to search for him from his wife and giving of unsuitable answers by her

paras: Tears rolled down from the visitor’s eyes. Yet he asked her as to where that sweet, tongued king was to be found?

She said: “Better it is, if you do not see, and go back safely without seeing that treacherous, ostentations, empty-headed net of the fools and a victim of misguidance. Lakhs of fools like you have become rebellious and disobedient because of him. It would be better if you do not fall into misguidance because of him. He is egomaniac, greedy and excessive eater. The sound of his drum has reached all around and in other places. His admirers belong to the community of the worshippers of calf, who rub their hands on such a bullock like him. One who gets impressed by this excessive eater is a foul-smelling corpse at night and a bluffer during the day. Not only he, all those who belong to the community of sufis, have given up all acquired knowledge and hundreds of academic achievements, and resorted to treachery and falsities. What a tragedy! Where are the followers of H. Musa, who could slaughter the worshippers of the calves? Where are those who follow the path shown by the Prophet and his companions? Where are the five-time worshippers, praisers of God with good morals of the Prophet? These fellows have thrown the laws and rules of piety behind their backs! Where is H. ‘Umar the strict enforcer of the command of ‘do good’, who is the need of the day? These fellows have validated illegalities in such a manner to such an extent that everyone deprived of wisdom, and the vagabonds find themselves free to do whatever they want.

chapters.title: Other Side of the Coin
chapters.subtitle: The disciple’s reply and scolding of the contemptuous woman upon her apostatic nonsense The visitor’s return from the shaikhs house and enquiring with the people about the shaikh’s address and their pointing towards a forest

paras: The young man shouted at her: “enough! NO more! From where has the police officer come to check on a bright day? You are talking ill of the great souls whose light has surrounded the east and west. Heavens, getting amazed at them have fallen in prostration before them. The light of truth das dawned upon the terraces and the sun felt ashamed and went behind the veils. How can the blabberings of devils like you keep me away from the dust of his house. I have not come here like the cloud upon the pushings of the winds that I would go back from him upon the blow of another wind. You call his disciples as the worshippers of calf. But his light is so generous that if it falls upon the calf, even the calf will become a centre of worship like the Qibla (Ka‘aba). And event the qibla without that light will become an idol and centre of idol-worship. This is for the reason that the light that the shaik has is the light of God.

sections.heading: Validation of Prohibited
paras: “Validation of the prohibited things that comes out of the vicious desires of the self is certainly misguidance, but the one that comes through the light of God is perfectionist. [This validation is of two types. One that comes from the misinterpretation the law by the dialecticians. This is due to the desires of the vicious self. This is certainly misguidance. But there is another validation that comes to sufi’s under the impacts of spiritual states, as for example, that occurs in a state of ecstasy of the clean hearted upon hearing music — Qazi Sajjad Hussain. For details, read Imam Ghazali’s treatise on music, translated and published as ‘Rules and Discipline of Music and Ecstasy’ by the translator, by Alghazali in state, Bangalore” — Translator].

This is what happened when with this unlimited light, idolatry became Islam and even Satan became a muslim as stated by the noble Prophet: “as everyone has, there is a Satan with me too. God helped me against him, and he has become a muslim, and obeys me.”

It is because of the light of God that those receiving it becomes the exponents of the love of God and also become His beloveds and cherubs, and the closely angels to go. Angels were directed to prostrate to Adam because his having gone above them with this light of God. This is similar to the prostration that the rind of fruit does to the pulp.”

sections.heading: Lamp of God Cannot Be Blown Off
paras: The disciple continued: “O old woman! You want to blow off the lamp of God with a puff of your mouth. Be warned, foul mouth, your head and your body will burn out with this lamp. A dog’s barking and licking of water cannot pollute the river. The sun cannot become dark and fall down, with your puffs. Instead of going deep into his great qualities, even if you go by his appearance, you can also see his apparent light, which his also so bright. The apparent noble acts of all the people are of no worth before him, but ar at het last point of deficiency. One cannot blow off the lamp of God with a puff and if he tries to do so, his own mouth will be burnt. Many bats like you see many dreams that the world should be orphaned of the sun’s light.

“Waves of the soul are faster and larger by a hundred times of the waves of the Noah’s deluge. But his son, Kan’aan had a hair growth in the eyes. He ignored the Ark and jumped upon the hill. The water of half of the wave swept off both him and the hill and threw them both into the pit of disgrace. The moon shines bright and the dog barks at it, as it cannot receive any benefit from moon light. Those on the journey march fast in the light without caring from the dogs barking. Parts fly fast toward the whole like arrows and for the sake of a hag like you. they do not stay put.

sections.heading: Piety: Demonstrative Command Good
paras: One how has understood God is the life and soul of the apparent laws as well as acts of piety. Understanding of God is a product of piety and comes after it. Piety is like agriculture and understanding of God is like growth of the plants and harvest. Faith and efforts in the pursuits of God are like the body; the object of both is to sow and reap the crop. They are both practical issuers of the command to do good and also the object of doing good. If you say that a H. Umar is required to issue the command for good acts, you may see that the shaikh is all in all good and a practical announcer of ‘command good’. He is a revealer of secret as well the secret itself. He is perfect in both inner and outer qualities. He is a king and commander for us today in this world, and also a commander tomorrow in that world. He is like the pulp, and we are like the rind; and where are the slaves of the pulp. With all these qualifications, if the shaikh says Anal Haq, (I am the truth), all fellows, blind at heart feel agitated and the shaikh simply passes off. The anger of the seers of the apparent words considers him to be a violator of the law and go after him. Their anger in this regard is justifiable, dependent upon apparent law. You may think that when the God’s servant loses himself in full in God, he is lost in toto and nothing of him remains. What remains left out of him, when he is nowhere? You may think over this!

“Look at these things and consider the facts well if you have the eyes. Think over as to what is left out after the stage of nothingness (Laa). Old woman may your lips, mouth and throat rupture. You are like one who spits above upon the moon. Certainly, your spittle will return and fall on your own face. Your spittle will return and fall on your own face. Your spittle cannot reach up to the sky. Spittle will fall upon you from God till the doomsday just as it is falling upon the soul of Abu lahab. Drum and flag are the exclusive possessions of the king and the dog’s share in it is only to run away from its sound in fear. Heavens are the slaves of the shaikh; both east and the west are the beggars of his bread. The honour of Laow laaka that was given by God to H. Muhammad is impregnated upon the top of the impeachment orders issued by the shaikh. [Loaw laaka represents the short form of the statement of God given to Prophet Muhammad Laow laaka lamaa khalqtul afleak (were you not to be, I would not have created the heavens. That is; it is for you that I created the universe. The universe is meant for you to observe — Translator]. All grants and graces meant for the Prophet are from the shaikh now. Had the shaikh not been there the sky would not have had its movements, and a repository of God’s light and home of the angels. There would have been no oceans and no shapes and designs of the fishes and brilliance of royal gems. There would not have been the earth with its treasures within and the fragrant jasmine upon it. Even food is an eater of food from him, and fruits are in thirst for the rains felled by him.

sections.heading: Piety: Demonstrative Command Good
paras: Yet, it is a strange instruction from God that these destitutes (sheikhs) should be granted charities when we are actually the receivers of the charities given by them. All the gold and dresses we wear are those given to us by these destitutes. In truth we are the destitutes who have received their charities, yet we are directed to give them charity.

“Being so mean persons, you’re being the wife of that great soul is like infidel women who was the wife of H. Noah. Had you not been connected with this august house, I would have torne you to pieces right now, and rid that great one like H. Noah of you. and as a result of killing, you were I to be killed as punishment, it would be a matter of great honour for me. But such a wrong act cannot come from me in the house of the emperor of the time. Go away from me. You are a bitch of this house on guard otherwise I would do whatever I would like to do.

After this, the disciple went here and there making enquiries with the people ad to where the shaikh could be found. Someone told him: “that Qutub (pole of spiritualism) has gone over to the hillock in the forest to collect firewood.” Instantly the sharp-witted disciple with a wit has sharp s Zulfiqar, H. Ali’s sword, marched towards the forest. In the meanwhile, Satan appeared to him in a manly form causing insinuation in his mind to hide the moon-like shaikh behind the dust of insinuations, as to why the great master of religion and faith has such a woman as his mate in this house.
“There is no love lost between opposites. He is a leader of humans and what connection does he have with an ape”.

Then he recited Laa haowla (NO authority except in God) thinking that having such ill feelings for the shaikh amounts to my casting as persons and objections from my vicious self. It amounts s to extreme meanness and infidelity on my part. It is all God’s own making and who am I to speculate upon them? His actions cannot be without a hidden purpose. Yet he was not fully satisfied. The insinuation further persisted and made a different attack upon his mind. This caused a smoke in his heart just as a heap of wet grass creates smoke. The insinuation was: what connection is there between Jibra‘iil and Satan that they go together. How could H. Ibrahim go with his father, Aazar (the idol maker). How can a guide go along with a dacoit?

chapters.title: Riding upon a Lion
chapters.subtitle: The disciple’s meeting with his object by meeting the shaikh near the forest

paras: While he was in those conflicting thoughts, the well-known shaikh came before him riding upon a lion. The lion was roaring loudly dragging the fuel for its fiery existence and that victorious shaikh was sitting upon that fire and fuel. Because of his nobility the whip in his hand (to control lion) was a male snake.

You may be sure to know that every shaikh rides upon ferocious lions. The only difference was that Abul Hasan’s lion was visible to the people, but the lions of others are not. They are visible only to those who have a spiritual insight within them. Shaikh Abul Hasan’s lion was meant for common folk. Lakhs of lions are under their command under their thighs upon which they sit. For the seers of the hidden things, they are just like firewood. They are all invisible, but this lion of shaikh Abul Hasan was made to appear as lion by God so that this disciple may also see the physical lion as he was yet a novice.

sections.heading: Trial of Patience by Wife
paras: The shaikh saw the disciple from the distance and he laughed at him and said: “do not hear the devil of what he said to you”. the grand shaikh had come to know of the goings on in the heart of the disciple through the light of heart, as heart is the best of the witnesses and arguments. He told him about all the insinuation that came into his heart, while he was on the way to him. Then started telling about the wife’s difficulties in her refusals and rejections. He was in her company and bearing with her, not for the obedience of sensuous feelings as the disciple had thought. The disciple should not remain stuck on that thought. I have her as my wife for the reformation of my self and to increase my capacity for patience. Had I not developed these qualities how could the male lion be under my service without any renumeration for me. I am stronger and faster like the large-sized camel and I am contented, inebriated but under the control of howdah of God. I am not half-baked in my obedience to God’s commands that I would worry about the comments and abuses of the people. Our usual acts and special acts are all under God’s commands and our soul is running fast in the search of God. I am far away from all the people’s praises and expectations and totally unconcerned with their acceptances and rejectors. Our remaining alone or in the company of others is not due to our choice. Our life is totally in the hands of God like dice. What to say about my wife, men like us have no are for the remarks of hundreds of fools like her. We are not either after beauty or after fine fragrance. What all we do is only for God’s sake.

sections.heading: Battlefield Within Heart
paras: “This much of a lesson, our disciples also have learnt, but there is no limit, to our grandeur and power in the battlefield against ourselves. It is up to that limit beyond which there is no way whatsoever except the flash of light of lightning from of the moon of God. This light is far away from all our imaginations and speculations. It is only the light of the light, further light of the light and light alone. For your sake I have stooped to low level of talk, so that you may learn to maintain your companionship with ill-natured fellows. So that you may happily bear with the hardships caused by them as patience is the key to comforts and peace. When you manage to bear with these mean fellows, you enter into the light of the practices of the prophets, as the prophets have scene many troubles from the mean fellows. They have suffered a lot from these snakes.”

A it was the design of every-forgiving-God, His object and command, there was only His light well before the creations of all things which cannot be exhibited other than through opposites, as that Uncomparable King did not have anything to compare with.

chapters.title: World of Opposites Leads to Truth
chapters.subtitle: Wisdom behind God’s statement: I am to create a vicegerent on earth: Innii jaa ‘ilun fil ardhi khalifatan: (Baqara 2: 30)

sections.heading: Continuing Oppositions
paras: Therefore, God made a possessor-of- heart (man) as His vicegerent, who could be a reflection of his kingship. So, he gave him unlimited cleanliness and beauty and then made his opposite with unlimited darkness. Thus, He raised two flags — one white and another dark. The one white was of Adam and the other dark one was as Iblis. Both of them form great armies which are always at war with each other. Similarly, in the second phase there was Abel with clear and clean light; and there was caine as his opponent. In this manner two opposing flags of justice and cruelty respectively came about one after one, till Nimrod, who was the opponent and enemy of H. Ibrahim. The armies of both were in oppositions and at war with each other. When the war between them prolonged without ending, fire was brought about to settle the dispute. Then He ordered fire and calamity so that the difficulties of both may come to end. Therefore, after a long period of time these two opponents came against each other as harsh Pharoah and kind, Musa. there was a war between them for years together, which went beyond limit, causing great trouble when, God made water of the Nile as an arbitrator to settle the dispute to make one victorious and the other vanquished. So also, a punishment came to the people of Thamud in the form of deafening noises, which took away their lives. So also, the community of ‘Aad was given punishment through a fast-blowing wind, which finished them. So also, Qarun (Korah of English Bible) was also punished. Earth opened her mouth and swallowed him like a python. The sober nature of earth became a calamity for him and dragged him and his wealth within its depth.

sections.heading: Same Thing Protects and Kills
paras: Morsels of food are the pillars of the body, which are like the swords to finish hunger, and to act as coats of mail in their fight with it. But when God makes the bread hostile to you, it gets stuck in the throat as happens in the sickness of khunnaq (quinsy: inflammation by tonsils) which narrows down the gullet. The dress that protects you from cold is converted into a chilly hydrosphere, resulting in your clothes completely overlapping your body like snow and biting like ice. You will get so disgusted that you will throw away all your clothes and fur coat and prefer to be in the chilly spheres of air high above earth (Zamhariir).

You do not contain water of the volume of two large sized pots in which a little dirt does not cause pollution (as per Imam Shafi ‘ii). You have only one small pot of water. Therefore, be not fearless about the narrative of the people of zhullah (shade), when under God’s command roofs and the walls of the houses of their towns and villages neither provided shade nor protection from sun and rain, compelling them to go their leader, H. Shu‘aib, and say to him: “We are all about to die, our leader. Please give us peace and protection.” We shall say only this much about them. The rest you may see in the books of exegesis. The staff of H. Musa became a snake in his smart hand, to establish the perfectness of God’s doing to make it clear for acceptance by Pharoah. This much is enough for you to realise, if you have enough wisdom. This process of clarification continued up to the days and place of H. Muhammad while dealing with Abu jahl, the commander of cruelties. He saw pebbles praising Muhammad in his sun-like bright hand and fingers. This denier of truth looked at this but did not bow his head in obedience out of his blind enmity.

sections.heading: Look Twice to See Well
paras: You have the sight and capacity to see, but it has no depth. It is like the clogged up source of the water of fount. It has stopped the flow of water. A single look does not expose the truth, as you can see only the exterior but not. What is hidden inside. That is why, God, the Decorator of thinking, has told his servants to look twice, once at the apparent and again in depth, when He said: Turn your vision a second time: Farji ‘il basra karrataini (Mulk: 67: 4). God does not want you to beat upon cold iron but to beat upon red-hot iron to convert it into what shape you want. He had made iron to get tamed at the hands of H. Dawood.

sections.heading: Wisdom Should Go with Inner Sighting
paras: In order to give life to your dead body you may go towards Israafiil, who with the blow of his bugle will give fresh life to your body. and as refresh your heart has gone cold and frigid, you may go to the lively, spirited, strong-hearted-spiritualist-saints, who will warm up your heart just as the sun does with ice. You have become one to entirely rely upon wisdom and thoughts and overlapped yourself in entirety with them, and to increase them you go to the sophists who use clever, quibbling but unsound arguments and rely entirely upon logic and vocabulary. As the sophists considers his own existence as unreal as a shadow, because of his in perfect wisdom; and ignorance of true knowledge coming from both outer and inner senses, he cannot be your proper guide. He uses only the brain not at all the heart. These dialectical, mental arguments are of no appeal to the common folk. You have to speak with others of your own level of dependence upon wisdom. Be careful! If you talk of these before common people, you will be disgraced in their circle. Seeing things from the other angle of inner sight is like removing materials clogging the source of water of the fount and allowing the water to flow out. This is what you have to do to remove the clog from your soul so that inner blocked up thoughts may freely flow and continue to exist.

sections.heading: Avicninna’s Great Clarification
paras: That philosopher, Abu Ali siinaa (Avicinna) has also said that when the soul gets freedom from the prison of the body, it goes toward a garden of freedom. [Abu Ali Sina in his treatise Mi‘raajaia said that man has to souls. One is a biological soul which is life which ceases to exist upon death and is like subtle vapour; and the other is human soul which continues to exist even after death and continues to exist freely. He calls this as the thinking and speaking soul, which continues to exist even after death. Thus, he also considers two types of sightings — one cursory of the apparent, (as by the eyes) and other of in-depth study and assessment as by mind, intellect and spirit). For this understanding, Avicinna is called as a renegade by some scholars. — Qazi sajjad Husain.]

Some scholars said that with this assessment, he became a renegade and went toward the bottomless pit: Alqari‘atu: (Al Qari‘a: 101: 9); or Fire blazing fiercely: naarun haamiytun: (Al-qari‘a: 101: 11). This may be his going to the bottomless pit as those people say; or it may be a underground path of the mouse in which it moves from this side to that. But inspite of being a philosopher, he has pointed to two situations and named them as animal soul and human soul and explained about them. How grateful we have to be to him for his explaining of this difference. We have to know about the affairs of the person who understands the difference between different commands and follows them. If such a person desires to make a thorn of a flower, it happens.

chapters.title: Calamiteis, and Protection from Them
chapters.subtitle: H. Huud’s miracle at the time of the blowing of fierce wind to protection his followers

paras: H. Hood drew a line around his followers so that his community could not undergo sufferings of the impacts of fierce wind. And they sat safe within this circle without receiving any pains from the harmful wind. the wind was like a deluge and the circle was like an ark. There are many kinds of such deluges and arks. Wind was the deluge and God’s grace was the ark, he has got many kinds of deluges and arks.

sections.heading: Different Deluges and Arks
paras: God makes a king as an ark and gives him greed to meet which he makes attacks on armies. The king’s aim is not to provide peace to people, but it is only to bring the country under him and to expand his kingdom. Ox of the water wheel moves fast only to protect itself from beatings. Its intention is not to draw wate or that there should be crushing of sesame to get oil. The ox fears only harsh beatings and has no wish to dry the cart and take forward the goods in it. But is provided with such pains and fears so that good results may come about from them.

In similar manner every professional sits in his shop not to provide profits to the world but to meet his own gains just as every person searches for an ointment for his own wounds. With their individual, self-interests an order has come about in the world. God has made fear as the pillar of this world, and everyone is engaged in some job out of this fear. Everyone is concerned with of some good or bad and not with himself. Thus, God has appointed a commander upon everyone, who is very near, but invisible to him. Though you cannot see it, it is always around you to catch you as though you are a thief. Therefore, be careful and watchful of it. It is sitting in hiding waiting to attack but people cannot find it out.

sections.heading: Needed Wisdom from Another World
paras: The sense with which this commander can be seen is not of this world but of the other world which is given to whosoever God wishes. If the animal or animal soul were to see it, every ox and donkey and men of their nature would be so great as to make them their Bayezid’s of time. The one who made the body as the exponent of soul and made H. Noah’s Ark as a fast heavenly burraq (of lightening speed, sitting upon which the noble Prophet had performed his journey of Ascent) can also make the ark itself as a deluge for you, if He so wishes. He has connected ever moment as your deluge with your ark and connected them both with your happiness and sorrows. If you cannot see the deluge and ark before you, you may see yourself as to how all parts of your body are in constant obedience to you.

When a man does not see the causes of his fears, he gets into the fears of different kinds of thoughts arising from his half-baked mind. A drunken, ignorant fellow gives a blow to a blind man, but the blind man thinks that he is kicked by a mule, as he heard the voice of the mule at that time. The mirror of the blind man is the ear and not the eye and so he did not see. Then he again thinks no, it was a stone that hit him and not the mule. It may also be a stone flying from the hill. He considered three reasons for the attack on him — the mule, a stone hit by some one or a stone arriving from a hill. All these three sources are miscalculations. He was busy in thinking: no t this, not that and so on. The one who created these fears in man remained invisible and man got entangled in inconclusive thoughts.

sections.heading: Right Only Creates Wrong
paras: Fears and shivers come from outside. A man is not afraid of himself. A philosopher considers fear as phobia caused by a mental situation or psychic function in which something is misunderstood for something else or baseless suspicion. He has understood it in a perverse manner. He considers that something is misunderstood as something else without any reasoning. He fails to understand that there are reasons for suspicions also. Suspicions do not come about from nowhere. One may fear no reasons that he might be killed. This is true as far as he is conserved. But he sees such happenings elsewhere. These happenings elsewhere become a cause of fear in him. This is similar to the circulation of counterfeit coins, which is possible only when there are genuine coins. It is the genuine coins that pave the way for circulation of counterfeit coins. Falsehood cannot prevail without there being truth. People resort to falsehood by calling it as truth, as truth has acceptability. In this way it is truth that has paved the way for falsehood. Therefore, falsehood has to be thankful to truth as truth only provides scope for false hood. This truth cannot be ignored.

sections.heading: Fresh and Dry Branches of Tree
paras: I do not know whether I should talk about the philosopher and his thoughts or about the arks and deluges. I shall speak of the arks as that is more appealing and all-embracing. Other things are only parts, and they are the wholes. Consider every friend of God as an ark and the companionship of the people as the deluge. Lions and pythons are not as dangerous as friends and colleagues. While in their company your time is wasted. And so also, when away from them, your mind remains engaged in their thoughts. Thinking about anyone is like a thirsty donkey which licks water from funnel. Thinking of friends sucks the water of the body and the mind.

By engaging yourself in their thoughts, all the life-giving-water of your body is lost and you get converted into a dry wooden log. Marks of the sucking of water in a tender branch of the tree can be seen in its capacity to wave. Fresh and tender branch of the tree contains plenty of water because of which it can be pulled in any direction. You can make a basket of it if you want or bend it make circular ring to pot in your neck. When the branch does not suck water from its stem and roots, it cannot be pulled and bent in the direction of your choice. This is the situation of hypocrites about whom the Quran says: when they stand for prayer, they stand without earnestness: Wa izaa qaumuu ilas sallti qaumuu kusaalaa: (Nisa: 4: 142). This is what happens when the milk of life is not provided by the breasts to man. God’s friend regularly receives the milk of life from God and are always amenable to Him. These are very hot discussions beyond the understanding of common folk and therefore, I stop at this and proceed to talk about that poor man and his search for treasure.

sections.heading: Fires, Fire of Heart, Fire of Love
paras: You have seen fire that burns out the plants. But you may look at the fire of the heart which burns out thinking capacity. There is the fire of love which burns out the heart and soul, apart from burning the thoughts. Rather it takes away the light of the heart and soul and renders it dark. Neither thought has peace with it nor the truth. This is a fire that sets a fire the soul itself. Fire of the love of God dominates over the brave and cunning lion and fox like qualities of man and destroys these instants. Thus, everything that exits will perish except God’s own face: Kullu shai ‘in haalikun illa wajhahu (Qasas: 28: 88). Get yourself lost into the radiance of His essence and get mixed up just as the letter alif from the noun ism got mixed up in God in the phrase Bismillah which became bismillaah instead remaining as bi -ism- Allah. The letter alif got lost in the word bismi. It is as though hit is within it, and also out of it. It has lost its separate individual existence, but in fact it remains as a part of bismii. In this manner all the letters become lost (remain silent) when they get mixed up with other letters. This is the reward for the getting mixed up and love of the letter alif for the letter bay in bismi that they together did not tolerate the presence of the letter alif in between them, taking it is as an extravagant and unnecessary interferer. When togetherness cannot tolerate a letter in between, it becomes necessary that the resort to eliminate unnecessary prolonging, and shorter my speech. And, when instead of the coming together of letters bay and sin, they are apart. It is better that I maintain total silence. When the letter alif has lost itself in bay and removed itself from in between, both bay and sin do not ignore it but take it in their meaning in togetherness as bismi and make it a part of themselves. This is what happens to God’s servant who gets himself lost in God, as the noble Prophet had done, consequent upon which what he did wit his hand was what God Himself did as per the statement in Quran: when you threw (a handful of dust), it was not your act but God’s act: wa maaramaita iz ramaita, walaakinnallaaha ramaa: (Anfal: 8: 17). [This refers to the Prophet’s throwing dust toward the enemy at the battlefield — Translator]. When the action fo the man cannot be attributed to man. So also, the words cannot be attributed to man but go back to God. Therefore, what the Prophet said were not his words but Allah’s words. So long as the medicine remains separate in the container, it is not medicine. It does not perform any act. But when it is consumed and digested by the sick man, it eliminates sickness and shows itself through its activity.

sections.heading: Meanings of Math(s)navi Without Limits
paras: Even if all the trees of all the forests become pens, and the oceans become ink, there is no scope for the coming to end of this Math(s)navi. The mould for making bricks will last as long as there is clay for making bricks. Consideration of the meaning of its every verse and indepth study will also continue to go on. Even when the entire clay of the earth does not remain anymore after getting blown off by the fierce winds (of the doomsday), Math(s)navi’s ocean will become more vigorous, creating its own clay to carry on tis brick-making-decorative-construction work. When the forests cease to exist upon the earth, forests will raise their heads from the ocean of tis words. It is for this reason that God with His expansive explanations has permitted us to explain matters from His ocean as it has no limits.

sections.heading: Child’s Play Also Gives Wisdom
paras: Now, you may return from the talks of the ocean and turn towards the dry land and talk about games and entertainment as these are better and more profitable for children, so that little by little from games, their wisdom may become familiar with the talks of the ocean. A child gets wisdom by playing, even though play does not appear to be connected with wisdom. A mad child does not play any game. Petty parts are required to understand the whole.

chapters.title: Searcher and Searched: Both Are Same
chapters.subtitle: Return to the narrative of dome and treasure

sections.heading: Manner’s Getting Lost in God
paras: Good thoughts of that unexposed poor man have been continuingly calling me to come over humbling me down. You cannot hear this voice, but I hear, as I am also a sharer of his thoughts. Do not consider him just as a searcher of treasure as he is himself a treasure. Being a sharer of his secret, I cannot remain away from him. There is a direct connection and relationship between a searcher and the object of search. Both are crazy and devoted to each other. They are one and the same. This is like one prostrating to a mirror reflecting one’s own image, when the image also appears to be prostrating to the prostrator. The searcher sees himself in the mirror. Instead of seeing his physical object, if he sees even a bit of the inner qualities of the object he totally gets absorbed in the object and forgets his own self and his independent existence. He sees himself in it, as it happened to Mansoor Hallaaj who lost himself in God and cried out: ‘I am the truth’. All his thoughts ceased to remain, and he was himself lost in the object (God). All his knowledge about God totally vanished from his mind. And he became totally ignorant of all knowledge of all things. In this manner, our lack of knowledge itself becomes a different kind of knowledge. It raises its head and cries out: ‘I alone and nothing else’.

sections.heading: Why Angels Ordered to Prostrate to Adam
paras: Prostration is valid and meant for God alone and by issuing a command to angels to prostrate to Adam, it was made clear to them that they were also exponents of God as Adam was an exponent of God. They should get merged in him. Here, there as a direction to the children of Adam to know that they are also the exponents of this reality. The cross-eyed-nature of the angels to see two objects in one object was set aside. They saw the earth also as a recipient of light as the sky was. they found both the earth and sky as the same. He meant the same when he said: ‘no God (laailaaha) to say, ‘except God’: (illa Allah)’. His ‘no God’ became ‘except God’. That is, God alone and thus clarified oneness of God as ‘One and only One.’ He alone was one with God. That is his saying: ‘I am God’ meant as good as saying: no God ‘except God’. The subject matter is the same but he way of expression is different.

sections.heading: Secrets, Not Be Revealed
paras: Now the time has come when God, that Beloved and Friend of Guidance should pull my ears and take me to the fount of law (shariat) to wash my face, as my discussion has gone to the shape where shariat does not permit me to speak of the secrets to the people, which it has kept hidden from them. Even if you speak of them, there will be no clarity in them, and none can understand them, but you will commit a crime for which you are required to be hanged to death. But I am the only one to speak of these confusing thoughts and also the hearer. Thus, I cannot be a violator of the law.

sections.heading: Love to Hear of Adventures and Sufferings
paras: Now, let there be no more talk of those matters. Speak of the apparent matters of that poor man and the direction of the hidden treasure. These people love to hear about adventures and the troubles one undergoes. Therefore, speak of adventures and pains. They want to hear not about godly matters but about man’s affairs and it is difficult for me to speak of man’s worldly affairs. But in view of the common people’s interest and taste I am compelled to narrate stories of this type. They have prohibited upon themselves the talks of shariat, which are nothing but the founts of faith and mercy. They ignore the water of this fount but go on drinking cups upon cups of deadly poison. They have collected lots of dust in their lapels to choke the mouth of these founts and dry them up. But the mouth of this fount that receives it supply of water from the ocean cannot be choked with this dust of good or bad quality, which are their baseless interpretations. They say that they closed their minds upon what is said to them by me (fount). It says: “But I also do not care for you as I am connected with the Endless and Everlasting as against you.”

sections.heading: Contentment with Exoteric Knowledge
paras: They are a perverted community engaged in their already decided subjective notions eating the mud above ignoring to drink the water flowing under the mud. They are opposed to the nature of the prophets, who used to talk of truth whether it was appealing or not to the people, these exoterics take the common people as their pillows and rest upon them to please them, with unworthy interpretations even though these pillows are like pythons.

But you say that you have come to know of the curtains having before the people, but do not know yourself, as to from what you have shut your eyes? By what means do you want to open the eyes of the people. Do you consider those means as totally wrong, because they are logical and rhetorical dispensations which are far away from the inner meanings and truths of shariat. They are meaningless, decorative persuasions, hard to understand philosophical jargons. Yet, you should speak out as there are certain persons upon when the sunlight of benevolence has fallen who interpret not upon the matters of faith but upon the interpretations that the earlier great men have done, as though they agree with the inner content but reject the labels. Their pessimistic approaches have also been taken as acceptable at times.

sections.heading: Wrongs Also Become Right
paras: But God’s dice brings about strange results of goodness by waving their wrongs from upon them and making them acceptable in some quarters. He has flowed fountains of love from their misinterpreted beliefs as well. In all generosity He has raised two hundred fountains of love from their misfortune itself. He produces flowers out of thorns. He provides a bead in the mouth of the snake, that acts as an antidote for its poison. He brings forth bright say from out of the dark night. He brings forth wealth from out of the hands of the destitutes. He made wheat out of sand grains for people like H. Ibrahim and the frightening sang in chorus with H. Dawood when he was in distress: also producing sweet tunes of musical instruments. O Dawood, you got distressed with people! Do not be so now! Get up! You have given up their company. We shall compensate by giving your own companionship.

chapters.title: The Searchers Prayer
chapters.subtitle: Further submission of the searcher of treasure to God after much failure and desperation saying: “O Revealer of the hidden things! Reveal the hidden thing for me”

sections.heading: Conditional Acceptance of Prayer
paras: That poor man said: “O knower of the secrets! I made meaningless efforts to get that treasure. Becoming mad of greed and excess I went fast and discarded slow actions and silent approach. I did not get a single morsel from the cauldron but blackened my hand and burnt my mouth. Why did I not speak to myself that I should get this knot unknotted by the knot-maker himself, when there was a stipulated condition that I should shoot arrows to locate the place of treasure? I had a doubt on this stipulated condition. The giver does not put such conditions. Yet instead of seeking clarification on this question on the statement of God with reference to His other statements. I straight away rushed to shoot arrows in an unthoughtful manner. I should have known that this was a knot put by Him and could be opened only by Him. The chess piece place by Him on the chessboard can be lifted by Him alone to win the game. None else can do it. This type of averments appears to be very easy to talk, but these are from “God’s own knowledge”, which are highly secretive and difficult to understand. Therefore. My Lord! Now I realise and repent for my hasty approach. Now that you have shut the door, you alone may open.

sections.heading: Sleep: Virtual Death
paras: “Inspite of my repentance, once again I am after my own attempts to understand, my own, as I did earlier, as I made an unsuitable supplication, which was a great wrong. There was no need for me to think of my abilities, my own self and even my disturbed heart. The stress here is upon my own self and my belongings. I should have considered myself only as His reflection and discarded myself completely. Every night all my abilities and designs sink like a boat in water when i go into sleep. Neither I remain nor my designs and my body remain without any self-consciousness, just like a dead body. not only I but also all humans become dead till the morning, and nobody responds to His question: ‘am I not your Lord? By saying: ‘yes! We do admit! You are our Lord!’. He rises this question, and they fail to answer. Therefore, He alone answers this question on our behalf to mean that: “we are all your obedient servants and do all that you want us to do.” This is because those to answer are not in their places. They are swept away by the flood, or the crocodile ahs swallowed them, tore them apart and shattered them to pieces. And, on the arrival of the morning He takes out his embellished sword from the scabbard and hits upon the darkness of the night.

sections.heading: Routine Engagements Are Prayers to God
paras: The sun completes its journey of the night and the crocodile of night spills out what all it had swallowed. And all the senses, consciousnesses and abilities of man come back to him. Just as H. Yunus came out of the belly of the fish, we come out of the belly of this crocodile and spread out with all our different colours and fragrances of our abilities. all creatures start recitation of the praises of God just as H. Yunus did as they had taken full rest during the darkness of the night. Everyone makes these praises by engaging himself in his jobs in the morning after coming out of the belly of the fish of dark night, saying: O Generous one! You kept so many tasty treasures of mercy and benevolence in that frightening night. Our eyes became brighter, our ears became sharper, and bodies became lighter in weight as a consequence of the crocodile of the night which took us her and there during the darkness of the whole night and relieved us of all our burdens. Such being the graces hidden in frightening situation, we shall never run away from them when you are with us to protect us.

sections.heading: Keen Observing Eyes Required
paras: What H. Musa saw as fire was not fire but light. We considered the night as a black negro, but it was a fair hoer (house). We do not ask you for anything other than the eyes, which are very sharp, selective, good in observation. From now onwards we shall ask for such eyes only so that the ocean may not appear to be covered up with grass scraps and leaves. When the eyes of the magicians became sharp, they got rid of hidden blindness and started clapping their palms with joy upon the loss of their hands and legs. Eyes of the people close only due to some misconceptions. Those who shiver due to misconceptions are the ones who have no proper sight. But there is no need for such of them also to despair as God has kept upon His doors for both the deserving and undeserving to take everyone inside His court. Both those with spread out palms of their hand, and those without, are freed from slavery with the freedom given by His mercy. Where were we entitled to come into existence from the world of non-existence (‘adam) that we got this life and existence and attained great wisdom.

sections.heading: God Gives and Receives
paras: “O the one who befriended the strangers, the One who granted the dress of flowers to thorns, you may make our dry mud green and fresh once again. Make the worthless worthy. You have given us this command to pray in this manner in the beginning itself; as otherwise where is a handful of dust to pray in this manner. When you have given us the command to pray, do accept our prayer too.

“The boat of intelligence and senses was broken at night. There was neither hope, nor fear and despair. God took me in the ocean of wonders. Let us see with what qualities He would fill me and send back. Some were filled up with light and majesty and the others with doubts and speculations. the former ore the saints and gnostics and the latter are philosophers and worldly people. All these are qualities not originating from them. If I were to have my own opinions and designs, these would have been under my own control. My consciousness would not have vanished from me during the night. All my birds would have been within my hold. I would have been aware of the different stations of my soul during to my sleep, unconsciousness and trials. When my hands are devoid of the control over them, it is strange, how I look at myself and consider myself as of any worth. There is no place for any pride for me. I, considered as unseen, what I was actually looking at, and once again open my begging bag before God.

sections.heading: Humble Beginning of Man
paras: O Generous One: Our origin starts with the word Umm, meaning mother. This is made up fo two letters — alif which is empty without any possession and the letter miim, which has a narrow eye, (a circular shape aits top). Being made up of those two black letters I have a heart which is harder than the narrow eye (upper circular shape) of miim. These letters alif and miim are my mother (umm) of existence. The eye of miim ais narrow and alifn is poorer than the narrow miim. This alif being empty has no worth of its own. It is nothing but ignorance and devoid of every worthiness. Miim is narrow minded. Both these together are worthy in this world full of wisdom. In the moments of my unconsciousness, I am totally worthless and at the moment of consciousness, I am in total confusion. Do not make this worthless fellow still more worthless by adding further worthlessness. Do not call this cross-eyed situation as worthy and valuable. Inspite of my not possessing anything, you make me worthy. But these hundreds of pains that I have are due to my suspicions of worthiness about myself. O my God: you may take care of me when I have nothing. I have seen many difficulties. You may provide relief to me.

sections.heading: Tears: a Great Gift
paras: “I do not have even tears in my eyes to flow. I stand at your door not only without tears but even without eyes. Provide for a servant of yours without eyes, both the eyes and tears and make his dry land into a green productive field with the wetness of tears. And, if there are eyes without tears, grant tears to my eyes as the Prophet wanted two eyes full of tears when he prayed to you: “O God provide to me with two tear shedding eyes: with so much of grandeur, acceptability and superiority. When he sought for the grant of tears from God, why should I not go weak and thin with tears of blood, particularly when I am totally empty-handed, worthless and flattering? When the eyes of such a great personality like the prophet had so much love and regard for tear, I need tears as of hundreds of rivers like jaihun. One drop of tear from his eye is worth the water of two hundred Jaihuns. With a single tear, when he prayed for deliverance, all the men and jinn’s got deliverance after his intercession was accepted by God.

When the Prophet being a garden of paradise prayed for rain, why should not my barren land not pray for water? Therefore, my brother do not lift your hands for prayer without thinking whether it will be answered or not. Praying for needs is your job and acceptance or otherwise in not yours. But tears are absolutely necessary while making prayers. The breed of worldly engagements prevents you from shedding tears. Therefore, get rid of this bread so that tears may roll down from the eyes. Make yourself smart and serious and prepare your bread with tears to make your prayer acceptable for not only the possessions of this world but of the other world too.”

chapters.title: Search at Far Off Places
chapters.subtitle: Call by the hidden announcer to the searcher of treasure; and revealing of the secret of the truth

paras: While he was engaged in these difficult, thoughts as inspiration, came from God which solved his difficulties and he got relieved of tensions. The inspiration said: “I had only asked you to keep the arrow on the bow. I had not asked you to draw the string. I had not told you to pull the string very much. I had told you to just keep it on the bow and not to shoot it out. But with your senselessness you lifted the bow up and resorted to the expertise in archery. Now you may go and stop this hard archery, keep the arrow and do not worry about its shooting out. When it falls down, you may dig up the place where it falls and search. Do not use your might but resort to humility and search for treasure. You ignored to search for God, who is nearer to you than your jugular vein and flew the arrows of your thoughts at distant places.

sections.heading: Search in Nearby Places
paras: Those relying upon the far flinging arrows ignore the prey available close by and run away from it to distant places. God, who is so close to them is searched at faraway places. One who considers that the object is at a distance, is faraway from the object. It is he who is faraway and not the object. Instead of seeing the object right before him with his vision, he uses his physical strength. The farther away he shoots his arrow, the farther away he is from the object and deprived of such a great treasure. The rationalist destroyed himself with his own thinking as he has kept his back toward the treasure and searched on the opposite side. Tell him that the more he runs in that direction, the farther away he will go from the treasure. God has said: and those who strive in our cause — We will certainly guide them to Our paths: Wallaziina jaahaduu fiinaa lanahdiyannahum subulanaa: (‘Ankabut: 29: 69). Be careful and see that He has not said: strive for us while being away from us: (jaahudu ‘annaa). This is what Noah’s son, kan‘aan did. He ran away from the humbleness of his father toward the peak of a lofty mountain. He thought it humiliating to be in a small ark. The farther he ran away in search of refuge, the greater he got separated from the place of refuge. This is what that poor fellow did to search for the gold mine and treasure. Every day he searched for a stronger bow. The stronger the bow he went after the more unfortunate eh was in tracing the location of the treasure.

sections.heading: Curtain of Too Much Learning
paras: This is an illustration for guidance in the life of everyone. Life of a foolish fellow is very cheap and full of pains. A foolish fellow thinks it humiliating to sit before a master to learn and opens his own stop without proper training. He is away from his object. Such a shop cannot come to the level of well-trained masters and will be full of loss causing dirt, scorpions and snakes. Do not maintain such a shop. Close it and turn away from it and go toward the green garden by the side of a stream. Do not be like kan‘aan son of Noah, who out of his ignorance and arrogance took the destructive mountain as a protective boat against the water of the deluge. Similarly, the knowledge of archery became a curtain for that poor man in reading his object which was in his pocket itself.

sections.heading: Simpletoers Live in Paradise
paras: Many a times, knowledge, intelligence and too much sharpness of mind become misguides and dacoits for a journeyman. Many of the residents of paradise are the ignorant fellows as the Prophet said: the faithful are noble and simpletons. Al mu‘minu ghirrun karuum: (Hadith(s)). [This is also a famous saying: men of paradise are simpletons: Qazi sajjad Husain]. This is for this reason that they do not entangle themselves with the confusions caused by the rationalists. Therefore, keep yourself rid of these useless excellences so that mercy and benevolences may continuously pour upon you. over intelligence is the opposite of humbleness and decency. Therefore, give it up and adopt simplicity and humility. Consider the search of hair-splitting arguments as a trap. Those of pure and simple hearts do not go for them. The rhetorically intelligent remain contented with their arguments and rhetoric, and the simpleton’s resort to a simple trade and work on it and become experts in it. A young child is provided food by the mother throughout the day holding him on her side with full protection and becomes his own hands and legs.

chapters.title: All Living and Non-Living Worship God
chapters.subtitle: Story of three co-travellers, — a Muslim, Chirstian and a Jew. They found food on the way. The Christian and Jew were belly full and they did not eat and decided to eat on the next day. But the Muslim was fasting, and remained hungry, as he was weak

paras: Hear this story, my son, so that you may not fall into the trial of artistry. Three persons — a Jew, Muslim and Chirstian went together on a journey. There was one faithful between two misguided, just as man’s wisdom remains along with his self and devil. One from Marghaz and other from Rey, while on journey go together and dine on the same dining sheet facing each other. They became like the Crow, owl and falcon kept together in a single cage like the regular worshipper and non-worshipper put together in the same prison. Travelling together is like that.

sections.heading: Consciousness Holds Opponents Together
paras: These three travellers, despite of being as different from each other as the east and west camped in one place with all patience and togetherness in the caravanserai. People having come from short and long distances camp here in a common place for many days due to chilly winter and snowfall. When the season is congenial, roads open and obstacles removed, they get separated and march toward their different destinations. Similarly, the birds put together in a single case will fly differently in different directions, when the cage is opened by some wise man. Before this flying off they were enthusiastic, remembering their friends with feathers ready to flap to fly to their respective places in the love of their families. They were continuously ready with spread-out wings full of sighs, tears and burning pain of the hearts, and immediately upon getting the opportunity went on their own ways.

Look at the different parts of your body as to from where they have come together, all made of water, mud, air and fire. Connected differently with the lands, heavens, cities of Rome and Kish. Each one is waiting to go back to the place of its origin but settled in this camp of the body for the time being out of the fear of ice and snow. Different kinds of ice provide peaceful settlement to each of the material part, in the chilly winter being away from the heat of the sun. when the heat of the ferocious sun fall, mountains become like scraps, sand, grass and wool. Heavy materials melt down just as the body changes in every way upon the departure of the soul.

sections.heading: Villagers Are Hospitable
paras: When these three co-travellers settled in a camp, a poor kind-hearted villager brought a sweet dish made in his kitchen for them and presented to all the three of them just as the kindly Generous God comes closer to man as it is said in the Quran: I am indeed close to them. Innii qariib (Baqara: 2: 186). He brought also hot bread and sweet prepared with honey expecting a reward only from God. Culture and intelligence are found among the urbanites. Hospitality and feeding among the villagers. God has kept food and hospitality in the village people for the good of the travellers. There is a new guest in the village every day, who has none but God to take care of him. There is a new caravan at every night in the village where there is none other than the All-Glorious God.

sections.heading: Well-Fed Have No Hunger
paras: One to over-feeding, the Chirstian and Jew were suffering from indigestion, but the Muslim was fasting and hungry. As the sweet dish had come at the time of fast-breaking time, the Muslim was very hungry and desired to eat. The other two fellows said: “We have no need of food this night, we shall keep the food for the next day. We shall lift our hands from eating to night and keep the food hidden for tomorrow”. The Muslim said: “keep your patience away for tomorrow. We shall eat it today itself.” Then they both said! “You appear to intend to be clever to eat the entire food yourself.” Then he said: “My friends; are we three not friends? We shall divide the food in three parts as there is a difference in approach. Whoever wishes may eat and whoever wishes may keep it safe for tomorrow.” They both said: “keep the thought of dividing away. Know this well that one who divides goes into hell?” the Muslim said: this refers to that divider who divides wrongly to please the vicious self and not to one with godly principles of justice. Mn is a property of God and entirely belongs to God. If you give a part of yourself to another and to other part of God. It brings about participating the other. One with God or dividing godhood into two.”

sections.heading: All Face Toward One God in Different Ways
paras: Like a lion dominating upon dogs, this Muslim would have dominated upon these two co-travellers, but domination of these two mean fellows upon him was greater. He was like a lion who was dominated by two cows. That was an occasion of the domination of treacherous cows. Anyway, that was their intention that he should not swallow food but his own grief. Thus, with hunger, he spent the night. He was defeated by them and accepted the defeat. Saying: “I heard you my friends: I concede to your point.” So also the others also slept during the night and woke up in the morning and performed their ablution. All of them wished their mouths and faces and turned their attention to towards their respective ways of warship. They kept themselves in prayer for sometime repeating their respective sermons, seeking God’s benevolences.

The faces of the Muslim, Chirstian, Jew and the Zoroastrian — all turn toward the great Ruler. The faces of all these people and also of the noble and vicious turn toward the One God. Rather, stones, mud, mountains and water — all turn towards God alone in their silent manners. Every thing turns to God. There is no end to this discussion.

sections.heading: Who Is Wise Are Superior
paras: Thereafter, all the three friends turned toward each other. One of them said: “let everyone speak of the dream he has seen in sleep in the previous night. Whosoever’s dream is better may take the entire food including the share of the one whose dream is lowly. Eating by one who is superior is wisdom is like the eating by those lesser in wisdom as a wiseman’s soul is superior to that of an ordinary man. His soul is full of greater brightness. The rest of the people should remain satisfied by serving him, as the wise have an everlasting life through their wisdom. That is to say that this world lives with them for ever!

sections.heading: The Jew’s Dream
paras: Then the Jew spoke of what he saw in his dream and as to which all the places where his soul roamed about. He said: “I saw H. Musa in front of me. A cat sees the lamb’s tail in its dream. I followed H. Musa up to the Mount Sinai (Tur) where all the three (he, H. Musa and Mt. Sinai) were covered up with light. The light, so bright as of the sun wiped off the shadows of all three of us.
