Then a door opened up in that light and a different kind of light came out of it, which went on increasing. All the three of us were lost in that light. Then, I saw that the mount broke into three pieces, as there was a blow of the light of God upon it. The quality of the shock of that light was so much that every part moved away from each other. One part went near the ocean making its poison like saltish water sweet. With the impact of another piece that penetrated into the earth, a fountain sprang up and water started flowing over ground. Its water, with the impact of God’s inspiration became medicine for all diseases. The third piece flew into the air and went near the Ka‘aba and became mount ‘Arafat.

“When I got up from this state of unconsciousness there was no trace of Mount Sinai at all. It was melting like ice under the feet of H. Musa. all its hardness and peak had gone. It was completely flattened on the ground, its elevation getting converted into lowland. Then after some time, I again regained my senses. I found both H. Musa and the Mount Sinai, well settled in their places. The valley was entirely full of grand creatures resembling H. Musa with his staff and his over coat, they were all going fast toward the Mount in great Joy. They had all spread their hands in prayer reciting together rhythmically: “Arine” (O lord, show yourself to me: (Kahaf: 7: 143) as H. Musa had said to God. Then my consciousness came back to me in full, I found the faces of all of them differently from each other. I concluded that they were all prophets friendly to H. Musa and that all prophets stand for the same single thing and message. Then I saw strange angels with their faces and bodies as if made up of ice. There was another group of angels seeking support who were all made up of fire.

sections.heading: End of All Is Good
paras: This Jew was telling all this: there are Jews who think and speak like this. These are the people whose final end is very good. Therefore, do not look at any idol worshipper with contempt, as there are hopes of their dying as Muslims. What can you assess of the end of their life that you turn your face away from them.

Therefore, the Christian started to narrate about his dream saying that he saw Jesus Christ in his dream. “I went along with him to the fourth heaven, which is the centre and location of the sun of this world. The strange forts of the heavens have nothing to do with the forts of other things of the earth. O my proud children: everyone knows well that the designs of the heavens are different from those of the earth.”

chapters.title: Respect to Elders
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the camel, cow and ram finding a bundle of grass on the way. Everyone claimed its right to eat; and then decided that the oldest among them should have it

paras: A camel, cow and ram found a bundle of grass on the way. The ram said: “this is too small. If we divide it amongst over selves nobody’s belly will fill and quench hunger. It is better that it should be given over to eat to the one oldest amongst us, as it has come in the Prophet’s saying that the elders should be given preference. This is the general good conduct. But in these days full of ill-meanness on two occasions only are the elder’s given preference. One while eating very hod food and the other when a discarded and ruined bridge is to be crossed. They do not serve the elderly-leading-guides without any mischievous personal gain. When such is the good conduct of preferring elders, you may imagine what they do while doing bad.

chapters.title: Treacherous Men: Worse Than Wolves
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the self-centred and their mischiefs in the form of kindness

paras: A king was going to the chief mosque of the city. Bodyguards and announcers accompanying him were hitting the people with their sticks and injuring their heads and tearing off their clothes. On the way an unconcerned freeman, received ten beatings without any reason but only upon the saying: “make way for the king.” He turned his bleeding head toward the king and said: “Look at this oven cruelty, and do not ask about hidden cruelty. This is the cruelty when you are one the way to do the good act of prayer to the mosque. When this is so while on the way to do a good act, what can be the harms on your way to do bad acts.

An elderly guide does not care to hear salutation from a mean fellow fearing that, it may later lead to his closeness with him. It is better for a saint to be caught by a wolf than meeting with an ill-tempered man. Though the wolf is very cruel, but it is not treacherous cunning and trapping. It is because of its lacking these qualities that it gets trapped in the net. All treacherous and designs are to be found in man. This is a treachery of a rich man that he hears the voice of a poor man and says: “I do not see anyone.”

chapters.title: Who Is Elder Than Whom
chapters.subtitle: Return to the story of camel, ox and ram and speaking of the age of everyone

paras: The ram said to the ox and camel: “My friends when we have been together, it is proper that everyone should speak of his age, so that the oldest amongst us be entitled and the others concede to it. As for me, I say that my meadow has been that to which that ram belonged, which was replaced by H. Isma‘iil for sacrifice.” The ox said: “I am older than you, being one of the pair of oxen which was used by H. Adam to plough his land, who is the father of all humans.” When the camel heard these two strange claims from the ram and ox, it lowered down its head and caught the bundle of grass in tis mouth and lifted it up in the air, without any hesitation saying: “there is no need for me to speak of my age as I have such a long neck and heavy body. My dears: everyone realises that I cannot be younger than you. every wise man knows that my existence is from a longer time than yours. My large size itself is a proof of my age. Everyone knows that I am as high as the sky, which is hundreds of times larger than this lowly earth. Where is the large expanse of the sky and where are these pieces of land upon the terrace of the sky before which treasure houses of the earth are nothing.”

chapters.title: Action Better Than Dreaming
chapters.subtitle: The Muslim’s answer by speaking of his dream and the feeling of regrets of others

sections.heading: Great Dreams Are of No Use
paras: Then the Muslim said: “O my friends! The king, Mustafa Muhammad appeared before me in my dream, who is the leader of leaders and king of prophets, the cause of honour for both the worlds and guide to all the paths. He told me: “one has gone up to the mount Sinai and entered into a game of love and familiarity with Musa to whom God spoke. The other was taken by Jesus Christ, the fortunate, to the fourth heaven, but you are under loss that you were not taken anywhere like them. You may get up and eat the sweet dish without any hesitation. Those experts and wise have gone up and read out the messages of victory and high states. They have already attained their excellences and got converted with the angels because of their intelligence. But you are a simpleton, less intelligent, remaining behind them. Therefore, get up and sit with the lowly sweet dish.” In obedience to the command of this king of the world, I, instantly ate the sweet dish and bread.

sections.heading: Dreaming and Actual Observation
paras: Then they said: “you are a greedy fellow at this time. It is strange that you ate a dish made of the dates”. And he said: “when that great king to be obeyed, ordered me, who am I to remain without obedience? Can you, as a Jew disobey a command of H. Musa, whether he calls you towards pleasures, sorrows or calamities? Can you, as a Christian, remain disobedient to the command of Jesus Christ? Then, how can I be disobedient to the honour of the prophets? I ate the sweet and I am pleased with this.” They both said to him: “By God! This is a true dream that you saw, and it is better than hundreds of dreams seen by us. You are a keen observer. Yours was not a dream in sleep but an actual observation, as its impacts are visible in fact. Your dream is not a dream but an actual observation, as you are a man of very good nature, as you reached your object in the form of a dream. Certainly, what you saw was not a dream but a reality, as you got a practical, practicable command to eat (kuluu). Certainly, you dream is a reality leading you to success and we remained sorrowful and pale-faced. O well-fed fellow! Certainly, your dream is real which you saw apparent and clear. “Your dream is like a dream of prophets which becomes clear without any need of interpretation. Therefore, keep yourself away from any claims of excellence, bravery and design as only obedience and good manners come to help. It is for this reason that God said in the Quran: I have only created jinn’s and man that they may serve me: wa maa khalaqtul jinna wal insa illaa liya ‘buduni: (Zurriat: 51: 56)”.

sections.heading: Direct and Interpretative Knowledge
paras: Of what use was Samiri’s art for him. In fact, his art kept him away from the door of God. Of what use was Qarun’s (kosah’s) gold for him? It took him down into the depth of earth. What did Bul hakam (Abu Jahl) get from his qualities. He fell down in hell because of his rejection of truth.

Consider that as an art which directly reveals the fire of truth to you and not the argument that smoke speaks of the proof of fire. Mere capacities of mind and worldly material knowledge cannot establish truth. Your logical arguments are of no worth before real wisdom. They are dependent upon lowly observations of the mean things like those of the physician who assess sicknesses by observing dirty urine. You are dependent only upon these dirty lowly mean things like urine and human stools. This knowledge of yours unreliable tool like the stick in the hand of a blind, which gives a clear evidence of the fact that its carrier is blind. Such arguments are lowly like our lowly thoughts, which do not stand before a wise person, as they are of little worth. I do not go after wild propaganda, showy demonstrations to catch and hold game animals. I do not care for them at all. Consider me to be helpless in this regard.

chapters.title: Consultation with the Wise
chapters.subtitle: Announcement of the king of Tirmiz as to who was there to go to Samarqand in three days to attend to his job, and receive grants and wealth from him? Hearing of this by a buffoon from a village and his going to the king just to say that he cannot do it

paras: The king of Tirmiz had a buffoon of interesting nature. The king had some important job in Samarqand. He wanted someone to go there and attend to his job. He got an announcement made that whoever would bring the required information within five days would be given a good reward with so much of gold and treasures that he would become an honourable leader in the country.

sections.heading: Strange Behaviour Causes Anxieties
paras: The king’s buffoon who was in his village came to know of this and started marching fast toward tirmiz. On the way two of his horses died because of their high speed and continuous running. After searching Tirmiz he was completely exhausted, stuck in dust; and without any washing straight away went to the king’s office at an in-appropriate time of the king and enquired about him. All the officials were surprised and started talking about this strange behaviour and the king also was upset upon receiving information of his arrival. People in the city also came to know of this and they were also upset fearing that some calamity has come about. They were afraid that there might be some enemy to attack them; or some other unexpected, hidden trouble has come about, that the buffoon came in such haste and lost two costly horses due to high speed and long sun. people collected at the king’s palace to know as to why the buffoon was in such a hurry. The entire city of Tirmiz was in great anxiety for the buffoon’s extra-ordinary hurry, hardship and trouble. There was so much tension that someone was beating upon his thighs in fear and another suspected that great troubles would come. Everyone lamented in fear, expecting calamities and trials. Every heart had such hundreds of suspicions as to what such a terrible event occurred, that the buffoon came over clothes full of dust and sought for entry into the royal court.

The buffoon sought for permission and the kind instantly permitted him, and the buffoon fell down before the king in adoration in extreme fear and the king asked him as to what happened he would keep his finger on his lips directing him to keep quiet. Because of this, the suspicion of everyone increased further and all the more surprised. The buffoon then said in gestures: “O generous king, give me some time so that I may bring back my breaths under control and coolness; so that I may compose all my thoughts and feelings as I am caught in very strange circumstances.” The king waited for some time with bitter throat and mouth with still more suspicions and fears, as he had never seen the buffoon like this at any time earlier, as none was better than this happy-go-lucky pleasing-companion with him.

sections.heading: Anxiety Causes Uncertain Fears
paras: He always used to cut jokes and narrate funny stories making the king heartily laugh and be happy. He used to make the company so full of laughter that the king would have uncontrollable laughter compelling to hold his belly with both hands. Sweat used to pour out because of too much laughing and many a times he used to fall down on his face while laughing. The king was astonished as to what happened to this fellow, that he was pale-faced and bitter in appearance keeping his finger on his lips, even gesturing to the king to keep quite. Doubts upon doubts and fears upon fears came in the king’s minds as to what great calamity was about to fall. He started suspecting that khwarizan shah, the king of Samarqand, of whom the king was very much afraid might have made some programme to attack his country and the buffoon had come to know of this. He considered khwarizan Shah to be very cruel. His capital was Samarqand, and he was supported and advised by a very clever and wise minister. Khwarizan Shah had killed all the king’s around his country by violent attacks or treacherous designs. This king of Tirmiz was under doubts about khwarizan Shah and the buffoon’s strange behaivour increased his doubt. So, he said to the buffoon: “Be fast to say as to what happened. What is the reason for so much of your anxiety and fear?

sections.heading: False Bubble Bursts Like Imposters
paras: The buffoon said: “I came to know in my village that the king has caused announcement at every junction of the highways that he wanted such a person who would run to Samarqand in three days and that he would be granted treasures and wealth, upon getting satisfied with the information brought by him. Therefore, I came running fast to tell your majesty that I do not have such strength to do so. There cannot be such fastness and alertness from a man like me and therefore, your majesty may not expect such efforts from me.”

The king said: “Fie upon your fastness! Two hundred doubts and speculations have come about in the city! Just for saying this much, you fool, you have set fire to the meadows and the grass therein! Like those hollow drum beaters and carriers of ostentations flags who proclaim that they are the leaders in faqr (voluntary destitution) and annihilation in God. They go on boasting about their master ship of knowledge in the world projecting themselves as great as Bayazid Bistami. They have made themselves as self-self-made wayfarers in the path of God and started institutions of non-sensical teachings, proclaiming themselves as having attained what all saints can attain with great efforts and guidance

sections.heading: One Side Preparation 344
paras: “They are like a would-be son-in-law whose house is full of marriage activities. When the in-laws are totally unaware of this. There was a great enthusiasm that half of the job was already finished and all that requires to be done from our side has been done. We have cleaned and whitewashed our houses and we are quite contented, settled and pleased. While this was their preparation and readiness, not a single message came from the other side. Not even a small bird came from there to sit upon their terrace. No information came from the other side at all inspite of all these preparations? If someone were to ask whether any message came from the bride’s side in answer to any of your messages, they would say: No! And it is not necessary as the other side is well aware of our affairs. There is a way from our heart to theirs.

The situation of a treacherous master is exactly like this. There are a hundred hidden and clear signals from him, but nothing comes about because there are curtains before these fellows. Had they been sincere in their approach, definitely messages would have come.”

sections.heading: Foolishness Results in Disaster
paras: Now let us go to the story of that foolish buffoon that, for no good reasons he invited troubles for himself. The minister addressed the king: “O pillar of truth, hear a suggestion from this humble servant. The buffoon has come from his village for some personal work. Having come here he has changed his object and is worried about it. He is playing a trick to get rid of some problem through this polished and painted design of a special kind of buffoonery. He is showing the scabbard but hiding the sword. He is required to be squeezed the spill out as to what he wants. He has shown the wrappers and hidden the dagger. He should be certainly by tightened until and unless you crush the apricot or pistachios, it will not show either its pulp or it its oil. Please do not give ears to his evading tactics but look at his colour and his trembling’s. God has said that the symbols of truth and falsehood can be seen from the face: On their faces are their marks: siimaahum fii wujuuhihim: (Fath: 48: 29). Marks of the face are the tale bearers. What he is expressing by words is different from what is his mind. This fellow is mixed up with mischief.”

The buffoons told the minister in an angry loud voice: “Sir, do not try to get this poor man killed. Many doubts and thoughts come into the heart, which are not true and correct. O Minister, God has said: suspicion in some cases is a sin: inna ba ‘adagha zhanni ith(s)mun (Hujurat: 49: 12) causing trouble to anyone and in particular to a poor man, is not right. The king certainly catches hold of a person who causes troubles. how can he catch hold of one who makes him laugh.”

sections.heading: Impacts of Truth, Foolish Men and Falsehood
paras: The minister’s suggestion caught the mind of the king and became one to clarify falsehood and treachery. He ordered that the buffoon be taken to the prison and regard be shown to his pleadings and falsities. Beat him as you beat upon empty drum which has nothing inside so that, just as the drum produces sounds, he may also speak out. Because a drum is both empty and full at the same time. Its sound informs us of all its contents and secrets. So that with these beatings the buffoon is compelled to speak of his secret to the fullest of our satisfaction as truth is always satisfying. Truth is always bright and satisfying. Hearts do not get convinced with falsehood. Falsehood is like a scrap and heart is like the mouth. A scrap can never remain hidden in the mouth. So long as it is there in the mouth, mouth goes on wobbling the tongue within until with proper application of wisdom it comes out. In particular when another scrap falls into the eye, the eye starts shedding tears, opening and shutting until it comes out. We shall also kick this scrap so that our mouth and the eye get rid of it.”

sections.heading: Impacts of Truth, Foolish Men and Falsehood
paras: The buffoon said to the king: “O king do not be in haste. Do not injure your dignified and kind face that always pardons. Why is there so much of haste in punishing? I am not flying away. I am within your control. The punishment that is for God’s sake should not be given in haste. Only one who punishes with emotions and temporary anger rushes to do so fearing that consonance with the offense may not come about. He further fears that development of consonance may chase away anger and his mood to take revenge and enjoy its pleasure may not be lost. One without real hunger tries to eat faster fearing that the pleasure of eating will be lost. In fact, this fearful hunger itself is a sickness. it is better to wait for some time to eat even in the case of real hunger so that the food may get digested without extra efforts.

sections.heading: Give Charity to Avoid Calamity
paras: “You are trying to kill me to chase away some oncoming calamity as you think that I am hiding something which upon becoming known might keep the trouble away. You feel that by getting rid of me you can plug the hole through which the trouble comes. But you should know that the fate ordained by God comes through many holes. It will come through other holes if it is destined to come. The method of getting rid of trouble is not by cruelty but it is through goodness, forgiveness and benevolence. The noble Prophet has said that charity chases away calamity. Therefore, you should treat your sicknesses with charity. Getting a poor man tortured is not charity. It amounts to blinding the eye that observes and decides rightly.”

sections.heading: Nothing Is Good or Bad in Itself
paras: The kind said: “Goodness and occasions to be good are definitely better only when done at the appropriate time. If you place the king in the place of the rook on the chessboard it will be utter foolishness. So also keeping the bishop in the king’s chamber. Shari‘at (law) provides both punishment and mercy. The place for the king is the presiding chair and of the horse is the gate. Equity is in keeping the appropriate thing at the appropriate place and cruelty is misplacing these things. It is justice and equity t ogive water to trees and giving it to thorns is cruelty. All that is created by God is not without purpose including wrath and self-control, and advice and treachery. Nothing is absolutely good, and nothing is absolutely bad. Gains and losses of all things are according to situations. Nothing is bad in itself nor are its impacts. Everything has a different situation for its utility and non-use. Therefore, it becomes necessary to know as to what is good and at what time and otherwise.

sections.heading: Injury: Good in Circumstances
paras: “At times a chastisement of a poor man is better than providing him with bread and sweets, as sweets produce escessive bile; and a slap on his face eliminates his ill manners. A poor fellow would be foolishly doing an act which might put him to death. A slap on his face might protect him from the greater trouble of death. A slap is given on the face is actually ill manners just as beatings are given to a blanket to remove the dust from it. Kings have pleasurable courts for the sincere advisers and also prisons for the ruffians. When a wound is in need of surgery, it should be done, mere application of ointment on it will further damage it to such an extent that it will destroy the flesh underneath it. There is little gain in the application of ointment but ultimately resulting in a fifty-times greater damage. Ointment in such a case will bring so much injury as to go lower and deeper into flesh ultimately resulting in death.”

sections.heading: Importance of Consultation
paras: The buffoon further said: “I do not pray to you to leave me free, but only to make proper enquires. I stress that the door of patience and self-control should not be shut. Please have patience and think over for some days. If after substantial self-control and patience, you come tot the level of full certainty, you may certainly punish me. Why should there be an about turn when there is scope for walking straight? Please have consultation with the noble people as the prophet was advised by God to: consult them in affairs of moment: wa shaawir hum fil amr (Al-Imran: 3: 159). It is also said about the noble people that their affairs are with mutual consultation: wa amruhum shuuraa bainahum: (Shuuraa: 42: 38). This consultation is required for the reason that acts upon it do not generally go wrong. Suggestions provide a light coming from twenty lamps. Twenty lamps instead of one, are certainly brighter. There is a possibility that one of those lamps might be one with the light of instructions directly from the spiritual world.
Search for the wise fortunate

“God has kept some of His favoured servants hidden behind curtain and made both those of high level mixed up with the lowly; and it is very difficult for us to differentiate between them. That is why God has also said: travel through the earth: “siiruu fil ardh” in many places in the Quran to search for good fortune and provisions, test and compare them with each other. Search for that wisdom in the gatherings of the wise, which the noble Prophet had, as that alone is his inheritance, with which he used to see all things before and behind as also that were apparent and hidden.

sections.heading: Monastic Life: Prohibited by the Prophet
paras: “Search for that sight among the various sights the details of which cannot be explained here. It is for this reason that the great grand Prophet has prohibited monastic life and seclusion in hills and mountains, so that contacts with such wise men may not cease to exist. Contacts with them provide insight and the alchemy of life which would convert baser things into precious gold. Among your nobles there is one who is the noblest, upon whose forehead is inscribed the seal of approval of royal decree of God. He is unrecognisable and hidden but his prayers are always positively accepted. All the great among the jinn’s and men cannot be equal to him. The sweet or sour opinion of anyone against him is of no worth before God, as God says about him: when we have ourselves elevated him to high level, all excuses and disputations about him are completely lifted away from him. To search for any other opinion other than his is of no use and worth just as there is no scope for speculations as to what direction is the qibla (centre of muslim prayers) when one is standing right before it. Therefore, stay away from all speculations as the centre of attraction and settlement thereat is right before you. even a slight deviation from this qibla will take you away from it making you a voluntary free servant of others. If you remain thankless to the one who grants you the capacity to differentiate and discriminate between things, the capacity to know the truth goes away from you. if you want to collect goodness from them like collecting wheat from the harvest, you should not turn your face away from the supporters and co-ordinators even for a moment. Once you go away from a good companion, inevitably bad companions will fill up the gap.”

chapters.title: Benefits of Togetherness
chapters.subtitle: Story of the connection between the mouse and the frog with their legs with a thread; and the lifting of the mouse by a crow high above the ground and the frog’s getting suspended in air; and its crying upon its going away from a species of its own and getting involved with another species

paras: It so happened that on the bank of a stream a mouse and a frog came together and became friends. Both used to meet together at regular timings in the morning time. They used to play the dice of heart with each other and empty their hearts of unwanted thoughts. Upon meeting with each other, their hearts were highly pleased by speaking and hearing of each other’s affairs. They used to speak of each other’s secrets with sounds and even without sounds. They knew well the meaning of the statement that togetherness is benevolent. Inspite of each of them devoted to oneself in pride and self-identity, when coming together, they used to speak of the personal experiences of their past days.

sections.heading: Impacts of Friends and Guides
paras: Rising of the enthusiasm to talk is a proof of friendship, and stoppage of talks is due to lack of concern for each other. A heart that has seen the beloved cannot remain constricted. A bulbul upon seeing the flower cannot remain silent. A friend fish, with the impacts of the soul of H. Khizr got back to life and went past swimming into the sea. When a friend sits face to face with his friend, lakhs of written tablets of the heart appear before him. When a disciple sits before the master, the master’s forehead appears like the protected tablet of God (Lowh-i-Mahfooz) spelling out the secrets of both the worlds. A saint is a guide of the path of spiritual journey. That is what the noble Prophet said about his companions that they are like stars, which show the path of destination in the deserts and oceans. Therefore, while traversing the spiritual journey, keep your eyes set upon the guide who is your star. Keep your eyes in constant observation of his face and hear him with full attention and do not spread dust before him with arguments and discussions, because the star gets covered up with dust. A constantly observing eye is always better than a slippery tongue, so that the saint may speak out what comes to him through godly inspiration. Godly inspiration settles down the dust of discussion and arguments stopping it from flowing any more.

sections.heading: Impacts of Godly Inspriations
paras: When H. Adam became the exponent of inspired knowledge and love, his talking ability spread out the product of: ‘He taught Adam the nature of all things’: wa ‘allama Adama al-asmaa‘a kullahaa: (Baqara: 2: 31). He gave the name to everything as per its nature. His tongue got the supply of water from the books of knowledge. Upon his seeing of things, his tongue was telling about the nature and quality of all things as they actually possessed. Names given by him were appropriate to them according to their qualities. He did not name a coward as lion. H. Nuh went on the true path for nine hundred years and spoke of an entirely new matter on each day. His lips got their strength to talk from strength of hearts, though he had not read and learnt from any great books like Risala of Imam Qushiiri and Qutul Qutub of Abu Talib Makki. He had not acquired the capacity to teach by reading the books and the commentaries. The source of all his knowledge was the fountain of revelations and the commentaries by the soul. The wine that flows from this source is such that even if a dumb drinks it, fountain of words starts flowing from his mouth.

A just born baby becomes wise and lucid and starts talking of highly elevated matters as Jesus Christ did. It is from this wine that H. Dawood learnt to sing sweet sonnets and songs in hundreds of numbers. Their influence was such that all the birds gave up their chirping and joined him as his accompaniments and in chorus. There is no wonder in the birds getting intoxicated with his tunes when even hard and lifeless iron would hear the sounds of his hands. Fast wind that became murderous for the people of ‘Aad, became a carrier for H. Sulaiman, which would carry the throne of this king upon its head covering the distance of one mouth’s journey in the morning and evening on all days. It was not only a carrier, but also a spy to hear the talks of the far away persons, and thereafter carry the information to the ears of that king submitting to him that: “so and so said, such and such, at such and such time, O fortunate king!”

chapters.title: Lover and Beloved Are One and the Same
chapters.subtitle: Suggestion of the mouse to the frog: “I cannot come to meet you when you are in water. There should be some means to inform you of my coming when I come on the riverbank. And you may inform me of your coming to my house which is in a dry place.”

paras: There is no end to the discussion on the wine of the love of God. Let us go to what the mouse said to the frog. It said: “O wise and sensible friend! Many a times I feel like telling you of some hidden matters when you would be here and there in water. I give a call to you from the riverbank, but you do not hear the voice of your lover while sunk in water. O brave one! In such a situation I cannot have the pleasure of talking to you.

sections.heading: Love of Common People and Devotees
paras: Common people address to God in their five time daily prayers, but lovers of God remain steadfast to their prayer always: Hum ‘alaa salaatihim daa‘imuun (Ma‘aarij: 70: 23). Their intoxication from the head cannot go in five times prayer as they have five lakh intoxicated heads within them. They have thousands of secrets that they have to share with God. Meeting the beloved on alternate days is not meant for them, as being truly devoted to God alone, their thirst to too great to be quenched in limited timings. Fishes do not have alternate and interrupted swims. They continuingly swim, because their souls do not have connection with anything other than water. Frightening situations in water are just like a gulp of water for the intoxications of the fishes. A moment of separation of the lover from the beloved is like one year. Separation for one year from the beloved can only be a passing thought for him.

sections.heading: Beloved Also Searches for Lovers
paras: Lover is thirsty and always in search of the beloved who is also thirsty and is in search of the lover. The situation of the lover and beloved is like that of day and night which are continuingly after each other. Day is in love with night and highly disturbed without it. Rather, if you keenly think over, you will see that the night is in greater love with the day. Both of them are after each other without even a moments reluctance. Both cannot remain at peace without the other even for a moment. One catches the feet of te other, and the other catches the ear of the other. One is semiconscious of the other and the other is fully unconscious of the one. Whatever is there in the heart of the lover is there in the heart of the beloved also. The heart of the Arabian beloved, ‘Azra also had a place for wamiq her lover, all the time. There is nothing in the heart of the Lover other than the beloved, and between them also there is nothing to separate them, not even a reason for separation. Both are like two bells hanging on the camel’s neck. Both ring simultaneously. There is no scope for these bells to ring at different times. So also, for the lover and beloved to love each other alternately. If a lover is told to think of the beloved or meet on alternate days, it means like telling a person to befriend himself on alternate days.

sections.heading: Man’s Love for God
paras: This unity and oneness applies also to man’s love with God. This is not unity and oneness that can be rationally understood. It comes to be known only upon one’s death. The only exception is of one, who has died during lifetime itself carrying all his possessions to God. That is: one who has attained the state of annihilation in God. If the understanding of this was possible through reasoning, there would be no need for the entanglement of oneself in constant meditation and contemplation and crushing of one’s desires for peace and comfort, as meditation and contemplation are tortures to the mind. This has been ordained by the king full of mercy, who is provider of comforts to all, yet He ordains to undergo this torture through crushing of the self. The object is to create the taste of love so as to make one know the meaning of unity and oneness in love.

chapters.title: Humble Submissions of the Lovers
chapters.subtitle: Persistence of the mouse in humility to seek connection with the water frog

paras: The mouse continued: “O my dear kind friend! I do not have rest for a moment without you. you are the light, warmth and possession of mine. You alone are my peace of mind, sleep at night and my happiness. It will be your great grace if you provide pleasures to me and remember me in your mind at every moment. You have provided me with your presence and thoughts, day in and day out, and in the pleasant afternoons. Yet I am not fully satisfied with this. I have become a different type of creature due to my love for you. I suffer from hundreds of different kinds of thirst, and each has a never quenchable hunger. Yet, you appear to be not aware of my sorrows of separation from you. please give the charity of the recognition of love with concern for this poor person.

sections.heading: Love Shifts from Creatures to God
paras: I pray to God: “I am an uncultured, worthless beggar, but your kindness is general, and for all, and above all. Your general benevolences do not discriminate between the worthy and unworthy. Hot bright sun puts its impacts upon dirty things but does not incur any loss and deficiency. It dries up foul and filthy dung and makes it worthy of use in the furnace and brightens it so much to cause of the baths. Filth becomes decorative when the sun casts its spell upon it. Not only this, sun even warms up the earth’s belly and swallows the filth on it and converts it into manure; and a part of itself to create scope for plants to grow and develop. In similar manner, God’s generosity also wipes off the sins. And fills up the clayish body of man with light. This is how, God wipes off the sins and fills their place with fresh grants. This makes the clay of man’s body worthy. This is how God shows His mercy upon His servants.

sections.heading: Special Gifts to the Virtuous
paras: “This is what the sun also does that it converts filth into sweet smelling colourful plants and flowers. When this is what is done by the sun, think of what all God does with the obedient and sincere servants. When the sinful are treated so well, imagine what all the virtuous people get from Him. He gives those gifts which are not seen by any eye, which cannot be explained by the tongue and words. O my God! You may tell me as to of what level I am. Brighten may days with good manners. Do not look at my ugliness and hateable worth as I am full of poison like the hilly snake. I am bad in every respect, and I have only undeniable conduct. But how can I become a flower when I have been made as a thorn. You may give beauty and pleasantness to the thorn and grant the beauty of peacock to this poisonous snake. I am at the highest level of viscousness and your grace is at the highest level of excellence and grants. Provide the needs of this person at the highest level of viciousness, with his requirements from your highest level of graces, just as you have granted straightness and tallness to the cypress tree.

sections.heading: Pleadings Shift to Frog
paras: “So also, my dear frog: you may consider that your grace will cry upon my death for losing one to whom benevolence could be shown. This is inspite of the fact that you are generous, on your own. Whether there is someone to show grace or not, you go on showing grace. You will sit near my grave for a long-time shedding tears of love for me. You will cry upon my separation from you and will not shut your eyes from the lowly conditions of my wretchedness. Instead of doing that after death, do a little of it now itself and put the ring of my slavery to you in my earlobe now itself, without making any announcement of it, as I am already your slave. What you intend to speak to the mud of my grave may be sprinkled upon my feelings and senses now itself. Extend your protective hand in my present state of distress and replace my sorrows with joys.

chapters.title: Right Now, Is Better Than Later
chapters.subtitle: Entreating of the mouse with the frog, not to plead excuses and to postpone the payment of its instant needs as delaying is full of troubles. A sufi is a child of time and obedient to time; and the dependant child never leaves the hand of the father. The loving father is like a kind sufi who is like time itself and instantly protects the child without postponing his needs. He keeps the child so engaged in the pasture of his needs. He never waits for the on coming of needs for his son just as others would do for others. He has no arguments of predestination and free will with regard to his child’s upkeep. So also, he is not an avoider of responsibility by giving excuses and not the one to leave matters to fate. There is no morning and evening for God. God has no past and future, beginning and end. There is no question of Adam preceding and Dajjal succeeding for Him as these occasions come within the zone of partial wisdom. There are no such occasions for the human soul also in the spaceless and timeless world. Every time is the same for Him. So also, for the father for his child. He acts at the spur of the moment without caring for the differences of time. This is so with God Who is one and only which is easy to understand. And bringing someone along with Him is simply deniable. But God’s oneness is the reality

sections.heading: [Read the Above Caption Again and Again to Digest the Points. They Are Oceans of Meanings — Translator]
paras: A rich man gave a silver coin to a sufi saying: “your feet are the resting place of my soul! You want to take a dirham on this day, or I shall give you three dirhams tomorrow morning.” The sufi said: “I am more agreeable for a single dirham today, rather than for a hundred tomorrow. Not only a grant! Even an instant slap on the face today is better than a gift tomorrow. Now, I have submitted myself before you. better give me the cash. I would even prefer a slap on my face from your hand as I am in love with your slap. O pleasure giver of the life and the world, you are better instantly than delayed! Do not hide your moonlike face from the travellers like me at night. O flowing water: do not turn away yourself from the stream, because with the impact of flowing water, banks of stream smiles and flowering plants raise their head. When you see green grass dancing on the banks of the river, you may conclude from a distance that there is water flowing in it. That is what the creator of the world has said: There are signs on the faces: siimaahum fi wujuuhihim: (Fath: 49: 29). That is why, greenery is the talebearer of rain. No one sees when the rain falls at night as every man and his breaths are in sleep, but they find its markings in the morning. The freshness of every beautiful garden is an evidence of the falling of the rain whether people see it or not.

chapters.title: Efforts, Successes, Failures: All from God
chapters.subtitle: Return to the story of the mouse and water frog

paras: The mouse continued to say: “O my brother I belong to mud, and you belong to water. But you are a king of grace and grants. In your grant, you may do so much as to allow me to come to your attendance whenever I so wish. I call upon you from the bank of the stream without expecting any response from you. only that much I can do, because entrance into water is prohibited for me, as my body is entirely made of mud. arrange for a messenger or some signal to inform you of my coming to you.”

sections.heading: Body Drags and Holds the Soul
paras: They discussed much on this point and decided that they should take a long string so that with its pulling the need of meeting may become known. One end of it must be tied to the leg of one and the other end tied to the leg of the another, so that both may thus remain connected with each other just as the body and soul are connected. Body is like a string for the feet of the soul, which drags down the soul from the heavens towards the earth. The frog of life lies unconscious in the eater of sleep-in great contentment upon getting disconnected with the body of the mouse. The mouse of the body, yet again drags the soul of frog through the string causing many bitterness’s to the soul. Had there been no dragging by the polluted mind of the body of the mouse, the frog as soul would have enjoyed a lot in water of sleep. This is the case of the connection between the body and soul in this world when you sleep and wake up alternatively. You will hear about its details and about the final and never-ending-sleep of death, from the creator of the world and grantor of light of the sun.

sections.heading: Forewarnings About Calamities
paras: The mouse told the frog: “I have one end of the string at my leg and you may have the other end at your leg, so that when I pull my leg, the other end at your leg will inform you of my calling. This suggestion appeared very bitter to the frog as it thought that this mean fellow was trying to trap me in a knot of the string. Such fears that come into the hearts of good people are not without some base. Do not consider such an inner intellect as senseless suspicion, as the light of the heart reorganises them by looking at the protected tablet (laoh-e-mahfooz). A faithful person gets such hints about the oncoming of troubles well in advance. Many animals also get such cautions and warnings. The elephants had such reluctance while marching toward ka‘aba inspite of the their drivers pressing them and driving them hard to move forward, as narrated in the surat: ‘Elephant: Alfiil in the Quran (Surat: 105). Their legs were not moving toward the ka‘aba inspite of receiving too many kicks. You may say that their legs dried up and their lives came to end. But that was not so, when they turned in the opposite direction towards Yemen, the bold elephants, used to lift their legs with all enthusiasm and run fast. the sense of the elephant had come to know of the hidden calamity. When this is the case of the elephants you may consider what would be the sensibility of a saintly fried of God about the events to occur later.

sections.heading: H. Yaqub’s Hesitation
paras: This has happened in the case of prophet Yaqub in the affairs of H. Yusuf and his brothers. His brothers sought permission from H. Yaqub to take Yusuf for some time toward the forest. All of them told him not to fear of any loss and to give them leave for a day or two. They asked him as to: “why he does not consider them as his guards and why he hesitates to leave Yusuf in the company of his guards. We want to take him toward the greed fields to play. We are totally sincere and trustworthy in this regard.” H. Yaqub said: “I know it very well that Yusuf going away from me would result in the increase of my sorrows and sickness. My heart never tells a lie, as it has its connections with the light of ‘arsh.” (Region beyond space).

sections.heading: Fate Defeats Fore Warnings
paras: That was a perfect argument about the oncoming mischief. But he could not do anything to avert it as the oncoming events were predestined by God. Inspite of such a perfect signal, he was left helpless, as there was another design of God behind it. It is not strange that a blind man falls into the well. But it is very strange that one who has a good sight also falls down into the well. There are many kinds of catches and controls of fate made by God. Whatever that God wishes happens: God does what He wills: Yaf ‘alullaahu maa yashaa’: (Ibrahim: 14: 27). Our hearts know about His designs and also do not know, when fate intervenes, our firm decision falls into doubts. Our hard iron-like-heart becomes soft like wax and starts telling us to yield to whatever that has to happen and not to hold decision firmly anymore. It starts pleading of all inabilities and surrenders entirely to fate. It tightens itself with the rope provided by fate. When a strong-headed yields in this manner and feels defeated by fate, he does not consider it as defeat by considers but as a trial to assess whether he prefers himself or develops consonance with God’s wish.

sections.heading: Continuing Flow from ‘Adam to the World
paras: This submission to fate and troubles on his part protects him from a hundred other troubles. getting down in this manner results in his upliftment to many other higher levels. This relieves him of the wine of lowly tastes and lowly intoxications. Ultimately he becomes a master, hard in life, getting the scope to take a long jump from the slavery of the world to attain full freedom. He becomes highly intoxicated of the everlasting wine and becomes rid of worldly connections and gets relief. He gets rid of the weak, untested common beliefs, with which the thoughts and sights of the common folk are filled up. Such people with these untested beliefs and lack of knowledge cannot do anything in life surrounded by the low and high tidal movements of this invisible ocean of predestination and free will. What ever materials and buildings found in this world have come from that non-material world (‘adam). Even such powers like sovereignty, kingdom and ministries. From that empty, barren ‘adam, hordes and hordes of those intoxicated with enthusiasm are continuingly entering into this visible, material world, every day and night.

sections.heading: Early Occupants Replaced by Later Arrivals
paras: These people come down and occupy our homes and replace us making announcements that their term has arrived. They have come and others should vacate and go away. You may see that when the son opens his eyes of wisdom, he sees that his father has carried and kept his materials upon the sky and occupies the father’s place. This is a highway on which there are caravans and caravans on the march from one side and there are oncoming batches of new arrivals. If you think over, you will see that we are on the walk even when we are sitting and resting in one place and do not see the place toward which we are walking, which is different and invisible to us. Whatever you are doing now is not for the time being alone, but by keeping the future also in view. A man on journey is walking and facing towards the destination which is yet to come but he is to reach later. This is like the thoughts that come to the heart from behind the curtains one after another, without getting tired, in the form of armies and battalions.

sections.heading: All Thoughts Arise from One Centre
paras: Just think over: if these thoughts are not from one centre, why they come over to the same heart one after one. There is one place to start with and one place of end at. These thoughts of ours in the farm of armies after armies come to the fountain of the heart to quench its thirst. They fill up their pots and walk away. Some of them are visible, understandable and clear, and some are hidden and beyond comprehension. Consider these thoughts as the stars of the heaven which revolve in the orbits of other heavens. You see some of them as auspicious and be thankful for his and become generous to give preference to the needs of others. And when you see them as inauspicious, you may perform repentance, seek forgiveness of some forgotten sins and give charity to avoid their ill-effects.

sections.heading: God Alone Causes Means for Good Effects
paras: What are we and who are we to deal with them, O master of ours! We may repent and give charity to please ourselves and the real grant is only from You. You may be kind enough to reverse the ill-effects and convert the causes of adversity into those of prosperity. Brighten our souls with the light of Your moon, as our souls have become dark with the moon’s entering into the zone of eclipsing. With the same light of your moon, you may brighten our souls, which have become dark due to the sickness of our heart. Relieve my soul of the impacts of vicious thoughts, doubts and suspicions. Disconnect the well of these thoughts with the trouble-giving-rope so that they may not come out of their source, so that my heart, with the impacts of your kindness may sprout out feathers and fly away from the clutches of the body made of mud and water. You may grant freedom. Like the king of Egypt who accepted the pleadings of H. Yasuf from the prison and set him free. Like the king of Egypt, who was friendly and faithful to promises, you may consider that the oppressed Yusuf is in your prison. But you only caused the freedom of Yusuf by making the king of Egypt see a strange dream, difficult to interpret, which only Yusuf could do. The same thing may be done for me also, my Lord as you love those who do good: Inna Allah yuhibbul muhsiniin: (Baqara: 2: 195)

You had shown the king of Egypt in his dream that seven weak and famished cows were eating seven fat and healthy cows. And also, seven ugly withered and dry ears of corn were grazing upon seven fresh and green ears of corn. The impact of this dream caused famine in Egypt. But my king, you may keep me safe from such impacts. I am like Yusuf in Your prison.

sections.heading: Effects of Passions
paras: Relieve me from this and also from the hands of women just as You had done to Yusuf. Lust of women bring about such effects that my mother’s lust pulled me and brought me down from ‘arsh (region beyond space), which was my original place. I feel down from that world of perfection into the prison of the womb of my mother without any willing from my side. Women’s planning and plotting are very great that they bring the soul from ‘arsh down to this shattered home. My first decline started with woman, when I fell down from the state of soul to state of body. the first fall was caused by woman which was a spiritual fall when I was given a physical body, again by a woman, my mother.

Hear this lamentation of Yusuf upon his falling upside down and pity him or have pity upon that Yaqub, full of love for him. I do not know whether I should grieve upon Yusuf’s brothers away from his motherhood or upon the women of Egypt who sent him to the prison. Women have also brought us down from the paradise as Adam was brought down. In both cases, it is the feelings of jealousy and of sexual passions that have put me into losses. For this reason, I am dried up like the leaves of the autumn season by eating the grain of wheat of the paradise of the spring season.

sections.heading: Protection from Evil Eye
paras: When I looked at Your concern and grace, and heard of your message of peace and security, I was afraid that an evil eye may fall on them and to avert them, I took out my black gram to burn it on fire so that its smoke may ward off the effects of the evil eye. But my black gram itself was afflicted with the evil eye. Therefore, there is no way of warding off of the evil impacts. It is only Your eyes full of Your own intoxicating qualities that can ward off the evil eye from back and front, and of all sides. O my king! Your noble eyes only can defeat and destroy the evil effects of the evil eye. That alone is the best treatment for it. Rather from Your eyes possess the alchemy that can change the evil eye into the blessing eye.

sections.heading: God and His Friends Go Together
paras: The eyes of the king struck so hard upon the eyes of the falcon of the heart that they become very strong and courageous to go beyond normally expected regions. So much of boldness was received by the falcon’s eyes that, this royal falcon could be caught by none other than the king’s lion in the form of the thoughts of the next life. What after all, is this lion? Rather this royal falcon of thoughts and meanings becomes Your own prey and you become his prey. This is what happens to the real friends of God, whose only ambition is life is to go with God and God also wants to go with them. When the falcon of their soul whistles from inside the pasture land of their hearts, it gives the message: I do not love that set: La uhibbul ‘afilina: (An‘aam: 6: 76), as Prophet Ibrahim had announced when the stars, moon and sun set which were initially taken by him as God in a step by step manner. The falcon of the heart of the saints that flies purely for Your sake receives the eyesight from Your never-ending grants. The nose got its smelling quality and the ears their hearing capacity only from You. so also, all senses are provided their qualities to different organs by You. whatever sensibility that You grant through the paths of the hidden world, does not get reduced in strength due to passage of time into old age, or upon death. You are the Master of all sovereignty: Malikul Mulk: (Aal Imraan: 3: 26). You give what ever You wish to whomsoever You wish, so that this sensibility given by You may lord over all other sensibilities.
Therefore, O reader, put your efforts so that your sensibility may go up, so that the job of the sensibility may go further above it.

chapters.title: Special Qualities of Special Persons
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of king Mahmud’s falling among a group of thieves on a night and telling them that he was also one among them; and getting informed about their affairs

paras: One night, Sultan Mahmud was roaming alone when he happened to fall into a group of thieves. They asked him: “tell us O honest one, as to who you are? The sultan said: “O members of the treacherous group! Let everyone speak of the matter of his instinctual expertise, so that he may keep informed his friends of his special experiences.”

One of them said: “O claimants of extraordinary qualities! I have such instinctual power in my ears that I can recognise what the dog says through its barking sound.” The others said: “you are worth two-sixtieth part of a dinar,” (which is not such a great value). Another thief said: “O Group of the worshippers of wealth: My great quality is in my eyes. Whomsoever I see in the darkness of the night, I can recognise in the light of the day without any doubt.” Another said: “My speciality is in my arms. I can break the wall with a blow of my hand.”

sections.heading: Special Qualities of Nose
paras: Another said: “My speciality is in my nose; I can smell the mud and find out the hidden things under it. It is for this reason that the noble Prophet has said that people are like the mines of gold and silver. I can find out from a heap of mud as to what wealth it contains and in how much quantity. There are mines which contain uncountable gold and the are mines the contents of which do not meat even the cost of digging. I can smell mud like Majnun and find out the place to which Laila has reached in her walk. I can smell every garment whether it is worn by one like H. Yusuf or Satan. My nose has received a part of the quality of the sharpness of smelling of the Prophet with which smell the fragrance of far-off Yemen. I can smell the mud that is in the neighbour hood of gold or the mud that has nothing in it but shear waste.”

sections.heading: Prophet’s Loop to Climb Up
paras: Another said: “My quality is in my hands that I can throw a loop on the top of a hill. At how much ever height the terrace of the palace may be, the loop thrown by me goes and strongly holds the parapet. It is like the noble Prophet Muhammad whose soul threw up its loop so high that it went up to the heavens. It was so strong that it took him toward the great fortune and thrown of God. God told him: “O the one to throw his loop upon the place of prostration of God (baital ma‘muur), you did not throw it but God threw it: Maaramaita iz ramaita walaakeinnallaaha ramaa: (Anfaal: 8: 17).” This is the highest point up to much man’s mind knowledge and spirit can reach.

After that the group of thieves asked Sultan Mahmood as to what special quality he has? The sultan said: “My great quality is in my beard that I get the criminals freed from punishments. When the criminals are handed over to the hangmen and upon this, if my beard shakes head, they are let free. When I shake my head in pity, resulting in the shaking of my beard, the criminals are instantly pardoned and let free.” The thieves said: “you are our great leader and reliever like the saint (Qutub) who is like the axis upon which the earth rotates. On our difficult day you will become the cause of our relief.”

sections.heading: All Talents Put to Use
paras: After this, they all went out toward the prosperous palace of the prosperous king. When a dog barked from their right side, one thief said: “the dog says that the king is also with you. “The other fellow smelt a heap of mud and said: “this is the mud of the fallen house of a widow.” Then the expert is throwing loop threw the loop so well that it reached the other side of the fort wall. Upon smelling the mud, the previous fellow said: “this smells of the unmatchable treasure of the king.” The fourth fellow with strong hands broke down the walls of the treasury with his hands and took them all to the treasure. They all looted plenty of gold, jewels and fabrics intervened with gold and silver threads, and hid them in a different place. The king had identified all of them and found out their place of hiding and the path toward it. He hid himself from them all and returned to his palace and narrated about all events of the night to the office. There upon the police went after them and brought them to the office. They were all shivering out for the fear of their lives.

sections.heading: King Recognised by Thief
paras: They were all brought before the king’s throne who was a friend of theirs during the night like the moon. The fellow who had the talent of identifying during daytime anyone seen by him in the darkness of night, recognised the king. He looked the king at the throne and whispered: he was our companion during the last night and moved along with us. All though he is the one who has such special qualities in his beard. he had the quality of tracing us out and getting us caught.” His eyes certainly recognised the king, with certainty and he opened his mouth and said loudly: “Just as God who is with you wheresoever you may be: wa huwa ma‘akum aina maa kuntum: (Hadiid: 51: 4), the king was with us. He saw all our acts came to know of all our secrets. My eyes found him out at hight and recognised his moon-like face and fell in love with it. I shall make a claim upon him for my people, as such a person never turns his face from those known to him.”

sections.heading: Great Sharpness of the Prophet’s Eyes
paras: Consider the eyes of the gnostic and saints as the peace-givers of both the worlds as every ruler seeks support from them. And H. Muhammad is intercessor for all the blots of men as his eyes saw nothing other than God. His eyes never sweverved, nor did they go wrong: Maazaaghal basaru wa maataghaa: (Najm: 53: 17). All the time when the sun is hidden from the eyes of the world during the night, he was the one to be looking at God. All hopes were upon him and all guidance’s and intercessions were through him. His eyes got the eye-black and got brightened to see what even Gabriel (Jibra‘iil) dared not see. This sight was provided to him as a special gift wit the expansion of his breast as stated in the Quran: Have we not expanded your breast: Alam nashrah laka sadraka: (Inshiraah: 91: 1). Any single, unlettered orphan who gets this eyeblack becomes unique personality like an extra ordinary-large-sized-pearl as Muhammad became. His eyesight was so powerful as to see even the tiniest particles invisible to others to such an extent that he became the object of search of God, who searched for him all through till then. The searcher became the object of the search. And also His sight was so bright that he could clearly see all activities of all creatures to such an extent that God called him as the witness (Shaahid), saying: “we have truly sent you as a witness, as a bringer of glad tidings and as a warner: Inna arsalnaaka shaahidan wa mubashhiran wa naziiran: (Fatj: 48: 8, and many other places). One who has seen and been a true eyewitness.

sections.heading: Great Worth of Witnesses
paras: Tongue and sharp sight are the tools of the witness. As the prophet remained awake in the night, he had a heart which could not go away from him, and nothing remained hidden from him. How much ever efforts a plaintiff may put to establish his case, the judge gives his ears only to the evidence given by the witness. This is the merit of the judges in the affairs of the people and governments; and both their eyes are bright enough to see the truth. The words of the witnesses are worthy because they speak of what the eyes have seen, and their seeing is without any self-interest and prejudice. What the eyes of the plaintiff see is prejudiced and subjective to meet his case and as such, purpose becomes a curtain and hides the truth from the eyes of the heart. That is why God desires that you should not have any personal objective and give up your purpose and be a true witness of matters. God says: give up your personal objects so that what you speak to us may become acceptable. Personal motives become curtains for the eyes which overlap as curtains upon curtains against truth. One with personal motives sees things as wavering, running away and unstable. His love for things makes him blind and deaf. He does not see any wrong in the beloved nor he hears against him.

sections.heading: Soul Is Invisible to Others
paras: When the sun of God’s light speed its brightness upon his heart, there was no worth for him for the light of star like light of others. With this, he saw all hidden secrets, in all clarity without any curtains in-between and looked at the speed of the roaming about of the souls of all the faithful’s and infidels. Nothing is as hidden in the earth and heavens as the human soul of man. With the help of God a person may open his both eyes, and see even hidden wetness and dryness (life an lifelessness) of all matters, which are all overlapped with many curtains (such as biological, physical, chemical secrets etc), but he cannot see the soul, as God has put a seal upon it, saying: it is one among my commands: Say: The spirit (comes) by the command of my Lord: (Banii Isra‘iil: 17: 85). But the Prophet happened to see it with his honoured eyes because of which nothing remained hidden from him. Because of this, he is a perfect witness in every dispute. His words shatter the headaches caused by any kind of inebriated subjective pleadings. God’s name is just and equitable and His witness is perfect and absolute; and as such, His real friend is a perfect eyewitness. Man’s heart is a revealer of truth in both the worlds and so He concentrates His eyes upon it. God’s love and its remaining hidden from others is the great asset of the lover. The love that the prophet had for God became the cause of the creation of everything. That is why at the time of His meeting with the Prophet on the night of Ascent. (Sha-e-Mi‘raaj), God said to the Prophet: But for you. I would not have created the heavens: Laow laaka lamaakhalqtul aflaak. (hadith(s)).

sections.heading: Knower of Predestination Commands It
paras: Predestination caused by God is a commander on all good and bad. This statement also needs a witness to prove. Knowers of God (Prophets and saints) are the witnesses of predestination, being made as such witnesses, participate in the commands of God and become His commanders also. Victims of fate go under the command of this commander. The Prophet, as a man, was also under the command of predestination, but as a knower and holder of the keys of predestination, he was chosen by God. That was because of the great quality of the special sharpness of his eyes to see the ins and outs of everything.

Knowers of God like the prophets and saints plead to their well understood God saying: “O Observer of all our good and bad acts! You are an adviser to us in all our good and bad acts, which You do through the hints given to our hearts. But we are not capable of finding those hints. You are the One who sees us day and night, but we do not see You. Our dependence upon cause and effect has shut our eyes.” Everyone of them says: “My eyes have become special and sharper than others, because of which I see the sun during the night. The pleasure of the knowledge about You has reached its highest point, because of Your own extra-ordinary grace upon me. Perfectness of the grace is in its becoming fullest in all respects. This is so in this world but take it to that fullest level even on the day of resurrection and protect us then from the disgracing tortures of that day. Do not give the day of separation to Your friend of the night. Do not keep the one away from You who has been closely to You. separation from You is a death full of pain and torture and in particular the separation that comes after closeness. Do not make the one who has seen You as one who has not seen You. sprinkle water on the greenery that has grown in his heart, freshen it and keep it intact.

sections.heading: Many Attractions and Pulls of Things
paras: I have not shown any carelessness on my path to You, and You may also do not do so and cause difficulties and keep me away. Do not keep Your face turned against one who has been shown once. Looking at any other face other than Yours is like putting a yoke around the neck, because ‘everything other than God is false.’ They are all false but show their faces to me as of great worth to attract me towards them thinking that I am also false, as falsities drag falsities towards themselves. Every particle existing in this earth and heavens drags every other particle of its species like Kahruba, (the plant which drags the particles of grass towards itself upon getting warmed up). Stomach drags the bread till its destined place, and heat of the liver drags water up till itself. Eyes drag the beloved from the streets, and the brains search for the fragrances of the gardens. Senses of the eyes drag the colours, and brains and noses go in search of five fragrances, because eyes get attracted to colours and the brain and nose go toward five fragrances. O God, the knower of all these attractions, drag us with the attractiveness of your benevolence towards peace. You are the purchaser; you are dominant upon all pulls and attractions; and it would be very good if you buy for yourself those who have been separated from You.

sections.heading: Impacts of Good and Bad Qualities
paras: The thief who had seen the sultan in the darkness of the night which was shining like the full moon on the night of fortune turned his face toward the king like the thirsty toward the cloud. He was bold enough to talk to the sultan as he had recognised his great qualities through his extraordinary quality. He said: “We are all like the soul that is imprisoned in mud, and you are like the sun of life on the day of judgement, which graces everybody with its light. Now, the time has come O king, the hider of wrongs, to be graceful and kind to us by shaking your beard. All of us have shown clearly their specialities, which have put them into misfortune. Those specialities have tied down our necks resulting in our degradation and lowliness. These qualities are like the twisted rope of palm-leaf fibre round the neck: Fi jiidihaa hablum min masad: (Lahab: 111: 5). These abilities are of no help on the day of death.”

The excepted fellow is only the one whose eyes had the quality of recognising the king in the darkness of the night. The qualities of all others were like the misguiding devils on the way. The only worthy eyes were those who were well aware of the king. On the occasion of meeting with him, the king’s eyes as his eyes were those which recognised the greatness of the king.

sections.heading: Good Results of Bad Qualities
paras: So also, the one who could find out what the dog means while barking must be considered as a dog as worthy as the one which was with the companions of the cave (Ashab-e-kahaf), because it was aware of the great king. His quality was great as he became aware of the lion-like sultan in the dog’s barking sound. A dog which is awake during the night-time like the king’s bodyguard cannot remain ignorant of the king’s wakefulness of mind even in sleep. Therefore, it is required that one should not feel it disgraceful to be with the unpopular fellows. One should keep one’s own senses dominant over their secrets and be careful. So also, one who becomes disgraced should not go after that disgrace only, remain at that level itself and remain immature, but go to change the situation. There are many pieces of gold which are deliberately painted black to protect them from loot and loss. those pieces say: “Everyone cannot see the secrets behind the apparently bad and defective. Open both of your eyes, look at our hidden worth and come close to us.”
